1	# Architecture
2	
3	Three layers with hard boundaries:
4	
5	```
6	React UI (components/)          declarative HUD/panels; reads snapshots, sends commands
7	    │  useSyncExternalStore + engine commands
8	GameEngine (lib/game/engine/)   headless simulation: all game state, stepped per frame
9	    │  reads/writes
10	Voxel world (lib/world/)        data + generation + meshing + queries
11	    ▲  read every frame by
12	GameRenderer (lib/game/render/) Three.js: maps simulation state → GPU objects
13	AudioDirector (lib/game/audio/)  WebAudio: maps engine events + state → procedural sound
14	```
15	
16	The engine has **no React, no DOM, no rendering** — it runs (and is tested) headlessly in `bun test`. The renderer, the audio director, and the input controller are the only modules touching Three.js scene objects, the `AudioContext`, and DOM listeners respectively.
17	
18	## React shell (`lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/`)
19	
20	- `useMinecraftGame` creates the `GameEngine` in the canvas mount's callback ref, then an effect builds the `GameRenderer`, the `AudioDirector`, and `inputController` and drives the `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `engine.step(dt, input)` (in bounded catch-up substeps of ≤50 ms, so slow frames — e.g. software GL — don't run the simulation in slow motion) → drain engine events (death/respawn handling, `attackSwung` → `renderer.triggerSwing()`, + `renderer.handleEvent` for particle bursts, + `audio.handleEvent`) → `minimap.sync(state)` → `renderer.sync(state)` → `audio.sync(state, dt)` → `renderer.render()`. The minimap must sync **before** the renderer because it reads `state.worldMeshDirty`, which `renderer.sync` clears.
21	- `components/GameShell.tsx` is the menu shell **above** `useMinecraftGame`: a profile-select → world-select → play state machine (profiles own worlds; see [save-format.md](save-format.md)) that runs the one-time legacy migration on mount and renders `MinecraftGame` keyed by `world.id` (+ a reload nonce). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset changes the key, so React unmounts the game subtree — running the effect cleanup that disposes renderer/audio/input and clears the rAF + autosave — and a fresh mount boots the next world, **no page reload**. The tab's active world is remembered in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes it while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. `useMinecraftGame` therefore takes the `world` + `profile` to play and persists to that world's own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key.
22	- UI state arrives as immutable `GameSnapshot`s via `useSyncExternalStore`; the engine replaces the snapshot object only when a visible value changes, so React re-renders are minimal and identity-driven.
23	- UI intents (`craft`, `swapSlots`, `selectSlot`, …) are dispatched as engine `Command`s. The only React state in the shell is pure UI concern: pointer lock, transient save messages, renderer failure.
24	- WebGL init failure is surfaced as `rendererError` and rendered as a fallback panel instead of crashing.
25	- On mount the shell installs a `window.__monecraft` debug handle (`{ engine, renderer, input, audio }`) and deletes it on unmount. The Playwright suite in `e2e/` drives the game through this handle — asserting on engine state and `renderer.renderedTriangles()` rather than pixels (see [testing.md](testing.md)); it's also handy from the browser console.
26	- UI pixel art is procedural: `lib/ui/` generates 16×16 item/HUD sprites as pure pixel buffers (`spritePixels.ts`, `hudPixels.ts` — DOM-free, unit-tested) wrapped by a cached canvas→data-URL layer (`sprites.ts`, falls back to a transparent pixel under happy-dom). `chromeTiles.ts` (`installUiTiles`, idempotent, `document`-guarded) installs the GUI textures as CSS vars: the menu-backdrop noise (`--mc-tile-dirt/stone`) and the chrome grain layered over the flat panel/slot/button colors (`--mc-tile-panel/well/button`, which default to `none` so SSR/pre-install falls back to the solid color). No image assets, no licensing exposure. `lib/ui/` must not import Three.js or the engine.
27	- Item hovers use `useItemTooltip` (`components/game/ItemTooltip.tsx`): a cursor-following, `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events:none` tooltip portaled to `document.body` (so it never clips inside the scrollable inventory or blocks the pointer-lock click), replacing native `title=` on the hotbar, inventory, and recipe entries. Elements keep their `aria-label` for the accessible name.
28	- The one binary asset is the UI pixel font (Monocraft, a Minecraft-style face under SIL OFL 1.1), self-hosted via `next/font/local` from the committed woff2 in `app/fonts/` and exposed as `--mc-font`; the monospace stack stays as the fallback and on the F3 debug readout, and Monocraft's coding ligatures are disabled in `base.css`. This is the single sanctioned exception to "zero binary assets".
29	- Note for the React Compiler lint rules: consume the hook with destructuring (`const { … } = useMinecraftGame()`); property access on the result object can false-positive `react-hooks/refs`.
30	
31	## Game engine (`lib/game/engine/`)
32	
33	- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command)`, advances `step(dt, input)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`) and the world size is overridable for fast headless tests.
34	- `state.ts` — `GameState` (player with `yaw`/`pitch`, inventory, mobs, vehicles,
35	  and thrown spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, mining
36	  progress, timers) plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
37	- `commands.ts` — the `Command` union: every UI/input mutation enters the simulation through exactly this door.
38	- `blockChanges.ts` — the delta tracker behind the save format: tracked block writes against the worldgen baseline; reverted edits drop out of the save.
39	- `systems/` — one module per mechanic, each a function over `GameState`:
40	
41	### Per-frame step order (in `GameEngine.step`)
42	
43	0. Pause gate: while `state.paused`, `step` refreshes the snapshot and returns — mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all freeze (autosave still serializes fine)
44	1. Stuck detection / auto-unstuck (`STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`)
45	2. Death check + respawn countdown (while dead, only mobs tick)
46	3. Sleep gate: while `state.sleepTimer > 0`, `step` decrements the fade and returns (full freeze, like pause); at zero it skips the clock to the next morning
47	4. Player or mounted-vehicle movement (`systems/playerMotion.ts` / `systems/vehicles.ts` — walking derives direction from `yaw`; mounted rafts/ships carry the player and check water support)
48	5. Hunger drain, health regen, continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and oxygen/drowning damage (`systems/playerStats.ts` — `tickWaterExposure`, `tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`, all on the armor-bypassing path)
49	6. Mining progress and block breaking (`systems/mining.ts`; placement also lives here)
50	7. Day-night clock (`systems/dayNight.ts` — `daylightAt()` is the single daylight formula); immediately after, `systems/weather.ts` sets the **transient** `state.weather` (rain/snow/clear) as a pure function of `dayClock` + seed — cosmetic only: never serialized, never touches spawn/daylight balance
51	8. Random block ticks (`systems/randomTicks.ts` — each interval samples columns near the player and runs per-block handlers; drives crop growth and is the extension point for future saplings / grass spread)
52	9. Night hostile spawning (`systems/spawnDirector.ts`, interval/cap in config)
53	10. Dungeon spawners (`systems/spawnDirector.ts` `tickSpawnerDirector` — each interval, every intact dungeon spawner with the player in range drips one hostile onto the room floor, bounded by a local cluster cap and the shared `HOSTILE_CAP`; time-independent)
54	11. Mob AI: wander/aggro/flee, attacks with line-of-sight, daylight burn (`systems/mobAI.ts`). Ranged mobs (skeletons, boss) kite and loose arrows instead of meleeing; the boss also bears down, melees up close, fires a spread, and summons minions
55	12. Projectiles (`systems/projectileAI.ts` `tickProjectiles` — arrows integrate under gravity in capped substeps; block hits reuse the swept world DDA and the entity test is substepped so fast arrows can't tunnel; spent arrows despawn). Also ticked in the dead branch so in-flight arrows clear
56	13. Animal breeding (`systems/breeding.ts` — feed-to-love timers, baby maturity, pairing in-love adults within range; the passive cap bounds the population)
57	
58	**Vehicles.** Rafts and ships are persistent logical entities (`VehicleState`) rather than blocks. `systems/vehicles.ts` owns water-surface placement, right-click boarding for rafts, step-on boarding for ships, mounted steering, dismount selection, water-support checks, and v16 save restore filtering. The rider link is session-only; placed vehicles persist through `SaveData.vehicles`.
59	
60	**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter: player arrows (the bow) hit mobs with knockback, mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated), and neither hits the firer. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.
61	
62	**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new kind requires entries in all seven exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `FACTION_BY_KIND`, `MOB_DROPS`, `MOB_XP`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).
63	
64	**Villages & raids.** Villages generate as house clusters on flat land (`placeVillages`, last in `generateWorld` on its own `villageRand` so other passes stay byte-identical); the engine re-derives their centers on load (`collectVillageSites`) and seeds **resident villagers** there — but only when the world has no villagers yet, so a reload restores them instead of doubling. Residents persist via the v14 `mobs` field (`isPersistentMob` covers `faction === "villager"`); each carries a `profession` (v15) that selects its trade subset (`TRADE_PROFESSION`) and tints its smock. A **raid** is a transient `state.raid` wave machine (`systems/raid.ts`, like the boss — never serialized): a craftable **Ominous Horn** starts it near a village (a `placeBlock`-precedence step mirroring `trySummonBoss`), waves of the `raider` kind spawn until all are cleared (win → emerald + XP) or the residents die (loss). The raider needed no `mobAI` change — its `"raider"` faction was already wired into the enmity/threat/credit tables, so it hunts villagers, your pets defend, and it counts against `HOSTILE_CAP` (Peaceful cancels the raid).
65	
66	**Game modes.** The four modes (`survival`/`creative`/`adventure`/`spectator`, `lib/game/gameModes.ts`) are a single `state.gameMode` axis. Systems gate on **intent predicates** rather than the raw id, so all four share one set of seams: `takesDamage` switches off the three damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts` (covering fall/void/lava/water/drown/mob/poison at once) plus hunger/regen/oxygen in `playerStats.ts`; `canEditBlocks`/`freeBuild` gate breaking and placing in `mining.ts`; `canInteract` gates the interaction commands in `dispatch`; `canFly`/`isNoclip` drive flight and the collision skip in `playerMotion.ts` (and the auto-unstuck skip in `step`); `mobsThreaten` folds into `activeHostile` in `mobAI.ts`; `usesInventory`/`takesDamage` hide HUD elements. `gameMode` rides the per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's **switchable in-game** — `setGameMode` (`GameEngine.switchGameMode`) resets transient hazard timers, bars, flight, and noclip-entombment on the change. The transient `isFlying` is never serialized.
67	
68	**Difficulty.** Orthogonal to the mode, `state.difficulty` (`peaceful`/`easy`/`normal`/`hard`, `lib/game/difficulties.ts`) decides _how hard_ survival is — it follows the same shape as game modes: an enum, an `isDifficulty` guard, `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` for the UI, and **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that systems read instead of the raw id. The seams: `spawnDirector.ts` gates the initial population + night director + dungeon spawners on `hostilesSpawn` and scales the cadence/cap; `mobAI.ts` multiplies every mob hit at the strike (templates untouched); `playerStats.ts` scales regen and runs the new **starvation** tick (hunger 0 chips to a per-level HP floor, lethal only on Hard, routed through the same floored/lethal damage paths as Poison/environment). Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` → a v9 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`) and is switchable in-game — `setDifficulty` (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`) just updates the value the directors read next tick, except dropping to Peaceful, which despawns the hostiles already present (a plain splice — no loot/XP, no false boss victory). The two axes don't cross-couple: spawning keys only on difficulty, threat/damage only on mode.
69	
70	**Hardcore.** A per-world boolean (`state.hardcore`, persisted in save v10 + `WorldMeta`, **immutable** unlike mode/difficulty). The constructor resolves it first so it overrides the other axes — forced to Survival + Hard — and `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` early-return under it (the player-facing switchers are disabled; the engine's own death transition sets the mode directly, bypassing the lock). Death is permanent: the two lethal seams (`applyDamage`, `applyEnvironmentalDamage`) divert to `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()`, which sets the persisted `gameOver` flag and flips the player to **Spectator** (a free-cam over the dead world, invulnerable so mobs can't re-trigger it) instead of arming the respawn countdown — so a reloaded `gameOver` world boots straight into spectating (the constructor resolves `gameMode` to spectator; the existing `!isNoclip` stuck-check leaves it un-teleported). The shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event so a tab-close still persists the dead world; the Game Over screen (`components/game/GameOverScreen.tsx`) owns navigation (spectate / quit / delete), and `pause` is blocked while `gameOver`. The hearts render in a withered palette (`lib/ui/hudPixels.ts`).
71	
72	**Advancements & statistics.** Progression meta (`systems/advancements.ts`) hangs off the **single `GameEngine.emit` chokepoint** every system already emits through: `emit` pushes the event for the shell, then runs `observeProgress` — `recordEvent` folds it into the `state.stats` counters (a `Map<string, number>`), and `evaluateAdvancements` unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed, adding it to `state.advancements` (a `Set`) and emitting `advancementUnlocked` (the one event type `emit` skips, to avoid recursing). The advancement set is a **declarative `{ stat, threshold }` registry**, so unlock is uniform and adding one is a single row with no logic. Tick-driven display stats (distance, play time) bump directly in `step` via `recordTick`, off the unlock path. Both `stats` and `advancements` persist in save v13 and, like `xp` and unlike `effects`, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). The L-key overlay (`AdvancementsPanel`) reads detail through `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render — only the open flag and the unlocked **count** ride the snapshot, so play never churns it with stat values the HUD doesn't show.
73	
74	Combat (`systems/combat.ts`) runs on the `attack` command rather than per frame: a held bow branches to `tryFireBow` (instant click-to-fire, no draw-charge), a spear melees at its longer `weaponReach`, and otherwise `tryAttackMob` swings. The `placeBlock` command runs a fixed right-click precedence (`systems/interact.ts` + engine): throw the selected spear (`tryThrowSelectedSpear`) → feed/tame/sit/trade aimed mobs → board an aimed vehicle → interact with the aimed block (`tryInteractBlock`, e.g. bed/furnace/chest/door) → summon the boss / start a raid → fish → place a held vehicle on water → use the held item (`tryUseHeldItem`, e.g. hoe tills soil, seeds plant a crop) → `placeSelectedBlock` — so each interaction consumes the click instead of getting a block placed against it. New mechanics get a new system module and a slot in this sequence — don't grow the engine class with inline logic.
75	
76	**Block-entities (chest contents).** Blocks are bare `BlockId`s, but a chest needs attached storage, so `state.containers: Map<voxelIndex, InventorySlot[]>` holds each placed chest's slots (keyed by `world.index`, the same space as the block diff). Placing a chest creates an empty entry; opening one (`interactChest`) sets `state.openContainerIndex` and `inventoryOpen` so the panel renders its grid; the `moveStack` command shuttles slots across the inventory/chest boundary (chest indices offset by `CONTAINER_SLOT_BASE`); breaking a chest spills its contents into the inventory via `inventory.tryInsertSlots` (refused if they don't fit). `serialize()` persists non-empty containers as `blockEntities`; see [save-format.md](save-format.md).
77	
78	**Dungeon loot chests.** Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents can't ride the block-diff baseline. The engine instead keeps two session-only sets — `dungeonChestIndices` / `dungeonSpawnerIndices` — rebuilt each boot from the seed via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`, which replays the dungeon placement math without writing blocks), plus a **persisted** `lootedDungeonChests` set. On a dungeon chest's first open or break, `systems/dungeon.ts` `fillDungeonChestIfUnlooted` rolls loot seeded from `world.seed ^ voxelIndex` (`lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`) and marks the index looted. Gating on the looted set — not on whether the chest is currently non-empty — is what stops an emptied-then-reloaded chest from re-rolling (an empty container is dropped from `blockEntities`).
79	
80	## Renderer (`lib/game/render/`)
81	
82	- `GameRenderer.ts` — scene/camera/WebGL/lighting; `sync(state)` maps simulation state to visuals each frame; `dispose()` frees every GPU resource. WebGL creation returns `{ ok: false, error }` instead of throwing.
83	- **Camera modes**: `state.cameraMode` (session-only, V key) selects first-person or a third-person rear/front boom. Pose math is pure (`cameraView.ts`); the boom is clamped each frame by a `voxelRaycast` from the eye so walls never occlude the player. Gameplay stays eye-relative in every mode — mining/combat raycasts and audio panning read player yaw/pitch, never the camera.
84	- **World mesh**: one mesh covers the visible region (not chunked), rebuilt when the player crosses a `RENDER_GRID` (20-block) boundary or when the engine sets `state.worldMeshDirty` (block edits, respawn, unstuck). Old geometry is disposed on rebuild.
85	- **Per-voxel lighting**: the world/glass materials are patched via `onBeforeCompile` (`patchVoxelLighting`) to consume the baked `aLight` attribute — they gate the scene-lit colour by sky exposure (caves go dark) and add block light back as an albedo-tinted glow (torches/lava light the dark). **Day/night needs no uniform and no re-mesh**: the scene sun + hemisphere already scale with `daylight` in `syncDayNight`, so a sky-exposed surface dims at night through the scene lights while caves stay dark regardless. The patch anchors on stable `ShaderChunk` includes; the e2e "renders without errors" smoke test guards it against a Three.js bump.
86	- `mobVisuals.ts` — mob id → model map; creates/removes models as mobs spawn/die and animates bob + leg gait from mob state (the simulation knows nothing about legs).
87	- `vehicleVisuals.ts` — vehicle id → procedural raft/ship meshes; creates/removes models as placed vehicles appear/disappear and mirrors their pose.
88	- `projectileVisuals.ts` — projectile id → mesh map for in-flight arrows; one extruded-sprite geometry + material is shared across every arrow (only transforms differ), each oriented so its long axis points along its velocity. Freed once in `dispose()`.
89	- `heldItem.ts` / `crackOverlay.ts` — first-person item model and the 8-stage mining crack box (stage = progress / hardness). Held blocks stay cubes; everything else is the item's 16×16 inventory sprite extruded into a pixel-thick voxel mesh (`extrudedSprite.ts`, vertex colors, silhouette-only side faces) — the render layer imports `lib/ui/spritePixels` for this, which is legal because spritePixels is pure pixel-buffer code with no DOM. The holder group is posed every frame by `heldItemPose.ts` (pure math): a one-shot swing on the `attackSwung` event (the shell calls `renderer.triggerSwing()` from the event drain), a looping swing while mining, a walk bob scaled by horizontal speed, an equip dip on slot switch, and a faint idle sway.
90	- `spearVisuals.ts` mirrors transient thrown spear state into procedural shaft/tip
91	  meshes keyed by projectile id.
92	- `playerModel.ts` / `playerPose.ts` / `playerVisuals.ts` — the player's own humanoid body, visible only in third person: box meshes with pivot groups at the joints, walk gait + attack/mining chop from pure pose math (mirroring `heldItemPose.ts`), the look pitch applied to the head only, and the held hotbar item in the right hand via the shared `itemModel.ts` builder (also used by `heldItem.ts`).
93	- **Atmosphere** (all procedural, zero assets, freed in `dispose()`): `particleSystem.ts` + the pure, unit-tested `particlePool.ts` draw event-driven bursts (block shards from `BLOCK_COLORS`, mob-death puffs, eat crumbs, jump/land/footstep dust) as one `THREE.Points` with a soft-sprite shader, spawned via `GameRenderer.handleEvent(event, state)` (wired into the event drain beside `audio.handleEvent`). `skyView.ts` + the pure `starField.ts` layer camera-following stars, a moon, a sun disc, and drifting canvas-noise clouds over the day-night sky lerp, ramped by `daylight`. `precipitation.ts` is the camera-following rain/snow field driven by `state.weather`, and `syncDayNight` adds the matching overcast sky tint + dimmed light + nearer fog.
94	- **Skins**: the body is colored by a `PlayerPalette` from `lib/game/playerSkins.ts` (six presets); `GameRenderer.setPlayerSkin(palette)` recolors the named materials in place. The choice persists on the active **profile** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`; `updateSkin` calls `setProfileSkin`) — identity, not world state — and both the create-profile and pause-menu pickers' bust portraits (`lib/ui/skinPortrait.ts`) derive from the same palettes. (The legacy global `minecraft_skin_v1` key, still defined in `lib/game/skinSettings.ts`, is read only once by the save migration to seed the default profile's skin.)
95	- `minimap.ts` / `minimapColors.ts` — the top-right minimap: pure column sampling (top non-air block, height-shaded `BLOCK_COLORS`) feeding a 2D canvas that rebuilds its 128×128 base only when the player crosses a 16-block grid boundary or `worldMeshDirty` is set (read-only — the renderer owns clearing it), then blits with a yaw-rotated player arrow at ~10 Hz.
96	
97	## Audio (`lib/game/audio/`)
98	
99	All sound is procedural — no audio files, mirroring the sprite system. SFX are synthesized by [ZZFX](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/ZzFX) parameter arrays; music is a generative ambient pad over raw WebAudio nodes.
100	
101	- `audioDirector.ts` — the shell-side observer, exactly parallel to the renderer: `handleEvent(GameEvent)` plays one-shots (block break/place by material, hurt/eat/jump/land, mob attacks, death/respawn stingers) and `sync(state, dt)` drives everything continuous (footsteps, mining hit ticks, mob ambience, music mood, and the weather rain bed). Music follows `state.daylight` immediately and the biome with 5 s hysteresis, and ducks while paused. The rain bed (`rainLoop.ts`) is a looping filtered-noise source on the graph, off the SFX voice budget, whose gain tracks `state.weather` rain intensity (silent for snow / while paused). The engine never imports this module.
102	- `synth.ts` — `SynthBackend`, **the only seam that touches WebAudio for SFX**: renders each `SoundDef` to an `AudioBuffer` once via `ZZFX.buildSamples` and plays it through gain/pan nodes with playback-rate jitter, a 10-voice cap, and per-sound retrigger throttling (which also de-dupes catch-up substep event bursts). Tests inject a recording fake instead.
103	- `soundParams.ts` / `materials.ts` — pure data: ZZFX parameter tables per `MaterialGroup`/`MobKind` (tune by ear in the [ZZFX designer](https://killedbyapixel.github.io/ZzFX/)) and the exhaustive `BlockId → MaterialGroup` mapping.
104	- `footsteps.ts` / `mobAmbience.ts` / `musicBrain.ts` — pure schedulers/composer (distance-accumulator strides, per-mob randomized call timers with distance gain + look-relative stereo pan, pentatonic random-walk note generation). `musicPlayer.ts` renders notes as detuned pad voices through a lowpass and a procedural convolution reverb.
105	- **Lazy unlock invariant**: no `AudioContext` exists until the first user gesture calls `unlock()` — including the `zzfx` import itself, which instantiates one at module scope and is therefore only ever imported dynamically inside `unlock()`. This satisfies the browser autoplay policy, keeps SSR/`bun test` import-safe, and keeps the console clean for the E2E fixture.
106	- Volume settings (`settings.ts`) persist under their own localStorage key (`minecraft_audio_v1`) — never part of the world save.
107	
108	## Input (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`)
109	
110	Owns every DOM listener. Continuous input (movement keys, mouse button, pointer lock, CapsLock) is exposed as a `FrameInput` the engine reads each step; discrete actions (hotbar, inventory toggle, place, eat, attack, unstuck, pause, F3 debug, V camera view) become commands; mouse-look calls `engine.applyLook`. The first click only acquires pointer lock; `KeyI` exits it.
111	
112	**Pause ↔ pointer lock**: the browser consumes Escape to exit pointer lock, so Esc never reaches keydown while locked — losing the lock during plain gameplay is the pause trigger (`pointerlockchange` dispatches `pause`). The inventory (`KeyI`) and death paths set their state flags _before_ the async `pointerlockchange` fires, and the engine's `pause` command additionally ignores those states, so they don't open the menu. While unlocked, Escape toggles pause directly (and closes the inventory). "Back to Game" resumes and re-requests the lock; Chrome's ~1.25 s cooldown after Esc can reject that request — the rejection is swallowed and the player just clicks the canvas.
113	
114	## Inventory and items (`lib/game/`)
115	
116	- `inventory.ts` — pure slot algebra (`adjustSlotCount`, `craft`, durability, armor); every function returns a new array or `null` for "no change". Crafting refuses when the result doesn't fit rather than destroying overflow. Equipped armor is **dedicated storage**: `state.equippedArmor` (`Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot | null>`) holds the worn pieces themselves — `toggleEquipArmor`/`unequipArmor` move a piece between the inventory and the record, and `equippedDefense`/`armorReduction`/`consumeEquippedArmorDurability` (and Mending's `mendXp`) read/wear/repair those instances directly rather than re-finding them in the inventory by id.
117	- `items.ts` — `ITEM_DEFS`, `BLOCK_TO_SLOT`, `BREAK_HARDNESS`, armor slots, slot factories. `recipes.ts` — `RECIPES` (each with an optional `station`, e.g. `"furnace"` for smelting).
118	- Drop tables: `mobLoot.ts` (`rollMobDrops` — per-`MobKind` loot) and `items.ts` (`rollBlockDrops` — block drops, e.g. grass→occasional seed, mature wheat→wheat + 1–2 seeds). Both take an injectable `rng`, so tests get deterministic counts.
119	- `config.ts` — every gameplay tunable, named: physics, hunger rules, daylight thresholds, mob director, mining reach, autosave interval, the legacy `SAVE_KEY`, and `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (the worldgen baseline each world records).
120	- `save.ts` — versioned (de)serialization with an injectable `Storage` and a per-world save key (`worldSaveKey`, `lib/game/worlds.ts`); `profiles.ts` / `worlds.ts` hold the profile and world manifests, `legacyMigration.ts` folds an old single save into them; `spawn.ts` — deterministic spawn search + random land points.
121	
122	## World layer (`lib/world/`)
123	
124	One module per concern, behind an `index.ts` barrel — consumers always import from `@/lib/world`:
125	
126	- `blocks.ts` — `BlockId`, `BiomeId`, `WORLD_SIZE_*`, and both block palettes (`BLOCK_COLORS` paints the atlas; `HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` tints the held-item model — intentionally different values). Door facing/open/half states are ordinary IDs so they persist in the existing block diff.
127	- `doors.ts` — door-state encoding helpers and the thin panel bounds shared by meshing and collision.
128	- `voxelWorld.ts` — `VoxelWorld` stores voxels in a flat `Uint8Array` (index = `x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) plus a parallel `light` array and cheap queries (`get`/`set`/`isSolid`/`highestSolidY`/`getBiome`/`getSky`/`getBlockLight`).
129	- `lighting.ts` — per-voxel light (sky + block, packed 0–15 each into `world.light`). `computeFullLight` bakes the whole field from the blocks at load (top-down sunlight column pass + BFS bleed; block-light BFS from emitters); `applyEdit` patches it locally on each block edit with a Minecraft-style remove/refill flood. **Derived cache, never serialized** — a pure function of `world.blocks`. `opacity`/`emission` classify each block (air/glass transmit, water/leaves attenuate, torches/lava emit).
130	- `generation.ts` — `generateWorld(world)`: deterministic terrain, caves, lava, water, ores, trees, houses, and underground dungeons (`placeDungeons`, last in the pipeline). `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` (so it can't shift ore RNG) and before `placeDungeons` (so rooms overwrite lava). `collectDungeonSites(world)` re-derives dungeon chest/spawner indices from the seed for the engine. Constants live in the frozen `GEN` object. **Byte-identical output per seed is a save-format contract**, pinned by `generation.test.ts` hash tests — fix code, never hashes.
131	- `meshing.ts` — `buildGeometryRegion(world, …)` with face culling, baked ambient occlusion, atlas UVs, and a per-vertex `aLight` (sky-exposure, block-light) sampled from the faced voxel; `buildGeometryLayersRegion` splits opaque terrain from clear glass for the renderer.
132	- `atlas.ts` — runtime canvas block atlas (`createBlockAtlasTexture`); tiles are generated from `BLOCK_COLORS`, no image assets. The only world module that touches the DOM.
133	- `queries.ts` — `voxelRaycast` (DDA), `collidesAt`, `hasSupportUnderPlayer`.
134	
135	## Engine invariants & gotchas
136	
137	Hard-won invariants — easy to silently break:
138	
139	- **Transparent blocks are explicit render layers**: `buildGeometryLayersRegion` sends glass to a blended, non-depth-writing material while opaque terrain keeps normal depth writes. Glass-to-glass and water-to-water internal faces are culled; opaque faces touching glass remain visible through it. Water still uses the opaque layer and all world materials are `THREE.DoubleSide` so water is visible from inside. New transparent blocks must extend both the layer routing and face-visibility rules. **Lava is the exception that proves the rule**: it is a normal _solid_ block, so the default opaque face-culling already shows only its surface — it needs no special routing. (It does need a lighting class — see below.)
140	
141	- **Lighting is a derived cache, never serialized**: `world.light` is a pure function of `world.blocks`, baked once at load (`computeFullLight`) and patched per edit (`applyEdit`), both in `lib/world/lighting.ts`. The bake/patch is wired in the **engine** (the constructor and `blockChanges.set`, the single chokepoint all gameplay edits flow through) — never the renderer — so the minimap-before-renderer `worldMeshDirty` ordering stays intact. Every new block needs a lighting class in `opacity`/`emission` (the default is opaque, no emission); sky light falls straight down a clear column for free at any level, so the bake's column pass and the incremental flood must agree (see `propagated`). `applyEdit`'s correctness is pinned by whole-array equivalence tests against a from-scratch bake.
142	
143	- **Lava and the head/body damage split**: lava is solid, so contact damage (`tickLavaExposure`) samples the block underfoot/at body height rather than immersion. Drowning (`tickOxygen`) keys on the _head_ (eye cell) and is deliberately separate from the body-keyed 60 s water-exposure timer — they coexist (one models holding your breath, the other prolonged immersion). All three transient timers/state reset on reload/respawn and are never serialized.
144	- **Doors are multi-cell state machines encoded as blocks**: four facings × open/closed × upper/lower produce 16 internal `BlockId`s. Placement and breaking update both cells atomically; interaction validates the matching pair before toggling. `doorBounds` drives both thin mesh geometry and AABB collision. `highestSolidY` ignores doors so mob surface-following cannot climb over them; mob movement still checks their panel collision and never calls the player-only interaction handler.
145	- **Being in water is not "stuck"**: the unstuck teleport fires only on solid-block overlap or falling below the world (y < 2). Don't make water count as a collision in `collidesAt` — players may stay submerged, though `tickWaterExposure` starts armor-bypassing damage after 60 continuous seconds. Its transient timers reset on exit and are never serialized.
146	- **Water is replaceable during placement**: the normal raycast still ignores water and targets the solid surface behind it; `placeSelectedBlock` accepts the resulting destination when it contains air or water. Failed self-overlap placement must restore the original cell (including water), not blindly write air.
147	- **Daylight thresholds** (daylight ranges 0.04–1.0, named in `config.ts`): hostiles night-spawn below 0.28; spiders are hostile only below 0.42 (passive in twilight); zombies/skeletons burn above 0.72. The game boots at dawn (~0.05), so initial hostiles aggro immediately — headless tests use a `calmDaytime` helper.
148	- **DDA boundary ambiguity**: a raycast origin exactly on a cell boundary (integer coordinate) may target a diagonal neighbor — relevant for tests that aim at specific blocks.
149	- **Pointer lock**: the first left-click only acquires pointer lock (no mining); `KeyI` explicitly exits lock; right-click places without requiring lock.
150	- **Client-only**: never touch `window`/`document`/localStorage at module top level — everything runs behind `"use client"` and mounts via the callback ref/effect. The engine itself must stay DOM-free so it keeps running under `bun test`.
151	
```

  "content": "# Online Multiplayer for Monecraft\n\n## Context\n\nMonecraft is today a single-player, client-only browser game (Next.js 16 / React 19 / TS strict / Three.js / Bun) saving to localStorage. Goal: online co-op multiplayer played in the browser, with accounts + cloud saves + instant guest access, deployed on managed infrastructure, without breaking offline single-player.\n\nExploration confirmed the engine is **already a headless simulation core**: `lib/game/engine/` + `lib/world/` (~13.4k LOC) is pure TS (no DOM/WebAudio/rAF), runs under `bun test`, mutates only via `dispatch(Command)` (28-command union in `lib/game/engine/commands.ts`), publishes ~60 `GameEvent`s the renderer/audio already consume as observers, has injectable RNG/Storage, and saves as seed + block diff. The real work is: (a) the state model is single-player-shaped (one `state.player`, ~25 flat per-player fields in `state.ts`); (b) worldgen noise uses `Math.sin` → not portable across JS engines (why CI pins Bun 1.3.12) — a Bun server and a V8 browser can disagree on terrain for the same seed; (c) there is zero server/network code.\n\n### Decisions (confirmed with user)\n\n| Decision | Choice |\n|---|---|\n| Scale | 2–8 players per world, private co-op via invite link. No chunk streaming / interest management in v1 — full-world rooms. |\n| Hosting | **Vercel**: Next.js app, better-auth, world/save/invite API, Neon Postgres. **Fly.io**: one Bun process hosting N world rooms (one `GameEngine` each, ~74 MB/room), WebSocket, 20 Hz fixed tick. They share only Neon + a ticket-signing secret. |\n| Authority | **Hybrid**: server runs the authoritative engine for the shared world (blocks, mobs, items, chests, time) and validates all Commands; each client owns its own avatar movement (streams pose @20 Hz; server clamps speed/teleports). Protocol shaped so full server-auth + prediction can be added later without wire changes. |\n| Auth | **better-auth**, self-hosted in Next, Postgres-backed, anonymous plugin: guest identity on first online action, in-place upgrade to email/OAuth keeping worlds. ## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Online Multiplayer for Monecraft

## Context

Monecraft is today a single-player, client-only browser game (Next.js 16 / React 19 / TS strict / Three.js / Bun) saving to localStorage. Goal: online co-op multiplayer played in the browser, with accounts + cloud saves + instant guest access, deployed on managed infrastructure, without breaking offline single-player.

Exploration confirmed the engine is **already a headless simulation core**: `lib/game/engine/` + `lib/world/` (~13.4k LOC) is pure TS (no DOM/WebAudio/rAF), runs under `bun test`, mutates only via `dispatch(Command)` (28-command union in `lib/game/engine/commands.ts`), publishes ~60 `GameEvent`s the renderer/audio already consume as observers, has injectable RNG/Storage, and saves as seed + block diff. The real work is: (a) the state model is single-player-shaped (one `state.player`, ~25 flat per-player fields in `state.ts`); (b) worldgen noise uses `Math.sin` → not portable across JS engines (why CI pins Bun 1.3.12) — a Bun server and a V8 browser can disagree on terrain for the same seed; (c) there is zero server/network code.

### Decisions (confirmed with user)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scale | 2–8 players per world, private co-op via invite link. No chunk streaming / interest management in v1 — full-world rooms. |
| Hosting | **Vercel**: Next.js app, better-auth, world/save/invite API, Neon Postgres. **Fly.io**: one Bun process hosting N world rooms (one `GameEngine` each, ~74 MB/room), WebSocket, 20 Hz fixed tick. They share only Neon + a ticket-signing secret. The game server is a plain Docker container (`/health`, env vars) — portable to Railway/Render/a VPS by swapping deploy config; Cloudflare DO ruled out (128 MB memory cap vs ~74 MB rooms, workerd runtime). |
| Authority | **Server-authoritative with one hybrid concession**: the server runs the real `GameEngine` per room — every gameplay Command (place/break/craft/attack/chest/…) is validated and executed server-side; canonical world state (blocks, mobs, items, chests, time) lives only there. The sole client-owned thing is each player's *own avatar movement* (streamed @20 Hz; server clamps speed/teleports and force-corrects). Full server-auth movement + prediction can be added later without wire changes — `cmd` envelopes already carry seq + claimed pose. |
| Auth | **better-auth**, self-hosted in Next, Postgres-backed, anonymous plugin: guest identity on first online action, in-place upgrade to email/OAuth keeping worlds. Game server never sees cookies — short-lived HS256 join tickets minted by the Next API. |
| SP | Stays fully offline-capable with localStorage saves, same engine (SP = 1-player case), no account required, no network code loaded. Optional cloud sync of SP saves when signed in (gzipped blob, LWW on `updatedAt`). Phase 2's acceptance bar — "entire existing e2e suite passes unchanged" — is the enforcement. |
| Seams | **No "extract the core" phase is needed** — the headless sim already exists and the Bun server imports it directly (Bun runs TS natively, no build step). What we build: Phase 1–2 make it deterministic + multi-player-shaped *in place*; Phase 5 adds the transport seam — `GameSession` (`createLocalSession` = today's offline path; `NetworkSession` = WebSocket + replica engine) with the protocol in shared `lib/net/`. |

## Delivery: 6 phases, each its own `mp/*` branch + PR, verify gate green each time

Phases 1–2 are pure refactors (zero product change) — the risk sponge. 3 (Vercel side) and 4 (Fly side) are independent after 2; 5 needs both.

---

### Phase 1 — Deterministic foundations (`mp/1-deterministic-foundations`)

**Goal:** identical engine source produces byte-identical worlds on Bun and Chromium; engine input surface loses its DOM-isms. No networking, no feel change.

- **Portable worldgen.** New `lib/world/noise.ts`: integer avalanche hash (`Math.imul`/xor-shift) → `hash2D`, integer-lattice value noise (3–4 octaves) replacing `smoothNoise2D`, and `portableSin/Cos` (range-reduce + minimax polynomial) for `carveCaves`' walk and `daylightAt`. Swap into `lib/world/generation.ts`; audit with `grep -nE 'Math\.(sin|cos|tan|atan|exp|log)'` over sim-affecting paths (`playerMotion` trig may stay — frame-local, never seed-determined). **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11** in `lib/game/config.ts`; re-baseline hashes in `lib/world/generation.test.ts` per the documented policy (the structural probes — flat is level, islands flood, villages find flat land — are the acceptance tests for terrain quality). Move digest constants to a new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`.
- **Cross-engine determinism e2e.** New `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`: in-page `crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", engine.state.world.blocks)` vs the baked Bun baseline → proves Chromium ≡ Bun per seed.
- **TickDriver.** New `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`: `createAccumulator` (the exact ≤50 ms/5-substep catch-up lifted from `useMinecraftGame.ts:294-305`) used by the SP rAF loop unchanged, and `createFixedTicker` (drift-corrected chained `setTimeout`, injectable clock) for the phase-4 server. SP stays variable-dt — forcing 20 Hz on the client would add latency for no v1 benefit.
- **Input intents.** `FrameInput` becomes `{ move: {forward,back,left,right,jump,sprint,crouch}, mineHeld }`; `systems/playerMotion.ts:77-91` reads intents; DOM key codes, CapsLock, and pointer-lock resolution move entirely into `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`. `applyLook` unchanged. Shared test helper for the 40+ `FrameInput` call sites.
- **Docs/tests:** architecture.md (input, TickDriver), testing.md (worldgen policy: cross-engine now e2e-pinned; Bun pin no longer load-bearing), save-format.md (v11 worldgen entry — old worlds discard diffs per existing rule), CHANGELOG (flag the world re-roll).

### Phase 2 — Multi-player engine core (`mp/2-multiplayer-engine`) — biggest phase

**Goal:** `players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; all 23 systems converted; save v17; SP behavior and the entire existing e2e suite pass unchanged (the acceptance bar).

- **State** (`state.ts`): `PlayerState` absorbs the ~25 flat per-player fields (position/velocity/yaw/pitch, inventory, armor, selectedSlot, hearts/hunger/oxygen, effects/xp/stats/advancements, isDead/respawnTimer/gameOver, sleeping, spawnPoint, mining, fishing, mountedVehicleId, UI-open flags, `input: FrameInput`, per-player timer split of `GameTimers`). `GameState` gains `players` + `primaryPlayerId`; world timers (spawn directors, randomTick, breed) stay global.
- **Compat aliases** (new `lib/game/engine/players.ts`): `state.player`, `state.inventory`, `state.hearts`, … become accessor properties delegating to the primary player — keeps `window.__monecraft`, every e2e assertion, and shell code working. Permanent, but **engine systems must not use them**: enforce with `no-restricted-syntax` on `state.player` under `lib/game/engine/systems/` once conversion completes.
- **Engine surface** (`GameEngine.ts`): `dispatch(cmd, playerId = primary)`; `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` replaces the `step` input param; `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` (serialize-on-leave); `apiFor(playerId)`; options gain `authority: "local" | "server"` (server ignores `pause`, skips weather + local player motion) and `headless` (skip snapshot building). Player-scoped `GameEvent`s gain `playerId` attribution.
- **Systems** (convert in dependency order, tests green at each step): mobAI targets `nearestTargetablePlayer`; spawn directors round-robin players as spawn centers with a global cap scaled `× ceil(players/2)`; randomTicks split their sample budget across players; **sleep** = per-player `sleeping` flag, fade when *all* non-dead non-spectator players sleep (+ new `wakeUp` command) — SP observable behavior identical; death/respawn per player (SP keeps its "only mobs tick while dead" semantics under `authority:"local"`); hardcore = per-player permadeath→spectator, world `gameOver` when all players are. `ProjectileState.fromPlayer` → `ownerPlayerId`; mob `owner`/vehicle `rider` become PlayerIds.
- **Save v17** (`types.ts`, `save.ts`): world-level fields stay top-level; `players: SavedPlayer[]`; `migrateSaveV16toV17` wraps the flat fields as `[{id:"local", …}]`. Round-trip + migration tests.
- **New tests:** `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (two players: mob targeting, death isolation, inventory isolation, all-asleep night skip, two-player save round-trip). **Docs:** architecture.md engine rewrite, save-format.md v17, testing.md helper, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 3 — Accounts, Postgres, cloud saves, invites (`mp/3-accounts-cloud-saves`)

**Goal:** identity + persistence + ticket mint on the Vercel side. No realtime.

- **DB:** Drizzle ORM + `postgres` driver (runs on both Bun and Node; PGlite driver in tests so CI stays daemon-free). New `db/{schema.ts,index.ts,migrations/}`: better-auth tables (+`skinId`, `isAnonymous`) plus `worlds` (`kind: 'sp-cloud'|'mp'`, seed, worldType, mode/difficulty/hardcore, `saveBlob bytea` gzipped, worldgenVersion, saveVersion, updatedAt), `worldMembers` (role owner|member), `worldInvites` (token, expiry, maxUses).
- **Auth:** `lib/auth/server.ts` (better-auth + anonymous plugin; the account-upgrade hook re-parents worlds/memberships — **integration-test this first**, it's the "guest keeps worlds" promise), `lib/auth/client.ts` (guest session created lazily on first online action, never on plain SP play), `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts`.
- **API routes** (`app/api/`): worlds CRUD; `worlds/[id]/save` GET/PUT gzipped SP blob with 409-on-stale LWW; invites create/resolve/accept; `worlds/[id]/ticket` POST → HS256 JWT (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, Web Crypto, 60 s TTL, claims `{sub, wid, name, skinId, role, pv}`) signed with `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`.
- **Client:** `components/menu/AccountPanel.tsx` (sign in/up, guest, upgrade); `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` (debounced ~60 s push piggybacking the autosave path + on quit; world-select merges local+cloud lists; play downloads blob→localStorage→normal boot; gzip via `CompressionStream`).
- **Dev:** `.env.example` (`DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`), `docker-compose.yml` (postgres:16-alpine).
- **Tests:** ticket round-trip/expiry, PGlite CRUD, invite idempotency, LWW conflict, AccountPanel component tests. **Docs:** new `docs/online.md`, architecture.md web/API layer, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 4 — Game server + protocol (`mp/4-game-server-protocol`)

**Goal:** Bun room server on Fly speaking protocol v1, persisting to Postgres; fully headless-testable.

- **Shared protocol** `lib/net/protocol.ts` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1`, hand-rolled total validators in `save.ts` house style):
  - C2S: `hello{ticket,protocol}` · `pose{seq,x,y,z,yaw,pitch,onGround}` @20 Hz · `cmd{seq,cmd,pose}` (client-claimed eye pose applied — sanity-checked — before dispatch so aimed raycasts resolve server-side with unchanged `Command` shapes) · `chat` · `ping` · `resync`
  - S2C: `welcome` (ids, seed, mode, roster) · one gzipped binary **world-sync** frame (changes/blockEntities/lootedChests/mobs/vehicles/dayClock) · per-tick `tick{n, ev, pp, mp(10 Hz, deadband), day?, self?}` where `self` is the per-client authoritative delta (inventory/hearts/xp/…) · `mobsKeyframe` every ~5 s · `playerJoined/Left` · `container` · `chat` · `pong` · `forcePose` · `kick{code}`. Close codes 4000–4008. JSON first; envelope leaves room for binary packing later.
  - `lib/net/codec.ts` (gzip: `Bun.gzipSync` / `DecompressionStream`), `lib/net/clock.ts` (RTT EWMA).
- **Server** `server/`: `index.ts` (`Bun.serve`: `/health`, `/rooms` w/ ADMIN_TOKEN, WS upgrade), `roomRegistry.ts`, `room.ts`, `connection.ts` (hello deadline, rate limits), `persistence.ts` (drizzle + in-memory adapter for tests), `remoteMotion.ts` (`applyRemotePoses`: clamp speed to `SPRINT_SPEED×effects×1.25`, reject teleports → `forcePose`, synthesize the move result feeding the unchanged hunger/fall-damage pipeline), `Dockerfile` (`oven/bun:1.3.12` = CI pin), `fly.toml` (single region, health checks, no autostop).
- **Room lifecycle:** construct engine `{authority:"server", headless:true}` from Postgres blob or fresh seed; `createFixedTicker` 20 Hz; persist gzipped save every 60 s + on last-leave + SIGTERM drain; idle 5 min → persist + evict; `MAX_ROOMS` start 6, tuned from `/rooms` p95 tick stats; backpressure via `ws.getBufferedAmount()` (shed pp/mp > 256 KB; kick > 1 MB sustained).
- **No build step:** Bun honors root tsconfig `paths` natively — `bun server/index.ts` just runs; `tsc --noEmit` already covers it; ESLint `no-restricted-imports` keeps `server/**` out of render/audio/ui/components.
- **Tests:** protocol validators, fixed-ticker drift (fake clock), `room.test.ts` with fake sockets + in-memory persistence (join/edit propagation/speedhack correction/idle eviction/self-deltas), one real-socket smoke on an ephemeral port; `scripts/netProbe.ts` CLI client for staging. **Docs:** new `docs/protocol.md`, online.md ops section, architecture.md server layer, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 5 — Client online play (`mp/5-client-online-play`)

**Goal:** browser plays on the server; SP path untouched.

- **Session seam:** `lib/game/session.ts` — `GameSession { engine, api, kind: "local"|"online" }`; `createLocalSession` absorbs today's construct/save/autosave from `useMinecraftGame.ts` (which now just accepts a session).
- **`lib/net/NetworkSession.ts`:** owns the WS + a **replica engine** (new `replica: true` option: worldgen from seed + join-diff applied, `step` runs only local motion + presentation — mobAI/spawns/dayNight replicated instead). Renderer/audio/minimap/HUD consume the replica's state **unchanged** — no renderer surgery. Outbound: pose @20 Hz; command routing table (local-only: toggles/pause/camera → replica; networked: craft/move/place/attack/… → `cmd` envelope, `selectSlot` optimistic both). Inbound: events replayed onto the replica (block events set `worldMeshDirty`; rest forwarded to the existing renderer/audio event drain); `pp`/`mp` → `lib/net/interpolation.ts` ring buffers sampled at `serverTime − 125 ms`; `self` deltas overwrite replica player fields. Guard the authority/replica system split with a declarative `SYSTEM_SCHEDULE` table (`runsOn: authority|replica|both`) in `GameEngine.step`.
- **Remote avatars:** `lib/game/render/remotePlayerVisuals.ts` reusing `playerModel.ts`/`playerPose.ts` + skin palettes + procedural name-tag sprite.
- **Shell/UX:** world-select **Online** section (create online world, copy invite link); `app/join/[token]/page.tsx` (guest auto-session → accept → play); ticket mint → `NetworkSession.connect`. New `ChatPanel.tsx` (T/Enter, exits pointer lock, fading log; MP-only) and `ConnectionStatus.tsx` (ping badge, reconnect banner, disconnect modal). Pause menu in MP is personal (world keeps running); "Save & Quit" → "Leave world". Mining is server-confirmed (~1 RTT break latency accepted for v1).
- **Tests:** NetworkSession vs fake socket (routing, self-delta, event replay), interpolation math, component tests. **e2e `multiplayer.e2e.ts`:** Playwright boots `next start` + `bun server/index.ts` (`PERSISTENCE=memory`), two browser contexts — B joins A's world via invite, block edit propagates < 2 s, chat round-trips, both see 2 players. **Docs:** manual.md (playing online), online.md, architecture.md session layer, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 6 — Hardening + ops (`mp/6-hardening-ops`) → GA (v0.13.0)

- Reconnect: retry ladder (1/2/4/8 s ×5) with fresh ticket → `resync` → full world-sync + keyframe; e2e kills the socket and asserts seamless resume.
- Latency sim knob: `NetworkSession.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` via `window.__monecraft.net` + env var.
- Replay debugging: per-room ring buffer of `{tick, playerId, cmd}` + pose checkpoints; `/rooms/:id/log` dump; `server/scripts/replay.ts` reproduces server state offline.
- Owner kick + invite revocation; `server/scripts/loadSim.ts` soak (N synthetic clients → tick p95/bandwidth → tune `MAX_ROOMS`, deadbands); `/rooms` stats; runbook in online.md; tuning.md gains net constants.

---

## Local development & play

- **Single-player (unchanged):** `bun run dev` → http://localhost:3000 → play offline exactly as today. No Postgres, no game server, no account — SP never touches the network stack.
- **Full online stack on localhost:** `docker compose up -d` (Postgres) + `bun run dev` (Next: menus, auth, API) + `bun server/index.ts` (game server, ws://localhost:8080). A `bun run dev:all` script starts all three; `.env.example` documents the env vars. Open two browser windows, sign in as two guests, join the same world via the invite link — full multiplayer against yourself on localhost.
- **Quick server-only iteration:** the game server runs with `PERSISTENCE=memory` (no DB) — same mode the Playwright MP e2e uses; `scripts/netProbe.ts` connects a CLI client for protocol debugging without a browser.
- **Debugging:** `window.__monecraft` handle keeps working in SP and MP (replica engine); Phase 6 adds a latency-simulation knob (`window.__monecraft.net.setSimulatedLatency(ms)`) and server-side command-log capture + offline replay (`server/scripts/replay.ts`).

## New dependencies

`better-auth`, `drizzle-orm`, `postgres` (runtime); `drizzle-kit`, `@electric-sql/pglite` (dev). No websocket lib needed (Bun native server, browser native client). Everything else stays procedural/zero-asset.

## Bandwidth/perf sanity (8 players)

S2C ≈ 10–35 KB/s per client JSON (poses 20 Hz, mobs 10 Hz deadbanded, events bursty); join payload ≈ 0.2–1.5 MB gzipped; C2S ≈ 1.2 KB/s. Room tick must stay ≪ 50 ms (SP steps run in single-digit ms today; `/rooms` reports p95 to tune `MAX_ROOMS`).

## Riskiest items (watch list)

1. **Phase 2 blast radius** — contained by the alias layer, dependency-ordered conversion, and the "existing e2e pass unchanged" bar; will dominate the schedule.
2. **better-auth anonymous→upgrade re-parenting** — integration-test before building UI on it.
3. **Value-noise terrain quality** — structural probes pin acceptance; budget a tuning loop.
4. **Single-threaded Bun room budget** — measure, don't assume; scale-out fallback (room→machine affinity via ticket mint) needs no protocol change.
5. Hybrid model trusts client pose on command envelopes (aim/reach hacks possible) — accepted for invite-only co-op; envelope already carries what server-side validation would need later.

## Out of scope for v1

PvP tuning, interest management/chunk streaming, client prediction/rollback, public rooms/matchmaking, moderation, spectator sharing, SP→MP world conversion (schema already permits it later).

## Verification (every phase)

`bun run lint` + `bun run typecheck` + `bun run format:check` + `bun test` + `bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` for phases 1, 2, 5, 6 (renderer/input/shell touched). Manual gameplay pass after phases 1 (terrain look, all four world types) and 5 (two real browsers on a Fly deploy). Docs + tests + CHANGELOG land inside each phase's PR, per AGENTS.md.

1	import { BiomeId, BlockId, WORLD_SIZE_X, WORLD_SIZE_Y, WORLD_SIZE_Z } from "./blocks";
2	import { isDoorBlock } from "./doors";
3	
4	/**
5	 * Voxel data store plus cheap world queries. Terrain generation lives in
6	 * generation.ts, meshing in meshing.ts, raycast/collision in queries.ts.
7	 *
8	 * ⚠ Save-format invariants: saves address voxels through index(), and getBiome()
9	 * feeds terrain generation. Changing either breaks every existing save — see
10	 * generation.test.ts.
11	 */
12	export class VoxelWorld {
13	  readonly sizeX: number;
14	  readonly sizeY: number;
15	  readonly sizeZ: number;
16	  readonly seed: number;
17	  readonly blocks: Uint8Array;
18	  /**
19	   * Per-voxel light, packed (skyLight << 4) | blockLight, 0..15 each. A DERIVED
20	   * cache (never serialized): computeFullLight bakes it from blocks at load and
21	   * applyEdit patches it on block edits — see lighting.ts. Starts dark; the
22	   * engine bakes it once the block grid is final.
23	   */
24	  light: Uint8Array;
25	
26	  constructor(sizeX = WORLD_SIZE_X, sizeY = WORLD_SIZE_Y, sizeZ = WORLD_SIZE_Z, seed = 1337) {
27	    this.sizeX = sizeX;
28	    this.sizeY = sizeY;
29	    this.sizeZ = sizeZ;
30	    this.seed = seed;
31	    this.blocks = new Uint8Array(sizeX * sizeY * sizeZ);
32	    this.light = new Uint8Array(sizeX * sizeY * sizeZ);
33	  }
34	
35	  index(x: number, y: number, z: number): number {
36	    return x + z * this.sizeX + y * this.sizeX * this.sizeZ;
37	  }
38	
39	  inBounds(x: number, y: number, z: number): boolean {
40	    return x >= 0 && y >= 0 && z >= 0 && x < this.sizeX && y < this.sizeY && z < this.sizeZ;
41	  }
42	
43	  get(x: number, y: number, z: number): number {
44	    if (!this.inBounds(x, y, z)) return BlockId.Air;
45	    return this.blocks[this.index(x, y, z)];
46	  }
47	
48	  set(x: number, y: number, z: number, block: BlockId): void {
49	    if (!this.inBounds(x, y, z)) return;
50	    this.blocks[this.index(x, y, z)] = block;
51	  }
52	
53	  isSolid(x: number, y: number, z: number): boolean {
54	    const block = this.get(x, y, z);
55	    return block !== BlockId.Air && block !== BlockId.Water;
56	  }
57	
58	  /** Sky-light level (0..15) at a voxel. Outside the world reads as open sky. */
59	  getSky(x: number, y: number, z: number): number {
60	    if (!this.inBounds(x, y, z)) return 15;
61	    return this.light[this.index(x, y, z)] >> 4;
62	  }
63	
64	  /** Block-light level (0..15) at a voxel. Outside the world is unlit. */
65	  getBlockLight(x: number, y: number, z: number): number {
66	    if (!this.inBounds(x, y, z)) return 0;
67	    return this.light[this.index(x, y, z)] & 0x0f;
68	  }
69	
70	  highestSolidY(x: number, z: number): number {
71	    for (let y = this.sizeY - 1; y >= 0; y -= 1) {
72	      const block = this.get(x, y, z);
73	      if (this.isSolid(x, y, z) && !isDoorBlock(block)) return y;
74	    }
75	    return 0;
76	  }
77	
78	  getBiome(x: number, z: number): BiomeId {
79	    // Two incommensurate, direction-rotated sine octaves per field, with
80	    // dominant wavelengths of ~250-900 blocks: each field traverses several
81	    // cycles across the 512-block map, so every world gets coherent patches
82	    // of all five biomes (~60-150 block scale).
83	    const s = this.seed * 0.007;
84	    const temp = Math.sin(x * 0.013 + z * 0.006 + s * 1.3) * 0.6 + Math.sin(x * 0.029 - z * 0.017 + s * 2.4) * 0.4;
85	    const moisture = Math.sin(x * 0.007 - z * 0.012 + s * 0.8) * 0.6 + Math.sin(x * 0.019 + z * 0.023 - s * 1.6) * 0.4;
86	    const continental = Math.sin(x * 0.008 + z * 0.01 + s * 2.1) * 0.55 + Math.sin(x * 0.014 - z * 0.009 - s * 1.7) * 0.45;
87	    const ridge = Math.sin(x * 0.024 + z * 0.02 + s) * 0.5 + Math.sin(x * 0.016 - z * 0.024 - s) * 0.5;
88	
89	    if (continental < -0.52) return BiomeId.Ocean;
90	    if ((continental > 0.5 && ridge > 0) || ridge > 0.8) return BiomeId.Mountains;
91	    if (temp > 0.2 && moisture < -0.12) return BiomeId.Desert;
92	    if (moisture > 0.18) return BiomeId.Forest;
93	    return BiomeId.Plains;
94	  }
95	}
96

120	/** The terrain config for a world type. "default" returns the GEN values verbatim. */
121	export function terrainConfigFor(worldType: WorldType): TerrainConfig {
122	  switch (worldType) {
123	    case "flat":
124	      // Flat dry ground just above sea level (no water); biome-colored top.
125	      return { seaLevel: GEN.seaLevel, biomes: biomeHeights(() => ({ baseHeight: 48, noiseScale: 0 })) };
126	    case "amplified":
127	      // Exaggerated relief; mountains clamp at the height ceiling as plateaus.
128	      return { seaLevel: GEN.seaLevel, biomes: biomeHeights((b) => ({ baseHeight: b.baseHeight, noiseScale: b.noiseScale * 2 })) };
129	    case "islands":
130	      return { seaLevel: 54, biomes: ISLANDS_BIOMES };
131	    default:
132	      return { seaLevel: GEN.seaLevel, biomes: biomeHeights((b) => b) };
133	  }
134	}

136	function hash2D(x: number, z: number): number {
137	  const n = Math.sin(x * 127.1 + z * 311.7) * 43758.5453123;
138	  return n - Math.floor(n);
139	}
140	
141	function smoothNoise2D(x: number, z: number, seed: number): number {
142	  const s = seed * 0.013;
143	  const val =
144	    Math.sin(x * 0.015 + s) * 1.2 +
145	    Math.cos(z * 0.012 + s * 1.4) * 1.2 +
146	    Math.sin(x * 0.005 - z * 0.007 + s * 0.7) * 3.5 +
147	    Math.cos(x * 0.031 + z * 0.027 + s * 2.1) * 0.4;
148	  return val;
149	}

151	export function generateWorld(world: VoxelWorld, worldType: WorldType = "default"): void {
152	  // Fork on the type up front, before any block write: "default" yields the GEN
153	  // values so its output is byte-identical to before this feature.
154	  const cfg = terrainConfigFor(worldType);
155	
156	  const rand = (() => {
157	    let t = (world.seed >>> 0) + 0x6d2b79f5;
158	    return () => {
159	      t += 0x6d2b79f5;
160	      let r = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), 1 | t);
161	      r ^= r + Math.imul(r ^ (r >>> 7), 61 | r);
162	      return ((r ^ (r >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
163	    };
164	  })();
165	
166	  generateTerrain(world, cfg);
167	  carveCaves(world, rand);
168	  placeWater(world, cfg);
169	  placeBeaches(world, cfg);
170	  placeOres(world, rand);
171	  // Coal runs on its own PRNG (placeCoal), so it adds ore underground without
172	  // shifting the shared `rand` — trees/structures/dungeons stay byte-identical.
173	  placeCoal(world);
174	  // After placeOres so it can't shift ore RNG (placeOres gates rand on air
175	  // adjacency, which lava would change), and before placeDungeons so dungeon
176	  // rooms — whose floors can sit at or below lavaLevel — overwrite any lava
177	  // rather than flooding. Trees/cacti/houses only read the surface, far above.
178	  placeLava(world);
179	  placeTrees(world, rand);
180	  placeCacti(world);
181	  placeStructures(world, rand);
182	  placeDungeons(world, cfg);
183	  // Villages run on their own decoupled PRNG (villageRand), so they add
184	  // structures without shifting any other stream — every pass above stays
185	  // byte-identical to a village-less world of the same seed.
186	  placeVillages(world, cfg);
187	  // Shipwrecks likewise run on their own PRNG (shipwreckRand), before ocean
188	  // flora so kelp can't occupy a hull cell the wreck is about to overwrite.
189	  placeShipwrecks(world, cfg);
190	  // Ocean flora is hash-gated like cacti (consumes no shared PRNG), so every
191	  // earlier pass stays byte-identical to a kelp-less world of the same seed.

200	  const maxZ = world.sizeZ - 1;

202	  // Fast clear and bedrock

216	      const topY = Math.max(5, Math.min(world.sizeY - 5, Math.floor(baseHeight + noise * noiseScale)));

223	        topBlock = BlockId.Stone;
224	      }
225	
226	      for (let y = 1; y <= topY; y += 1) {
227	        if (y === topY) {
228	          world.set(x, y, z, topBlock);
229	        } else if (y > topY - 3) {

246	    for (let z = 0; z < world.sizeZ; z += 1) {

259	    const maxYc = Math.min(world.sizeY - 2, Math.ceil(cy + radius));

262	    for (let y = minY; y <= maxYc; y += 1) {

4	/** Daylight level 0.04–1.0 for a given day clock. The single source of the formula. */
5	export function daylightAt(dayClock: number): number {
6	  const phase = (dayClock % DAY_CYCLE_SECONDS) / DAY_CYCLE_SECONDS;
7	  return Math.max(0.04, Math.sin(phase * Math.PI * 2) * 0.95 + 0.05);
8	}

13	}

1	import { WEATHER_CYCLE_SECONDS, WEATHER_RAIN_FRACTION } from "@/lib/game/config";
2	import { BiomeId } from "@/lib/world";
3	import type { GameState, WeatherKind } from "../state";
4	
5	/**
6	 * Cosmetic, transient weather. Deterministic from `dayClock` + world seed: time
7	 * is split into fixed windows, a seeded hash of the window index decides whether
8	 * it precipitates, and a triangular envelope ramps intensity 0→1→0 across the
9	 * window so it eases in and out.
10	 *
11	 * Being a pure function of `dayClock` (no internal accumulator) makes it immune
12	 * to the engine's substep catch-up loop — slicing the same elapsed time into
13	 * more or fewer steps yields the identical result. Weather is NEVER persisted
14	 * and NEVER touches spawn/daylight balance — it only sets `state.weather`.
15	 */
16	
17	function hash01(n: number, seed: number): number {
18	  const v = Math.sin((n + 1) * 12.9898 + seed * 78.233) * 43758.5453;
19	  return v - Math.floor(v);
20	}
21	
22	export function weatherAt(dayClock: number, seed: number): { active: boolean; intensity: number } {
23	  const cycle = Math.floor(dayClock / WEATHER_CYCLE_SECONDS);
24	  if (hash01(cycle, seed) >= WEATHER_RAIN_FRACTION) return { active: false, intensity: 0 };
25	  const phase = (dayClock % WEATHER_CYCLE_SECONDS) / WEATHER_CYCLE_SECONDS; // 0..1
26	  return { active: true, intensity: 1 - Math.abs(phase * 2 - 1) };
27	}
28	
29	/** Snowy biomes get snow; dry biomes stay clear; everything else rains. */
30	function precipKindFor(biome: BiomeId): WeatherKind {
31	  if (biome === BiomeId.Mountains) return "snow";
32	  if (biome === BiomeId.Desert || biome === BiomeId.Ocean) return "clear";
33	  return "rain";
34	}
35	
36	export function tickWeather(state: GameState): void {
37	  const { active, intensity } = weatherAt(state.dayClock, state.world.seed);
38	  if (!active) {
39	    state.weather.kind = "clear";
40	    state.weather.intensity = 0;
41	    return;
42	  }
43	  const kind = precipKindFor(state.world.getBiome(Math.floor(state.player.position.x), Math.floor(state.player.position.z)));
44	  state.weather.kind = kind;
45	  state.weather.intensity = kind === "clear" ? 0 : intensity;
46	}

  "content": "/**\n * Bit-portable noise and trig for seed-determined code (worldgen, biomes,\n * weather windows, daylight). ECMA-262 leaves Math.sin/cos implementation-\n * defined, so two JS engines can disagree in the last bits — enough to flip a\n * Math.floor and change generated world bytes for the same seed. Everything\n * here uses only operations IEEE 754 specifies exactly (+, -, *, /,\n * Math.floor, Math.imul, bit ops), so a Bun/Node server and any browser\n * generate identical worlds from a seed. Frame-local gameplay math (aiming,\n * mob steering, doors) may keep native Math trig: it never feeds\n * seed-determined bytes. See docs/testing.md.\n */\n\nconst TWO_PI = 6.283185307179586;\nconst INV_TWO_PI = 1 / TWO_PI;\n\n// Taylor coefficients for sin on [0, π/2]; degree 11 keeps the truncation\n// error (< 6e-8 at π/2) far below anything terrain math can observe. Exact\n// rationals, so no dependence on someone's minimax tables.\nconst S3 = -1 / 6;\nconst S5 = 1 / 120;\nconst S7 = -1 / 5040;\nconst S9 = 1 / 362880;\nconst S11 = -1 / 39916800;\n\n/**\n * sin(x), engine-portable. Range-reduces to a quarter wave with Math.floor,\n * then evaluates an odd degree-11 polynomial. |error| < 1e-7 vs true sine —\n * visually identical, but bit-identical across engines.\n */\nexport function portableSin(x: number): number {\n  let t = x * INV_TWO_PI; // turns\n  t -= Math.floor(t); // [0, 1)\n  let sign = 1;\n  if (t >= 0.5) {\n    // sin(θ + π) = -sin θ\n    t -= 0.5;\n    sign = -1;\n  }\n  if (t > 0.25) t = 0.5 - t; // fold the second quarter back onto the first\n  const u = t * TWO_PI; // [0, π/2]\n  const u2 = u * u;\n  return sign * u * (1 + u2 * (S3 + u2 * (S5 + u2 * (S7 + u2 * (S9 + u2 * S11)))));\n}\n\n/** cos(x), engine-portable (quarter-turn phase shift of portableSin). */\nexport function portableCos(x: number): number {\n  return portableSin(x + TWO_PI * 0.25);\n}\n\n/** 32-bit avalanche hash (xorshift-multiply); uniform in [0, 2^32). */\nexport function hashU32(v: number): number {\n  let h = v | 0;\n  h ^= h >>> 16;\n  h = Math.imul(h, 0x7feb352d);\n  h ^= h >>> 15;\n  h = Math.imul(h, 0x846ca68b);\n  h ^= h >>> 16;\n  return h >>> 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * Deterministic [0, 1) from two (possibly fractional) block coordinates.\n * Coordinates are quantized to 1/4096 of a block before hashing; worldgen\n * callers pass values well inside int32 after scaling.\n */\nexport function hash2D(x: number, z: number): number {\n  const xi = Math.floor(x * 4096) | 0;\n  const zi = Math.floor(z * 4096) | 0;\n  return hashU32((Math.imul(xi, 0x9e3779b1) ^ Math.imul(zi, 0x85ebca6b)) | 0) / 4294967296;\n}\n\n/** Deterministic [0, 1) from an integer index plus a seed (weather windows). */\nexport function hash01(n: number, seed: number): number {\n  return hashU32((Math.imul(n | 0, 0x9e3779b1) ^ Math.imul(seed | 0, 0x85ebca6b)) | 0) / 4294967296;\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { describe, expect, test } from \"bun:test\";\nimport { hash01, hash2D, hashU32, portableCos, portableSin } from \"./noise\";\n\n/**\n * portableSin/portableCos accuracy is checked against native Math.sin — not for\n * exactness (the whole point is NOT matching an engine-defined function) but to\n * pin that the polynomial is a faithful sine. The golden-value tests pin exact\n * doubles: if they ever fail on some runtime, that runtime broke the\n * cross-engine determinism contract worldgen depends on (see docs/testing.md).\n */\n\ndescribe(\"portableSin\", () => {\n  test(\"stays within 1e-6 of a true sine across many periods\", () => {\n    let maxErr = 0;\n    for (let i = -3000; i <= 3000; i += 1) {\n      const x = i * 0.0173; // irrational-ish stride, ~±52 rad\n      maxErr = Math.max(maxErr, Math.abs(portableSin(x) - Math.sin(x)));\n    }\n    expect(maxErr).toBeLessThan(1e-6);\n  });\n\n  test(\"cos matches sin's quarter-turn shift and stays within 1e-6\", () => {\n    let maxErr = 0;\n    for (let i = -1000; i <= 1000; i += 1) {\n      const x = i * 0.041;\n      maxErr = Math.max(maxErr, Math.abs(portableCos(x) - Math.cos(x)));\n    }\n    expect(maxErr).toBeLessThan(1e-6);\n  });\n\n  test(\"exact anchor points\", () => {\n    expect(portableSin(0)).toBe(0);\n    expect(portableSin(Math.PI / 2)).toBeCloseTo(1, 9);\n    expect(portableSin(-Math.PI / 2)).toBeCloseTo(-1, 9);\n    expect(portableCos(0)).toBeCloseTo(1, 12);\n  });\n\n  test(\"is periodic: one full turn returns the same double\", () => {\n    // 2π in doubles is not exactly a period of true sine, but portableSin\n    // range-reduces in turns, so whole-turn offsets that survive float\n    // addition exactly must agree bit-for-bit.\n    expect(portableSin(1.25)).toBe(portableSin(1.25 + 6.283185307179586 * 4));\n  });\n\n  test(\"golden values are bit-stable (cross-engine determinism pin)\", () => {\n    // Doubles printed with full precision; any engine that disagrees on these\n    // would generate different worlds from the same seed.\n    expect(portableSin(1)).toBe(0.8414709847959145);\n    expect(portableSin(12.34)).toBe(-0.22444217660992121);\n    expect(portableSin(-77.7)).toBe(0.5849170824568748);\n    expect(portableCos(3.21)).toBe(-0.9976063813191737);\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe(\"hashes\", () => {\n  test(\"hashU32 avalanche: adjacent inputs decorrelate\", () => {\n    const a = hashU32(1);\n    const b = hashU32(2);\n    expect(a).not.toBe(b);\n    // Hamming distance of adjacent hashes should be substantial.\n    let bits = (a ^ b) >>> 0;\n    let count = 0;\n    while (bits) {\n      count += bits & 1;\n      bits >>>= 1;\n    }\n    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(8);\n  });\n\n  test(\"hash2D is deterministic, in [0,1), and sensitive to both axes\", () => {\n    expect(hash2D(12.7, -3.4)).toBe(hash2D(12.7, -3.4));\n    expect(hash2D(12.7, -3.4)).not.toBe(hash2D(12.7, -3.3));\n    expect(hash2D(12.7, -3.4)).not.toBe(hash2D(12.8, -3.4));\n    for (let i = 0; i < 500; i += 1) {\n      const v = hash2D(i * 1.7 + 11.3, i * 2.3 - 7.1);\n      expect(v).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);\n      expect(v).toBeLessThan(1);\n    }\n  });\n\n  test(\"hash2D distribution is roughly uniform (gate fractions hold)\", () => {\n    let above = 0;\n    const n = 20000;\n    for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 1) {\n      if (hash2D(i * 0.37 + 0.05, i * 0.91 - 3.2) > 0.88) above += 1;\n    }\n    // 12% expected; allow generous slop — this pins \"usable as a gate\", not statistics.\n    expect(above / n).toBeGreaterThan(0.09);\n    expect(above / n).toBeLessThan(0.15);\n  });\n\n  test(\"hash01 depends on window index and seed\", () => {\n    expect(hash01(3, 1337)).toBe(hash01(3, 1337));\n    expect(hash01(3, 1337)).not.toBe(hash01(4, 1337));\n    expect(hash01(3, 1337)).not.toBe(hash01(3, 1338));\n  });\n\n  test(\"golden values are bit-stable (cross-engine determinism pin)\", () => {\n    expect(hashU32(1337)).toBe(1682228659);\n    expect(hash2D(1.5, -2.25)).toBe(0.9436538850143552);\n    expect(hash01(7, 424242)).toBe(0.5761599410325289);\n  });\n});\n"
}

  "new_string": "// changes, so old block-diffs (which index against generated terrain) can't be\n// applied to a different baseline: v6 added dungeons; v7 added deep-cave lava\n// lakes; v8 added shallow coal ore; v9 added generated villages; v10 added\n// ocean flora (kelp/coral) and the aquatic-update structures; v11 moved all\n// seed-determined noise to bit-portable implementations (lib/world/noise.ts),\n// so the same seed now generates identical bytes on every JS engine — the\n// prerequisite for a multiplayer server sharing worlds with browsers. Each world\n// records the WORLDGEN_VERSION it was generated under; a world whose recorded\n// version differs from this constant has its block-diffs discarded and is\n// rebooted from its stored seed (lib/game/worlds.ts). The save *schema* (SaveData)\n// is independent of this — lighting is a derived cache and lava is worldgen, so\n// neither is persisted, and additive schema bumps don't touch it.\nexport const WORLDGEN_VERSION = 11;"
}

  "content": "import { WORLDGEN_BASELINES } from \"@/lib/world/generationBaselines\";\nimport { expect, test } from \"./helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Cross-engine worldgen determinism: the same seed must generate byte-identical\n * worlds on every JS engine, because saves ship only seed + block diffs and a\n * multiplayer server (Bun) must agree with browser clients (V8) on the\n * generated baseline. generation.test.ts pins these digests under Bun/JSC;\n * this spec recomputes the full-size digest inside Chromium/V8 against the\n * same constants — if the two engines ever disagreed, lib/world/noise.ts\n * failed at its one job.\n */\ntest(\"Chromium generates the same seed-1337 world bytes as the Bun baseline\", async ({ gamePage }) => {\n  // Freeze the sim first: block edits after boot (e.g. a creeper explosion)\n  // would corrupt the digest. A fresh world has no random-tickable blocks, so\n  // the only mutation vector is gameplay, and pause gates all of it.\n  await gamePage.evaluate(() => {\n    window.__monecraft!.engine.state.mobs = [];\n    window.__monecraft!.engine.dispatch({ type: \"pause\" });\n  });\n\n  // Guard the guard: prove no block edits happened before the hash, so a\n  // digest mismatch can only ever mean cross-engine divergence.\n  const editCount = await gamePage.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.serialize().changes.length);\n  expect(editCount, \"no block edits before hashing\").toBe(0);\n\n  const digest = await gamePage.evaluate(async () => {\n    const blocks = window.__monecraft!.engine.state.world.blocks;\n    const bytes = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest(\"SHA-256\", blocks));\n    return Array.from(bytes)\n      .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, \"0\"))\n      .join(\"\");\n  });\n  expect(digest).toBe(WORLDGEN_BASELINES.full512Seed1337);\n});\n"
}
