65:## The worldgen hash policy
73:1. A **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.
74:2. A **Bun version bump** — the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined (ECMA-262 leaves transcendentals implementation-specific). CI pins `bun-version` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for this reason; bump both together and verify the digests merely shifted rather than the generation logic changing.
78:The **deep-cave lava worldgen** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.
80:The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was the prior re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.
82:The same caveat means the hash tests prove _refactor purity on the pinned engine_, not cross-browser save portability — a player switching browsers may theoretically regenerate slightly different terrain for the same seed. That limitation predates the test suite; it is now at least documented.
---
23:- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of **worldgen** loot chests (dungeon, shipwreck, or buried treasure) the player has already opened or broken. Worldgen chests' contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`, mixed with a per-family constant, from the family's own table) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only sets of _which_ indices belong to each family are not stored; they are re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` / `collectShipwreckSites` / `collectTreasureSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). The field kept its name when shipwrecks/buried treasure generalized it (state-side it is `lootedWorldgenChests`), so pre-aquatic saves read unchanged. Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
43:- **Unreleased (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10)** — the **aquatic update**. Kelp/coral (`BlockId`s **appended**: 55–57), sunken **shipwrecks**, and **buried treasure** all write generated blocks, so the worldgen baseline bumps 9→10 (old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed; the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md). The save **schema stays v16**: cod/salmon are fungible wild mobs (never persisted; `restoreMobs` in older builds drops unknown kinds), kelp growth/harvest rides the block diff, the `treasure_map`/`dried_kelp`/coral items are additive string ids with **no instance state** (the map's compass target is derived from the seed at runtime), and shipwreck/buried chests reuse the persisted `lootedChests` index set unchanged (see above — the fill family is re-derived, not stored).
44:- **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.
45:- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). Validated against the known professions on load. **Generated villages** in the same release bump **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** (villages add structures, so old block-diffs are stale and discarded — the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md); village residents persist via the existing v14 `mobs` field, and **raids** are transient (`state.raid` + raiders aren't serialized, like the boss), so neither needs further save schema beyond the additive `profession` and the by-id Ominous Horn item.
46:- **v14** (persisted mobs — Living World, PR 1) — adds an optional top-level `mobs` (`SavedMob[]`). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no persisted mobs; the world re-seeds its wildlife as before). This is the first mob persistence in the format: `isPersistentMob` keeps only **tamed pets** here (PR-B adds village residents), since the fungible population is re-created each boot. Restored before `spawnInitialMobs`, with `y` re-grounded onto the current surface and fresh ids assigned. The new `faction`/`owner`/`sitting`/`targetId`/`retargetTimer` mob fields are session-side; only the durable ones land in `SavedMob`. The wolf and cat are additive `MobKind`s with no `BlockId`/item changes, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
47:- **v13** (advancements & statistics) — adds optional top-level `stats` (`{ id, value }[]`) and `advancements` (`string[]`). `migrateSaveV12toV13` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ no stats, no advancements yet earned). Both are progression meta folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint and, like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` and `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. No new `BlockId`, no new item, and no worldgen change — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
48:- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
49:- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
50:- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
51:- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

63	**Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.
64	
65	## The worldgen hash policy
66	
67	Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.
68	
69	**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**
70	
71	Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly two cases:
72	
73	1. A **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.
74	2. A **Bun version bump** — the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined (ECMA-262 leaves transcendentals implementation-specific). CI pins `bun-version` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for this reason; bump both together and verify the digests merely shifted rather than the generation logic changing.
75	
76	To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values in the same commit as the cause.
77	
78	The **deep-cave lava worldgen** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.
79	
80	The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was the prior re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.
81	
82	The same caveat means the hash tests prove _refactor purity on the pinned engine_, not cross-browser save portability — a player switching browsers may theoretically regenerate slightly different terrain for the same seed. That limitation predates the test suite; it is now at least documented.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.12.0] - 2026-07-03

### Added

- **The aquatic update**: the ocean the new rafts and ships sail is now worth sailing — fish, flora, wrecks to dive, and treasure to hunt, all on **zero binary assets**. Bumps **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10** (kelp/coral/wrecks/buried chests write generated blocks, so existing worlds reboot from their seed and every worldgen/world-type/meshing digest except flat was re-baselined per docs/testing.md) with **no save-schema change** — the schema stays **v16**.
  - **Kelp & coral**: the sandy ocean floor grows swaying **kelp stalks** and pink/blue **reef coral** (a new hash-gated `placeOceanFlora` pass that consumes no shared PRNG). Kelp is a solid cube painted to read as a plant (the wheat trick — no new geometry): stalks always keep a **3-block clear-water band** below the surface so boats and fishing casts never snag, growth via the existing random-tick sampler enforces the same cap, and **breaking a cell breaks the stalk above it, refilling submerged cells with water — never air**. Kelp smelts **3-at-a-time into dried kelp** (a 2-hunger snack); corals are decorative salvage. New `BlockId`s **appended** (55–57)
  - **Cod & salmon**: the first water-dwelling mobs. A dedicated **aquatic AI branch** (3D wander/flee, every move gated on the destination cell being water, no ground clamp) runs before any land logic; a beached fish flops and suffocates. Both drop **raw fish** — the recipe-book hint for it now reads "Hunt a cod". Fish are fungible (never persisted; old saves load cleanly), spawn as schools in whatever water lies near spawn, and a new **aquatic spawn director** trickles them in around the player (up to `AQUATIC_CAP` 24) so far-flung oceans are stocked too — failing closed on dry worlds (Superflat spawns none). Legless "fish" model variant on `createMobModel`, bubble-blip ZZFX calls
  - **Shipwrecks**: flooded plank hulls (broken walls, snapped mast, always fully submerged) sink onto the deep ocean floor on their own decoupled PRNG, holding 1–2 chests of nautical salvage — and the **treasure map** at a 40% roll. The dungeon lazy-fill generalizes to `fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted`: the site set holding a chest's index picks both the loot table and a family-distinct seed constant, and **all families share the persisted `lootedChests` field unchanged** (no re-roll exploit, no save bump)
  - **Buried treasure & the treasure map**: hold a map (wreck loot, or a rare fishing catch) and a **compass pill** points at the _nearest_ unearthed hoard while red **X**s mark the minimap; dig two blocks under the beach sand for the richest chest table in the game (emeralds guaranteed). The map is deliberately **stateless** — no per-item target, no save field: the compass derives everything from the seed and retargets automatically after each dig. Chests place on a fourth decoupled PRNG with a **seed-pure beach proxy** (terrain-height band + a below-sea neighbor column — never post-water block reads), sand-capped so a breaching cave can't expose them. First dig fires the new **treasureUnearthed** event → **X Marks the Spot** advancement + a **Treasures Unearthed** statistic
---
26:- UI pixel art is procedural: `lib/ui/` generates 16×16 item/HUD sprites as pure pixel buffers (`spritePixels.ts`, `hudPixels.ts` — DOM-free, unit-tested) wrapped by a cached canvas→data-URL layer (`sprites.ts`, falls back to a transparent pixel under happy-dom). `chromeTiles.ts` (`installUiTiles`, idempotent, `document`-guarded) installs the GUI textures as CSS vars: the menu-backdrop noise (`--mc-tile-dirt/stone`) and the chrome grain layered over the flat panel/slot/button colors (`--mc-tile-panel/well/button`, which default to `none` so SSR/pre-install falls back to the solid color). No image assets, no licensing exposure. `lib/ui/` must not import Three.js or the engine.
78:**Dungeon loot chests.** Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents can't ride the block-diff baseline. The engine instead keeps two session-only sets — `dungeonChestIndices` / `dungeonSpawnerIndices` — rebuilt each boot from the seed via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`, which replays the dungeon placement math without writing blocks), plus a **persisted** `lootedDungeonChests` set. On a dungeon chest's first open or break, `systems/dungeon.ts` `fillDungeonChestIfUnlooted` rolls loot seeded from `world.seed ^ voxelIndex` (`lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`) and marks the index looted. Gating on the looted set — not on whether the chest is currently non-empty — is what stops an emptied-then-reloaded chest from re-rolling (an empty container is dropped from `blockEntities`).
93:- **Atmosphere** (all procedural, zero assets, freed in `dispose()`): `particleSystem.ts` + the pure, unit-tested `particlePool.ts` draw event-driven bursts (block shards from `BLOCK_COLORS`, mob-death puffs, eat crumbs, jump/land/footstep dust) as one `THREE.Points` with a soft-sprite shader, spawned via `GameRenderer.handleEvent(event, state)` (wired into the event drain beside `audio.handleEvent`). `skyView.ts` + the pure `starField.ts` layer camera-following stars, a moon, a sun disc, and drifting canvas-noise clouds over the day-night sky lerp, ramped by `daylight`. `precipitation.ts` is the camera-following rain/snow field driven by `state.weather`, and `syncDayNight` adds the matching overcast sky tint + dimmed light + nearer fog.
101:- `audioDirector.ts` — the shell-side observer, exactly parallel to the renderer: `handleEvent(GameEvent)` plays one-shots (block break/place by material, hurt/eat/jump/land, mob attacks, death/respawn stingers) and `sync(state, dt)` drives everything continuous (footsteps, mining hit ticks, mob ambience, music mood, and the weather rain bed). Music follows `state.daylight` immediately and the biome with 5 s hysteresis, and ducks while paused. The rain bed (`rainLoop.ts`) is a looping filtered-noise source on the graph, off the SFX voice budget, whose gain tracks `state.weather` rain intensity (silent for snow / while paused). The engine never imports this module.
130:- `generation.ts` — `generateWorld(world)`: deterministic terrain, caves, lava, water, ores, trees, houses, and underground dungeons (`placeDungeons`, last in the pipeline). `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` (so it can't shift ore RNG) and before `placeDungeons` (so rooms overwrite lava). `collectDungeonSites(world)` re-derives dungeon chest/spawner indices from the seed for the engine. Constants live in the frozen `GEN` object. **Byte-identical output per seed is a save-format contract**, pinned by `generation.test.ts` hash tests — fix code, never hashes.

42	
43	- **Unreleased (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10)** — the **aquatic update**. Kelp/coral (`BlockId`s **appended**: 55–57), sunken **shipwrecks**, and **buried treasure** all write generated blocks, so the worldgen baseline bumps 9→10 (old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed; the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md). The save **schema stays v16**: cod/salmon are fungible wild mobs (never persisted; `restoreMobs` in older builds drops unknown kinds), kelp growth/harvest rides the block diff, the `treasure_map`/`dried_kelp`/coral items are additive string ids with **no instance state** (the map's compass target is derived from the seed at runtime), and shipwreck/buried chests reuse the persisted `lootedChests` index set unchanged (see above — the fill family is re-derived, not stored).
44	- **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.
45	- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). Validated against the known professions on load. **Generated villages** in the same release bump **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** (villages add structures, so old block-diffs are stale and discarded — the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md); village residents persist via the existing v14 `mobs` field, and **raids** are transient (`state.raid` + raiders aren't serialized, like the boss), so neither needs further save schema beyond the additive `profession` and the by-id Ominous Horn item.

  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts",
  "content": "/**\n * Time-stepping drivers for the simulation. The engine's step(dt) is\n * dt-agnostic; these own how wall time becomes step calls:\n *\n * - createAccumulator — variable-dt catch-up stepping for the browser rAF\n *   loop (the shell's driver; feel-identical to stepping every frame).\n * - createFixedTicker — drift-corrected fixed-rate ticks for a headless\n *   authoritative server, where every world must advance at the same cadence\n *   regardless of callback jitter.\n *\n * Both clamp runaway catch-up the same way: at most MAX_SUBSTEPS steps of at\n * most MAX_STEP_SECONDS are owed at once; time beyond that is quietly dropped\n * (e.g. after a background-tab stall or an event-loop hiccup) rather than run\n * in fast-forward.\n */\n\n/** Longest single step the simulation is fed (bounds per-step integration error). */\nexport const MAX_STEP_SECONDS = 0.05;\n/** Most catch-up steps per advance; older debt is dropped. */\nexport const MAX_SUBSTEPS = 5;\n/** The authoritative-server tick length (20 Hz — one MAX_STEP_SECONDS step per tick). */\nexport const TICK_SECONDS = MAX_STEP_SECONDS;\nexport const TICK_RATE = 1 / TICK_SECONDS;\n\nexport type Accumulator = {\n  /**\n   * Advance to wall-clock `nowMs`, invoking `step(dt)` in bounded catch-up\n   * substeps. Returns the simulated seconds this call (what audio.sync wants).\n   */\n  advance(nowMs: number, step: (dt: number) => void): number;\n};\n\n/**\n * Catch-up stepping: a slow frame (software GL, busy machine) can take far\n * longer than one step, and a single clamped step would run the simulation in\n * slow motion. Bounded substeps keep sim time tracking wall time; the cap\n * bounds work per frame and quietly drops time beyond it.\n */\nexport function createAccumulator(opts: { startMs: number; maxStepSeconds?: number; maxSubsteps?: number }): Accumulator {\n  const maxStepSeconds = opts.maxStepSeconds ?? MAX_STEP_SECONDS;\n  const maxSubsteps = opts.maxSubsteps ?? MAX_SUBSTEPS;\n  let last = opts.startMs;\n  let pendingSeconds = 0;\n  return {\n    advance(nowMs, step) {\n      pendingSeconds = Math.min(pendingSeconds + (nowMs - last) / 1000, maxStepSeconds * maxSubsteps);\n      last = nowMs;\n\n      let stepped = 0;\n      while (pendingSeconds > 0) {\n        const dt = Math.min(pendingSeconds, maxStepSeconds);\n        step(dt);\n        pendingSeconds -= dt;\n        stepped += dt;\n      }\n      return stepped;\n    }\n  };\n}\n\nexport type FixedTicker = {\n  stop(): void;\n};\n\nexport type FixedTickerOptions = {\n  onTick: (dt: number) => void;\n  tickSeconds?: number;\n  maxCatchUpTicks?: number;\n  /** Injectable ms clock and timer for tests; default wall clock + setTimeout. */\n  now?: () => number;\n  setTimer?: (fn: () => void, ms: number) => ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;\n  clearTimer?: (id: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>) => void;\n};\n\n/**\n * Fixed-rate ticker that schedules each callback against an absolute target\n * time instead of chaining raw delays, so per-callback latency never\n * accumulates into clock drift. If the event loop stalls past\n * `maxCatchUpTicks` owed ticks, the remaining debt is dropped and the\n * schedule re-anchors at the present (mirroring the accumulator's cap).\n */\nexport function createFixedTicker(opts: FixedTickerOptions): FixedTicker {\n  const tickSeconds = opts.tickSeconds ?? TICK_SECONDS;\n  const maxCatchUpTicks = opts.maxCatchUpTicks ?? MAX_SUBSTEPS;\n  const now = opts.now ?? (() => performance.now());\n  const setTimer = opts.setTimer ?? ((fn, ms) => setTimeout(fn, ms));\n  const clearTimer = opts.clearTimer ?? ((id) => clearTimeout(id));\n  const tickMs = tickSeconds * 1000;\n\n  let stopped = false;\n  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;\n  let target = now() + tickMs;\n\n  const fire = () => {\n    if (stopped) return;\n    let ticks = 0;\n    while (now() >= target) {\n      opts.onTick(tickSeconds);\n      target += tickMs;\n      ticks += 1;\n      if (ticks >= maxCatchUpTicks && now() >= target) {\n        // Stalled well past the cap: drop the debt, re-anchor to the present.\n        target = now() + tickMs;\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n    if (!stopped) timer = setTimer(fire, Math.max(0, target - now()));\n  };\n  timer = setTimer(fire, tickMs);\n\n  return {\n    stop() {\n      stopped = true;\n      if (timer !== null) clearTimer(timer);\n    }\n  };\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "/**\n * Manually-pumped clock + timer queue. advanceTo(ms) jumps the clock to `ms`\n * FIRST, then fires everything due — so a big jump models a stalled event\n * loop (timers fire late and see the late clock), while many small jumps\n * model a punctual one. That distinction is exactly what the ticker's\n * drift/catch-up logic exists for.\n */\nfunction fakeTime() {\n  let nowMs = 0;\n  const timers: Array<{ at: number; fn: () => void; id: number }> = [];\n  let nextId = 1;\n  return {\n    now: () => nowMs,\n    setTimer(fn: () => void, ms: number) {\n      const id = nextId++;\n      timers.push({ at: nowMs + ms, fn, id });\n      return id as unknown as ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;\n    },\n    clearTimer(id: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>) {\n      const i = timers.findIndex((t) => t.id === (id as unknown as number));\n      if (i >= 0) timers.splice(i, 1);\n    },\n    /** Jump the clock to `ms`, then fire all due timers (each may schedule more). */\n    advanceTo(ms: number) {\n      nowMs = ms;\n      for (;;) {\n        timers.sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at);\n        const next = timers[0];\n        if (!next || next.at > ms) break;\n        timers.shift();\n        next.fn();\n      }\n    },\n    /** Advance punctually in `stepMs` hops (timers fire ~on time). */\n    run(toMs: number, stepMs = 10) {\n      for (let t = nowMs + stepMs; t <= toMs; t += stepMs) this.advanceTo(t);\n    }\n  };\n}"
}

/** Per-frame continuous input, owned by the input controller. */
export type FrameInput = {
  keys: ReadonlySet<string>;
  capsActive: boolean;
  leftMouseHeld: boolean;
  pointerLocked: boolean;
};

export const IDLE_INPUT: FrameInput = {
  keys: new Set<string>(),
  capsActive: false,
  leftMouseHeld: false,
  pointerLocked: false
};

  "new_string": "/**\n * Owns every DOM listener and the DOM→intent mapping: raw key codes, CapsLock,\n * and pointer lock stay in here; the engine sees only the abstract FrameInput\n * (a future keybinding screen changes this file alone). Discrete actions\n * become engine commands; mouse-look goes through engine.applyLook.\n */\nexport function createInputController(args: CreateInputControllerArgs): InputController {\n  const { canvas, engine, onResize, onLockChange } = args;\n\n  // Raw DOM-side state, reduced to intents after every change.\n  const pressed = new Set<string>();\n  let capsActive = false;\n  let leftMouseHeld = false;\n  let pointerLocked = false;\n\n  const move: MoveIntents = { forward: false, back: false, left: false, right: false, jump: false, sprint: false, crouch: false };\n  const input: FrameInput = { move, mineHeld: false };\n\n  const syncIntents = () => {\n    move.forward = pressed.has(\"KeyW\");\n    move.back = pressed.has(\"KeyS\");\n    move.left = pressed.has(\"KeyA\");\n    move.right = pressed.has(\"KeyD\");\n    move.jump = pressed.has(\"Space\");\n    move.crouch = pressed.has(\"KeyC\");\n    move.sprint = capsActive;\n    // Mining requires gameplay pointer capture; fold the gate in here so the\n    // engine needs no notion of the cursor.\n    input.mineHeld = leftMouseHeld && pointerLocked;\n  };"
}

108	
109	## Input (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`)
110	
111	Owns every DOM listener. Continuous input (movement keys, mouse button, pointer lock, CapsLock) is exposed as a `FrameInput` the engine reads each step; discrete actions (hotbar, inventory toggle, place, eat, attack, unstuck, pause, F3 debug, V camera view) become commands; mouse-look calls `engine.applyLook`. The first click only acquires pointer lock; `KeyI` exits it.
112	
113	**Pause ↔ pointer lock**: the browser consumes Escape to exit pointer lock, so Esc never reaches keydown while locked — losing the lock during plain gameplay is the pause trigger (`pointerlockchange` dispatches `pause`). The inventory (`KeyI`) and death paths set their state flags _before_ the async `pointerlockchange` fires, and the engine's `pause` command additionally ignores those states, so they don't open the menu. While unlocked, Escape toggles pause directly (and closes the inventory). "Back to Game" resumes and re-requests the lock; Chrome's ~1.25 s cooldown after Esc can reject that request — the rejection is swallowed and the player just clicks the canvas.
114	
115	## Inventory and items (`lib/game/`)
116	
117	- `inventory.ts` — pure slot algebra (`adjustSlotCount`, `craft`, durability, armor); every function returns a new array or `null` for "no change". Crafting refuses when the result doesn't fit rather than destroying overflow. Equipped armor is **dedicated storage**: `state.equippedArmor` (`Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot | null>`) holds the worn pieces themselves — `toggleEquipArmor`/`unequipArmor` move a piece between the inventory and the record, and `equippedDefense`/`armorReduction`/`consumeEquippedArmorDurability` (and Mending's `mendXp`) read/wear/repair those instances directly rather than re-finding them in the inventory by id.
```

> AGENT

**Phase 1 is complete** — all four commits are on `mp/1-deterministic-foundations` (unpushed, per your workflow), with the full verify gate and all 19 e2e specs green.

What landed, per commit:

1. **`feat(world)` — portable worldgen noise** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11). All seed-determined noise moved to `lib/world/noise.ts`, built only from IEEE-exact operations. The headline result: the new `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` generated the full 512×150×512 world **inside Chromium/V8 and got the byte-identical SHA-256 as the Bun/JSC baseline** — the property the whole multiplayer sync model (seed + block diff) rests on. I deliberately kept the original wave formulas on a polynomial sine instead of switching to value noise, which preserved terrain character so well that every structural probe passed the re-baseline untouched. This also retired the "hashes only valid on pinned Bun" caveat.
2. **`refactor(engine)` — tick drivers.** The rAF catch-up stepping moved into `tickDriver.ts` (`createAccumulator`), joined by the drift-corrected `createFixedTicker` the Phase-4 server will use, both fake-clock unit-tested. Single-player keeps variable-dt stepping — feel-identical.
3. **`refactor(input)` — abstract intents.** `FrameInput` is now `{move: {forward…crouch, sprint, jump}, mineHeld}`; DOM key codes, CapsLock, and pointer lock live only in the input controller. This is the shape a network client will put on the wire.
4. A small hygiene commit prettier-ignoring the local `.entire/` tooling dir.

Docs (`architecture.md`, `testing.md`, `save-format.md`), CHANGELOG, and tests shipped inside each slice. One user-facing consequence flagged in the CHANGELOG: **existing worlds re-roll from their seed** (block edits discarded) — standard worldgen-bump policy.

Two things for you:
- The plan calls for a **manual gameplay pass** after this phase (terrain look across the four world types — `bun run dev` and eyeball a few seeds).
- The branch is ready for your review/push whenever you want; I haven't pushed anything.

Next up per plan is **Phase 2, the players-map engine refactor** — the biggest phase (all 23 systems, save v17, with "existing e2e passes unchanged" as the bar). I'll branch it off `mp/1` since it builds on these commits. Want me to proceed?

  "content": "import type { GameState, PlayerId, PlayerState, PlayerTimers, WorldTimers } from \"./state\";\n\n/**\n * The players map and the legacy alias layer.\n *\n * GameState.players holds one PlayerState per player; single-player is the\n * one-entry case. The flat fields the codebase grew up with (`state.player`,\n * `state.inventory`, `state.hearts`, …) remain available as accessor\n * properties that delegate to the PRIMARY player — installed here — so the\n * React shell, the Playwright suite (window.__monecraft), and existing tests\n * keep working unchanged.\n *\n * The aliases are a permanent convenience for the single-player shell, NOT a\n * transition shim — but ENGINE SYSTEMS MUST NOT USE THEM: a system that reads\n * `state.player` silently acts on \"whoever is primary\", which is wrong on a\n * server. Systems take the acting PlayerState explicitly.\n */\n\n/** GameState keys aliased 1:1 onto the primary PlayerState (same name, same type). */\nconst PLAYER_ALIAS_KEYS = [\n  \"inventory\",\n  \"equippedArmor\",\n  \"selectedSlot\",\n  \"gameMode\",\n  \"isFlying\",\n  \"gameOver\",\n  \"hearts\",\n  \"hunger\",\n  \"oxygen\",\n  \"effects\",\n  \"xp\",\n  \"stats\",\n  \"advancements\",\n  \"isDead\",\n  \"respawnTimer\",\n  \"spawnPoint\",\n  \"mining\",\n  \"fishing\",\n  \"mountedVehicleId\",\n  \"inventoryOpen\",\n  \"advancementsOpen\",\n  \"craftingStation\",\n  \"activeVillagerProfession\",\n  \"openContainerIndex\"\n] as const satisfies ReadonlyArray<keyof PlayerState & keyof GameState>;\n\n/** PlayerTimers keys aliased onto state.timers (world timers stay real properties there). */\nconst PLAYER_TIMER_KEYS = [\n  \"voidTimer\",\n  \"regenTimer\",\n  \"waterExposureTimer\",\n  \"waterDamageTimer\",\n  \"lavaBurnTimer\",\n  \"lavaDamageTimer\",\n  \"drownTimer\",\n  \"starvationTimer\",\n  \"sprintDistanceBudget\",\n  \"walkDistanceBudget\",\n  \"jumpBudget\",\n  \"effectRegenTimer\",\n  \"effectPoisonTimer\",\n  \"stuckTimer\",\n  \"spearThrowCooldown\",\n  \"bowCooldownTimer\"\n] as const satisfies ReadonlyArray<keyof PlayerTimers>;\n\nexport function getPlayer(state: GameState, id: PlayerId): PlayerState | undefined {\n  return state.players.get(id);\n}\n\nexport function mustGetPlayer(state: GameState, id: PlayerId): PlayerState {\n  const player = state.players.get(id);\n  if (!player) throw new Error(`Unknown player id: ${id}`);\n  return player;\n}\n\nexport function primaryPlayer(state: GameState): PlayerState {\n  return mustGetPlayer(state, state.primaryPlayerId);\n}\n\n/**\n * The world-level fields of GameState — what the engine constructor actually\n * builds as data. The per-player flat fields (plus `player` and the player\n * half of `timers`) are installed as accessors by installPlayerAliases.\n */\nexport type GameStateBase = Omit<GameState, (typeof PLAYER_ALIAS_KEYS)[number] | \"player\" | \"timers\"> & {\n  timers: WorldTimers;\n};\n\n/**\n * Installs the primary-player accessor aliases onto a base state and returns\n * it as the full GameState. `state.timers` is augmented in place: world timers\n * remain data properties, player timers become accessors onto the primary\n * player's PlayerTimers.\n */\nexport function installPlayerAliases(base: GameStateBase): GameState {\n  const state = base as unknown as GameState;\n\n  Object.defineProperty(state, \"player\", {\n    get: () => primaryPlayer(state),\n    enumerable: true,\n    configurable: true\n  });\n\n  for (const key of PLAYER_ALIAS_KEYS) {\n    Object.defineProperty(state, key, {\n      get: () => primaryPlayer(state)[key],\n      set: (value) => {\n        (primaryPlayer(state) as Record<typeof key, unknown>)[key] = value;\n      },\n      enumerable: true,\n      configurable: true\n    });\n  }\n\n  for (const key of PLAYER_TIMER_KEYS) {\n    Object.defineProperty(state.timers, key, {\n      get: () => primaryPlayer(state).timers[key],\n      set: (value: number) => {\n        primaryPlayer(state).timers[key] = value;\n      },\n      enumerable: true,\n      configurable: true\n    });\n  }\n\n  return state;\n}\n"
}

3	export type BossTracking = {
4	  /** Clockwise screen-space bearing: 0 ahead, 90 right, 180 behind, 270 left. */
5	  bearingDegrees: number;
6	  /** Horizontal distance in world blocks. */
7	  distanceBlocks: number;
8	};
9	
10	/** Derives a compass-style bearing and ground distance from the player to any world point. */
11	export function trackTarget(player: PlayerState, x: number, z: number): BossTracking {
12	  const dx = x - player.position.x;
13	  const dz = z - player.position.z;
14	  const forward = -dx * Math.sin(player.yaw) - dz * Math.cos(player.yaw);
15	  const right = dx * Math.cos(player.yaw) - dz * Math.sin(player.yaw);
16	  const bearing = Math.atan2(right, forward) * (180 / Math.PI);
17	
18	  return {
19	    bearingDegrees: Math.round((bearing + 360) % 360),
20	    distanceBlocks: Math.round(Math.hypot(dx, dz))
21	  };
22	}
23	
24	/** Bearing/distance from the player to the boss (see trackTarget — the treasure compass shares it). */
25	export function bossTracking(player: PlayerState, boss: MobState): BossTracking {
26	  return trackTarget(player, boss.position.x, boss.position.z);
27	}

1	import { MAX_HEARTS, MAX_HUNGER, RESPAWN_SECONDS } from "@/lib/game/config";
2	import { takesDamage } from "@/lib/game/gameModes";
3	import { armorReduction, consumeEquippedArmorDurability } from "@/lib/game/inventory";
4	import { resistanceMultiplier } from "./statusEffects";
5	import type { GameState } from "../state";
6	
7	/**
8	 * Applies armor-mitigated damage (always at least 1) and wears equipped armor.
9	 * The Resistance effect further scales the post-armor amount (combat damage only —
10	 * environmental/poison damage uses the unmitigated/non-lethal paths below).
11	 * Returns true when the hit was lethal — the engine emits the death event.
12	 * Creative/Spectator are invulnerable, so every damage source no-ops here.
13	 */
14	export function applyDamageWithArmor(state: GameState, amount: number, rng?: () => number): boolean {
15	  if (state.isDead || !takesDamage(state.gameMode)) return false;
16	  const value = Math.max(0, Math.floor(amount));
17	  if (value <= 0) return false;
18	
19	  state.equippedArmor = consumeEquippedArmorDurability(state.equippedArmor, 1, rng) ?? state.equippedArmor;
20	  const reduction = armorReduction(state.equippedArmor);
21	  const mitigated = Math.max(1, Math.floor(value * (1 - reduction) * resistanceMultiplier(state)));
22	
23	  state.hearts = Math.max(0, state.hearts - mitigated);
24	  if (state.hearts > 0) return false;
25	
26	  state.isDead = true;
27	  state.respawnTimer = RESPAWN_SECONDS;
28	  return true;
29	}
30	
31	/** Applies environmental damage exactly, bypassing armor and durability wear. */
32	export function applyUnmitigatedDamage(state: GameState, amount: number): boolean {
33	  if (state.isDead || !takesDamage(state.gameMode)) return false;
34	  const value = Math.max(0, Math.floor(amount));
35	  if (value <= 0) return false;
36	
37	  state.hearts = Math.max(0, state.hearts - value);
38	  if (state.hearts > 0) return false;
39	
40	  state.isDead = true;
41	  state.respawnTimer = RESPAWN_SECONDS;
42	  return true;
43	}
44	
45	/**
46	 * Applies armor-bypassing damage that can never be lethal: hearts never drop
47	 * below `floorHp`. Used by Poison, which should chip a player down to half a
48	 * heart yet never deliver the killing blow. Returns true when any damage landed.
49	 */
50	export function applyNonLethalDamage(state: GameState, amount: number, floorHp = 1): boolean {
51	  if (state.isDead || !takesDamage(state.gameMode)) return false;
52	  const value = Math.max(0, Math.floor(amount));
53	  if (value <= 0 || state.hearts <= floorHp) return false;
54	  state.hearts = Math.max(floorHp, state.hearts - value);
55	  return true;
56	}
57	
58	/**
59	 * Counts down the respawn timer while dead. Returns true when the player
60	 * comes back to life this tick — the engine then performs the respawn.
61	 */
62	export function tickRespawnTimer(state: GameState, dt: number): boolean {
63	  if (!state.isDead) return false;
64	  state.respawnTimer -= dt;
65	  if (state.respawnTimer > 0) return false;
66	
67	  state.hearts = MAX_HEARTS;
68	  state.hunger = MAX_HUNGER;
69	  state.isDead = false;
70	  state.respawnTimer = 0;
71	  state.timers.waterExposureTimer = 0;
72	  state.timers.waterDamageTimer = 0;
73	  return true;
74	}

16	/**
17	 * Status-effect core. Effects live in `state.effects` (a Map of id → remaining
18	 * seconds) — session-state that persists across reload (save v6) but is cleared
19	 * on death. Each effect is read by exactly one seam: Speed multiplies movement
20	 * (`playerMotion`), Strength adds melee damage (`GameEngine` attack dispatch),
21	 * Fire Resistance / Water Breathing gate the lava / drowning ticks
22	 * (`playerStats`), and Regeneration / Poison are applied here on their own
23	 * accumulators each tick.
24	 */
25	
26	/** Stable HUD/iteration order for the effects readout. */
27	export const EFFECT_ORDER: readonly EffectId[] = [
28	  "speed",
29	  "strength",
30	  "haste",
31	  "resistance",
32	  "jump_boost",
33	  "regeneration",
34	  "fire_resistance",
35	  "water_breathing",
36	  "poison"
37	];
38	
39	export function hasEffect(state: GameState, id: EffectId): boolean {
40	  return (state.effects.get(id) ?? 0) > 0;
41	}
42	
43	export function effectRemaining(state: GameState, id: EffectId): number {
44	  return state.effects.get(id) ?? 0;
45	}
46	
47	/** Adds (or refreshes) an effect to at least `seconds` remaining — never shortens a longer one. */
48	export function addEffect(state: GameState, id: EffectId, seconds: number): void {
49	  if (seconds <= 0) return;
50	  state.effects.set(id, Math.max(state.effects.get(id) ?? 0, seconds));
51	}
52	
53	/** Drops every active effect and resets the periodic accumulators — used on death/respawn. */
54	export function clearEffects(state: GameState): void {
55	  state.effects.clear();
56	  state.timers.effectRegenTimer = 0;
57	  state.timers.effectPoisonTimer = 0;
58	}
59	
60	/** Movement-speed multiplier from the Speed effect (1 when inactive). */
61	export function speedMultiplier(state: GameState): number {
62	  return hasEffect(state, "speed") ? EFFECT_SPEED_MULTIPLIER : 1;
63	}
64	
65	/** Extra melee damage per hit from the Strength effect (0 when inactive). */
66	export function strengthBonus(state: GameState): number {
67	  return hasEffect(state, "strength") ? EFFECT_STRENGTH_BONUS : 0;
68	}
69	
70	/** Mining-speed multiplier from the Haste effect (1 when inactive). */
71	export function hasteMultiplier(state: GameState): number {
72	  return hasEffect(state, "haste") ? EFFECT_HASTE_MULTIPLIER : 1;
73	}
74	
75	/** Incoming armor-mitigated combat-damage multiplier from the Resistance effect (1 when inactive). */
76	export function resistanceMultiplier(state: GameState): number {
77	  return hasEffect(state, "resistance") ? EFFECT_RESISTANCE_MULTIPLIER : 1;
78	}
79	
80	/** Extra jump launch velocity from the Jump Boost effect (0 when inactive). */
81	export function jumpBoostBonus(state: GameState): number {
82	  return hasEffect(state, "jump_boost") ? EFFECT_JUMP_BOOST_VELOCITY : 0;
83	}
84	
85	export type StatusEffectDeps = {
86	  /** Armor-bypassing, never-lethal damage (poison) — emits playerHurt. */
87	  applyPoisonDamage: (amount: number) => void;
88	  emit: EmitGameEvent;
89	};
90	
91	/**
92	 * Advances every active effect by dt: counts each down (emitting `effectExpired`
93	 * at zero), then applies Regeneration (heals on its own cadence, even at low
94	 * hunger) and Poison (chips away but can't kill). Runs after `tickHealthRegen`
95	 * and before the environmental ticks so the fire-resist / water-breathing gates
96	 * are current when lava / oxygen read them.
97	 */
98	export function tickStatusEffects(state: GameState, dt: number, deps: StatusEffectDeps): void {
99	  for (const [id, remaining] of state.effects) {
100	    const next = remaining - dt;
101	    if (next <= 0) {
102	      state.effects.delete(id);
103	      deps.emit({ type: "effectExpired", effect: id });
104	    } else {
105	      state.effects.set(id, next);
106	    }
107	  }
108	
109	  // Regeneration: heal on an independent accumulator, ignoring the hunger gate.
110	  if (hasEffect(state, "regeneration")) {
111	    state.timers.effectRegenTimer += dt;
112	    while (state.timers.effectRegenTimer >= EFFECT_REGEN_INTERVAL) {
113	      state.timers.effectRegenTimer -= EFFECT_REGEN_INTERVAL;
114	      if (state.hearts < MAX_HEARTS) state.hearts = Math.min(MAX_HEARTS, state.hearts + EFFECT_REGEN_HP);
115	    }
116	  } else {
117	    state.timers.effectRegenTimer = 0;
118	  }
119	
120	  // Poison: never-lethal damage over time (the deps wrapper floors at half a heart).
121	  if (hasEffect(state, "poison")) {
122	    state.timers.effectPoisonTimer += dt;
123	    while (state.timers.effectPoisonTimer >= POISON_INTERVAL) {
124	      state.timers.effectPoisonTimer -= POISON_INTERVAL;
125	      deps.applyPoisonDamage(POISON_HP);
126	    }
127	  } else {
128	    state.timers.effectPoisonTimer = 0;
129	  }
130	}

1	import { XP_PER_LEVEL } from "@/lib/game/config";
2	import { mendXp } from "@/lib/game/enchantments";
3	import { BlockId } from "@/lib/world";
4	import type { EmitGameEvent, GameState } from "../state";
5	
6	/**
7	 * XP & levels. XP is banked as points in `state.xp`; `XP_PER_LEVEL` points make
8	 * one level. Levels are the currency spent at the enchanting table. XP accrues
9	 * from mob kills (`mobXp.ts`), ore mining (`ORE_XP` below), and fishing — and is
10	 * NOT cleared on death (unlike status effects), since it's a long-term currency.
11	 */
12	
13	/** XP granted for mining each ore block; everything else yields none. */
14	const ORE_XP: Partial<Record<BlockId, number>> = {
15	  [BlockId.CoalOre]: 1,
16	  [BlockId.SliverOre]: 2,
17	  [BlockId.RubyOre]: 4,
18	  [BlockId.GoldOre]: 4,
19	  [BlockId.SapphireOre]: 6,
20	  [BlockId.DiamondOre]: 8
21	};
22	
23	export function xpForBlock(block: BlockId): number {
24	  return ORE_XP[block] ?? 0;
25	}
26	
27	/** Whole level from banked XP points. */
28	export function xpLevel(xp: number): number {
29	  return Math.floor(xp / XP_PER_LEVEL);
30	}
31	
32	/** Progress toward the next level, 0..1. */
33	export function xpProgress(xp: number): number {
34	  return (xp % XP_PER_LEVEL) / XP_PER_LEVEL;
35	}
36	
37	/**
38	 * Banks XP points (a no-op for ≤ 0), emitting `xpGained` so the HUD and audio react.
39	 * Mending first diverts some of the gained XP to repair damaged held/worn gear; only
40	 * the remainder is banked, but the event reports the gross amount so the HUD/audio
41	 * still react to the full pickup.
42	 */
43	export function awardXp(state: GameState, amount: number, emit: EmitGameEvent): void {
44	  if (amount <= 0) return;
45	  const { slots, equipped, xpLeft } = mendXp(state.inventory, state.selectedSlot, state.equippedArmor, amount);
46	  if (slots !== state.inventory) state.inventory = slots;
47	  if (equipped !== state.equippedArmor) state.equippedArmor = equipped;
48	  state.xp += xpLeft;
49	  emit({ type: "xpGained", amount });
50	}
51	
52	/** Spends whole levels when affordable; returns true on success, false (unchanged) if too poor. */
53	export function spendXpLevels(state: GameState, levels: number): boolean {
54	  if (levels <= 0) return true;
55	  if (xpLevel(state.xp) < levels) return false;
56	  state.xp -= levels * XP_PER_LEVEL;
57	  return true;
58	}
59

function makeState(xp = 0, inventory: InventorySlot[] = [], selectedSlot = 0): GameState {
  return { xp, inventory, selectedSlot, equippedArmor: createEmptyArmorEquipment() } as unknown as GameState & PlayerState;
}

describe("xp levels & progress", () => {
  test("level is floor(points / XP_PER_LEVEL) and progress is the remainder fraction", () => {
    expect(xpLevel(0)).toBe(0);
    expect(xpLevel(XP_PER_LEVEL - 1)).toBe(0);
    expect(xpLevel(XP_PER_LEVEL)).toBe(1);
    expect(xpLevel(XP_PER_LEVEL * 3 + 4)).toBe(3);
    expect(xpProgress(0)).toBe(0);
    expect(xpProgress(XP_PER_LEVEL / 2)).toBeCloseTo(0.5, 5);
    expect(xpProgress(XP_PER_LEVEL)).toBe(0);
  });
});

38	export function tickHungerDrain(state: GameState, move: MoveTickResult): void {

72	export function tickHealthRegen(state: GameState, dt: number): void {

74	    state.hearts = MAX_HEARTS;

/** Advances starvation by `seconds` of game time in one call. */
function starve(state: GameState & PlayerState, seconds: number): void {
  tickStarvation(state, seconds, applyFloored(state), applyLethal(state));
}

describe("tickHealthRegen difficulty scaling", () => {
  test("Peaceful heals in half the time of the baseline interval", () => {
    const peaceful = makeState({ difficulty: "peaceful", hearts: 10, hunger: 20 });
    tickHealthRegen(peaceful, HEALTH_REGEN_INTERVAL_SECONDS * 0.5); // Peaceful's faster cadence
    expect(peaceful.hearts).toBe(11);

    // Normal needs the full interval — half of it isn't enough.
    const normal = makeState({ difficulty: "normal", hearts: 10, hunger: 20 });
    tickHealthRegen(normal, HEALTH_REGEN_INTERVAL_SECONDS * 0.5);
    expect(normal.hearts).toBe(10);
  });
--8<--
  test("fire resistance negates lava burn", () => {
    const state = makeState({ world: uniformWorld(BlockId.Lava) });
    let damage = 0;
    tickLavaExposure(state, 0.5, (a) => (damage += a), true);
    expect(damage).toBe(0);
    tickLavaExposure(state, 0.5, (a) => (damage += a), false);
    expect(damage).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test("water breathing keeps the lungs full and immune to drowning", () => {
    const state = makeState({ world: uniformWorld(BlockId.Water), oxygen: 0 });
    let damage = 0;
    tickOxygen(state, 1, (a) => (damage += a), true);
    expect(damage).toBe(0);
    expect(state.oxygen).toBe(MAX_OXYGEN);
    // Without the effect, an empty meter underwater drowns.
    state.oxygen = 0;
    tickOxygen(state, 1, (a) => (damage += a), false);
    expect(damage).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});

174	/** Places the selected block against the targeted face, refusing self-entombment. */
175	export function placeSelectedBlock(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): void {
176	  if (!canEditBlocks(state.gameMode)) return; // Adventure and Spectator can't place
177	  const { world } = state;
178	  const origin = eyePosition(state, scratchEye);
179	  const direction = lookDirection(state.player.yaw, state.player.pitch, scratchDir);
180	  const result = voxelRaycast(world, origin, direction, MINE_REACH);
181	  if (!result) return;
182	
183	  const tx = result.previous.x;
184	  const ty = result.previous.y;
185	  const tz = result.previous.z;
186	  if (!world.inBounds(tx, ty, tz)) return;
187	  const replacedBlock = world.get(tx, ty, tz);
188	  if (replacedBlock !== BlockId.Air && replacedBlock !== BlockId.Water) return;
189	
190	  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];
191	  if (!slot || !slot.id || slot.kind !== "block" || slot.count <= 0 || slot.blockId === undefined) return;
192	  if (slot.blockId === BlockId.Bedrock) return;
193	
194	  // Creative builds without spending the held stack (so no take, no refund).
195	  const consume = !freeBuild(state.gameMode);
196	  if (consume) {
197	    const afterTake = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, slot.id, -1, state.selectedSlot);
198	    if (!afterTake) return;
199	    state.inventory = afterTake;
200	  }
201	  let replacedUpper: BlockId | null = null;
202	  if (slot.id === "door") {
203	    const support = world.get(tx, ty - 1, tz);
204	    replacedUpper = world.get(tx, ty + 1, tz) as BlockId;
205	    if (ty + 1 >= world.sizeY || (replacedUpper !== BlockId.Air && replacedUpper !== BlockId.Water) || !world.isSolid(tx, ty - 1, tz) || isDoorBlock(support)) {
206	      if (consume) state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, slot.id, 1, state.selectedSlot) ?? state.inventory;
207	      return;
208	    }
209	    const facing = doorFacingFromYaw(state.player.yaw);
210	    state.blockChanges.set(tx, ty, tz, doorBlock(facing, false, false));
211	    state.blockChanges.set(tx, ty + 1, tz, doorBlock(facing, false, true));
212	  } else {
213	    state.blockChanges.set(tx, ty, tz, slot.blockId);
214	  }
215	  if (collidesAt(world, state.player.position, PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT)) {
216	    state.blockChanges.set(tx, ty, tz, replacedBlock as BlockId);
217	    if (replacedUpper !== null) state.blockChanges.set(tx, ty + 1, tz, replacedUpper);
218	    if (consume) state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, slot.id, 1, state.selectedSlot) ?? state.inventory;
219	    return;
220	  }
221	
222	  // A placed chest gets a fresh, empty block-entity store.
223	  if (slot.blockId === BlockId.Chest) {
224	    state.containers.set(
225	      world.index(tx, ty, tz),
226	      Array.from({ length: CHEST_SLOTS }, () => createEmptySlot())
227	    );
228	  }
229	
230	  state.worldMeshDirty = true;
231	  emit({ type: "blockPlaced", blockId: slot.blockId, x: tx, y: ty, z: tz });
232	}

```
 * `knockback` is the extra horizontal impulse from the Knockback enchantment (0 by
 * default); `lootingLevel` (the held weapon's Looting) is forwarded to the kill
 * callback so the drop roll uses the *killing* weapon, not whatever is held when a
 * delayed kill resolves — Looting is a melee enchant, so indirect kills pass 0.
 */
export function tryAttackMob(
  state: GameState,
  damage: number,
  onMobKilled: (index: number, lootingLevel?: number) => void,
  reach = ATTACK_REACH,
  knockback = 0,
  lootingLevel = 0
): MobKind | null {
  const { position } = player;
  const bestIndex = findAimedMobIndex(state, reach);
  if (bestIndex < 0) return null;
  const mob = state.mobs[bestIndex];
  mob.hp -= damage;

  scratchKnock.copy(mob.position).sub(position).setY(0);
  if (scratchKnock.lengthSq() > 0.0001) {
    scratchKnock.normalize();
    mob.direction.copy(scratchKnock);
    mob.position.addScaledVector(scratchKnock, MELEE_KNOCKBACK_IMPULSE + knockback);
    mob.position.y += 0.12;
  }

  if (mob.hp <= 0) onMobKilled(bestIndex, lootingLevel);
  return mob.kind;
}

export function tryFeedAimedMob(state: GameState, player: PlayerState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  const slot = player.inventory[player.selectedSlot];
  if (!slot?.id || slot.count <= 0) return false;
  const index = findAimedMobIndex(state);
  if (index < 0) return false;
  const mob = state.mobs[index];
  emit({ type: "petSitToggled", kind: mob.kind, sitting: mob.sitting === true });
  return true;
}

/** Opens the inventory in furnace mode so its smelting recipes unlock. */
function interactFurnace(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  player.inventoryOpen = true;
  player.craftingStation = "furnace";
  emit({ type: "openedStation", station: "furnace" });
  return true;
}

/** Opens the inventory in brewing mode so its potion recipes unlock. */
function interactBrewingStand(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  player.inventoryOpen = true;
  player.craftingStation = "brewing";
  emit({ type: "openedStation", station: "brewing" });
  return true;
}

/** Opens the inventory in enchanting mode so the enchanting panel unlocks. */
function interactEnchantingTable(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  player.inventoryOpen = true;
  player.craftingStation = "enchanting";
  emit({ type: "openedStation", station: "enchanting" });
  return true;
}

/** Opens the inventory in anvil mode so the repair/combine/rename panel unlocks. */
function interactAnvil(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  player.inventoryOpen = true;
  player.craftingStation = "anvil";
  emit({ type: "openedStation", station: "anvil" });
  return true;
}

/** Opens the inventory in grindstone mode so the disenchant panel unlocks. */
function interactGrindstone(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  player.inventoryOpen = true;
  player.craftingStation = "grindstone";
  emit({ type: "openedStation", station: "grindstone" });
  return true;
}

/**
 * Right-click a villager to open its trades (the inventory in "villager" station
 * mode, which unlocks the trade offers in the recipe book). Returns true when an
 * aimed villager consumed the click. Runs after feeding in the right-click
 * precedence, but villagers aren't breedable so the two never collide.
 */
export function tryTradeAimedVillager(state: GameState, player: PlayerState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  const index = findAimedMobIndex(state);
  const mob = index < 0 ? null : state.mobs[index];
  if (!mob || mob.kind !== "villager") return false;
  player.inventoryOpen = true;
  player.craftingStation = "villager";
  // The open villager's profession filters the Trading panel to its offers and
  // gates which trades the craft command will accept.
  player.activeVillagerProfession = mob.profession ?? null;
  emit({ type: "openedStation", station: "villager" });
  return true;

/** Sleep in a bed: only at night, only when no hostile is near. Sets the respawn point. */
function interactBed(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent, x: number, y: number, z: number): boolean {
  if (state.daylight >= SLEEP_ALLOWED_BELOW_DAYLIGHT) {
    emit({ type: "sleepDenied", reason: "daylight" });
    return true;
  }
  for (const mob of state.mobs) {
    if (mob.hostile && mob.position.distanceTo(player.position) <= SLEEP_HOSTILE_RADIUS) {
      emit({ type: "sleepDenied", reason: "hostiles" });
      return true;
    }
  }

  player.spawnPoint = { x, y, z };
  state.sleepTimer = SLEEP_FADE_SECONDS;
  emit({ type: "sleepStarted" });
  return true;
}

230	/**
231	 * An aquatic mob's whole tick — it swims in 3D and bypasses every land
232	 * assumption in the main loop (the surfaceYAt ground clamp, border bounce, and
233	 * the collidesAt foot test): each move is instead gated on the destination cell
234	 * being water, so a fish can never swim into land, air, or out of bounds. It
235	 * flees the player in 3D within FISH_FLEE_RANGE, wanders with a gentle pitch
236	 * otherwise, and out of water it lies beached, suffocating until it dies (or a
237	 * knockback returns it to water).
238	 */
239	function tickAquaticMob(state: GameState, mob: MobState, dt: number, deps: MobTickDeps): void {
240	  const { world } = state;
241	
242	  const inWater = world.get(Math.floor(mob.position.x), Math.floor(mob.position.y), Math.floor(mob.position.z)) === BlockId.Water;
243	  if (!inWater) {
244	    mob.moveSpeed = 0;
245	    mob.position.y = deps.surfaceYAt(mob.position.x, mob.position.z) + mob.halfHeight * 0.5;
246	    mob.hp -= FISH_SUFFOCATION_HP_PER_SECOND * dt;
247	    return;
248	  }
249	
250	  scratchToPlayer3D.copy(state.player.position).sub(mob.position);
251	  const distanceToPlayer = scratchToPlayer3D.length();
252	  let moveSpeed = mob.speed;
253	  if (distanceToPlayer < FISH_FLEE_RANGE) {
254	    if (distanceToPlayer > 0.001) mob.direction.lerp(scratchToPlayer3D.normalize().multiplyScalar(-1), 0.25).normalize();
255	    moveSpeed *= 1.6;
256	  } else if (mob.turnTimer <= 0) {
257	    const angle = deps.rng() * Math.PI * 2;
258	    const pitch = (deps.rng() - 0.5) * 0.7;
259	    mob.direction.set(Math.cos(angle) * Math.cos(pitch), Math.sin(pitch), Math.sin(angle) * Math.cos(pitch)).normalize();
260	    mob.turnTimer = 1.5 + deps.rng() * 3;
261	  }
262	  mob.moveSpeed = moveSpeed;
263	
264	  const nx = mob.position.x + mob.direction.x * moveSpeed * dt;
265	  const ny = mob.position.y + mob.direction.y * moveSpeed * dt;
266	  const nz = mob.position.z + mob.direction.z * moveSpeed * dt;
267	  const inBounds = nx >= 2 && nz >= 2 && nx <= world.sizeX - 2 && nz <= world.sizeZ - 2 && ny >= 1 && ny <= world.sizeY - 2;
268	  if (inBounds && world.get(Math.floor(nx), Math.floor(ny), Math.floor(nz)) === BlockId.Water) {
269	    mob.position.set(nx, ny, nz);
270	  } else {
271	    mob.direction.multiplyScalar(-1);
272	    mob.turnTimer = 1;
273	  }

278	  const { world, daylight, mobs, isDead } = state;
279	  const playerPosition = state.player.position;

283	  const threatened = mobsThreaten(state.gameMode);
284	  // Difficulty scales every hit a mob lands (melee + arrows): Easy 0.5×, Hard 1.5×.
285	  // Applied here at the strike, never by mutating the per-mob templates.
286	  const dmgScale = mobDamageMultiplier(state.difficulty);
287	
288	  for (let i = 0; i < mobs.length; i += 1) {

463	
464	    // The boss conjures minions while it is engaged with the player.
465	    if (!isDead && isBoss && activeHostile && distanceToPlayer < mob.detectRange) {
466	      tickBossSummon(state, mob, dt, deps);
467	    }
468	
469	    // A creeper lights its fuse when it gets close, then detonates — destroying
470	    // terrain and hurting the player and nearby mobs. Walk out of range while it
471	    // is primed and the fuse aborts. It dies in its own blast (dropping gunpowder
472	    // via the post-loop sweep); killing it before the fuse runs out cancels it.
473	    if (!isDead && mob.kind === "creeper") {
474	      if ((mob.fuseTimer ?? 0) > 0) {
475	        if (!activeHostile || distanceToPlayer > CREEPER_ABORT_RANGE) {
476	          mob.fuseTimer = 0;
477	        } else {
478	          mob.fuseTimer = (mob.fuseTimer ?? 0) - dt;
479	          if (mob.fuseTimer <= 0) {
480	            explode(state, mob.position.x, mob.position.y, mob.position.z, CREEPER_EXPLOSION_POWER, deps);
481	            mob.hp = 0;
482	          }
483	        }
484	      } else if (creeperFuseReady && hasLineOfSight) {
485	        mob.fuseTimer = CREEPER_FUSE_SECONDS;
486	        deps.emit({ type: "mobAttacked", kind: "creeper" }); // the hiss
487	      }
488	    }
489	
490	    // Zombies, skeletons, and creepers burn in broad daylight; the boss is immune.
491	    if (mob.hostile && mob.kind !== "spider" && mob.kind !== "boss" && daylight > HOSTILE_BURN_ABOVE_DAYLIGHT) {
492	      mob.hp -= dt * 0.8;
493	    }
494	  }
495	
496	  // Sweep the dead after the loop (descending, so splices don't shift live
497	  // indices). A post-loop sweep — not per-iteration — also catches mobs killed by
498	  // an explosion (or another mob) earlier in the same pass, including the creeper
499	  // that just blew up. Loot + XP go to the player only for credited factions, so a
500	  // pet's kill feeds you but a slain villager/pet yields nothing.
501	  for (let i = mobs.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
502	    const dead = mobs[i];
503	    if (dead.hp <= 0) deps.removeMobAt(i, 0, CREDITED_FACTIONS.has(dead.faction));
504	  }
505	}
506

Single-player: the\n * one player — exactly the old `state.player` reads.\n */\nexport function nearestPlayerTo(state: GameState, x: number, z: number): PlayerState | null {\n  let best: PlayerState | null = null;\n  let bestSq = Infinity;\n  for (const player of state.players.values()) {\n    const dx = player.position.x - x;\n    const dz = player.position.z - z;\n    const d = dx * dx + dz * dz;\n    if (d < bestSq) {\n      bestSq = d;\n      best = player;\n    }\n  }\n  return best;\n}\n\n/**\n * Nearest player hostiles may hunt — Creative/Spectator players aren't a\n * threat target (mobsThreaten), so they're skipped. import * as THREE from "three";
import { BlockId, doorState, isDoorBlock } from "@/lib/world";
import { EXPLOSION_DAMAGE_PER_POWER, TNT_CHAIN_FUSE_MAX_SECONDS, TNT_CHAIN_FUSE_MIN_SECONDS, TNT_EXPLOSION_POWER, TNT_FUSE_SECONDS } from "@/lib/game/config";
import type { EmitGameEvent, GameState } from "../state";

/**
 * Everything an explosion needs from the engine. A subset of `MobTickDeps`, so
 * the creeper branch in mobAI can pass its `deps` straight through.
 */
export type ExplosionDeps = {
  applyDamage: (amount: number) => void;
  rng: () => number;
  emit: EmitGameEvent;
};

/** Blocks the blast can never break (mirrors the mining unbreakables + worldgen hazards). */
function isBlastproof(block: BlockId): boolean {
  return block === BlockId.Bedrock || block === BlockId.Spawner || block === BlockId.Lava;
}

/** Higher = harder to destroy: the blast strength at a cell must exceed this to break it. */
function blastResistance(block: BlockId): number {
  switch (block) {
    case BlockId.Stone:
    case BlockId.Cobblestone:
    case BlockId.Brick:
    case BlockId.MossyCobblestone:
    case BlockId.Furnace:
    case BlockId.CoalOre:
    case BlockId.SliverOre:
        }
        changed = true;
      }
    }
  }
  if (changed) state.worldMeshDirty = true;

  const damageRange = power * 2;
  const peak = power * EXPLOSION_DAMAGE_PER_POWER;

  // Player: armor-aware damage + knockback away from the blast.
  const { player } = state;
  const pdist = Math.hypot(player.position.x - cx, player.position.y - cy, player.position.z - cz);
  if (pdist < damageRange) {
    const falloff = 1 - pdist / damageRange;
    deps.applyDamage(Math.max(1, Math.round(peak * falloff)));
    if (pdist > 0.001) {
      scratchKnock
        .set(player.position.x - cx, player.position.y - cy, player.position.z - cz)
        .normalize()
        .multiplyScalar(power * falloff);
      player.velocity.x += scratchKnock.x;
      player.velocity.z += scratchKnock.z;
      player.velocity.y = Math.max(player.velocity.y, Math.abs(scratchKnock.y) + 2);
    }
  }

16	/**

18	 * point on it closest to (px, py, pz), clamped to the segment endpoints.

20	function closestParam(ox: number, oy: number, oz: number, dx: number, dy: number, dz: number, len: number, px: number, py: number, pz: number): number {
21	  const t = (px - ox) * dx + (py - oy) * dy + (pz - oz) * dz;

31	/**
32	 * Advances every in-flight arrow. Each arrow integrates under gravity in capped
33	 * substeps so a fast shot can't skip a 1-block wall or a thin mob: per substep
34	 * it sweeps the world DDA for a block hit and tests the segment against the
35	 * relevant entity (mobs for player arrows, the player for mob arrows), resolving
36	 * whichever is nearer. Spent arrows (hit, expired, or out of bounds) despawn.
37	 */
38	export function tickProjectiles(state: GameState, dt: number, deps: ProjectileTickDeps): void {

function makeState(mobs: MobState[]): GameState {
  const world = new VoxelWorld(48, 48, 48, 1);
  return {
    world,
    blockChanges: createBlockChangeTracker(world),
    primedTnt: new Map<number, number>(),
    worldMeshDirty: false,
    gameMode: "survival", // hostiles only threaten survival/adventure players
    difficulty: "normal", // baseline 1× mob-damage multiplier
    mobs,
    projectiles: [],
    nextProjectileId: 1,
    daylight: 0.1, // night-ish so hostiles stay active and don't burn
    player: { position: new THREE.Vector3(24, 30, 24), velocity: new THREE.Vector3(), yaw: 0, pitch: 0, onGround: true }
  } as unknown as GameState;
}

function makeDeps() {
  const events: GameEvent[] = [];
  let damage = 0;
  const deps: MobTickDeps = {
    surfaceYAt: () => 29, // keeps mob.y ≈ player.y so the vertical gap stays small
    applyDamage: (a: number) => {
      damage += a;
    },
    removeMobAt: () => {},
    rng: () => 0.5,
    emit: (e: GameEvent) => events.push(e)
  };
  return { deps, events, getDamage: () => damage };
}

--8<--

function makeState(world: VoxelWorld, mobs: MobState[] = []): GameState {
  return {
    world,
    blockChanges: createBlockChangeTracker(world),
    player: { position: new THREE.Vector3(0, 64, 0), velocity: new THREE.Vector3(), yaw: 0, pitch: 0, onGround: true },
    mobs,
    primedTnt: new Map<number, number>(),
    worldMeshDirty: false,
    timers: createTimers()
  } as unknown as GameState;
}

function deps(events: GameEvent[], damages: number[]) {
  return {
    applyDamage: (amount: number) => damages.push(amount),
    rng: () => 0.5,
    emit: (e: GameEvent) => events.push(e)
  };
}

98	 * The day-one population around the player's spawn point. Passives scatter
99	 * over a wider ring than hostiles so the spawn area doesn't feel like a
100	 * petting zoo; hostiles stay closer (the dawn-aggro behavior tests document).
101	 */
102	export function spawnInitialMobs(state: GameState, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn): void {
103	  const centerX = state.player.position.x;
104	  const centerZ = state.player.position.z;
105	  const passiveRadius = RENDER_RADIUS * 1.2;
106	  const hostileRadius = RENDER_RADIUS * 0.7;
107	  const groups: Array<[MobKind, boolean, number, number]> = [
108	    ["sheep", false, 6, passiveRadius],
109	    ["chicken", false, 5, passiveRadius],
110	    ["horse", false, 3, passiveRadius],
111	    ["cow", false, 4, passiveRadius],
112	    ["pig", false, 4, passiveRadius],
113	    // Wild wolves and cats roam with the other animals (passive, flee the player)
114	    // until tamed with a bone / raw fish — without these they'd never appear and
115	    // companions would be unreachable.
116	    ["wolf", false, 4, passiveRadius],
117	    ["cat", false, 3, passiveRadius],
118	    // Villagers no longer scatter loosely — they live in generated villages now
119	    // (see spawnVillageResidents), so the world's villager population is its
120	    // settlements. A village-less world (e.g. all-ocean) simply has no villagers.
121	    ["zombie", true, 8, hostileRadius],
122	    ["skeleton", true, 6, hostileRadius],
123	    ["spider", true, 6, hostileRadius],
124	    ["creeper", true, 4, hostileRadius]
125	  ];
126	  // Peaceful spawns no hostiles at all — only the passive groups populate the world.
127	  const spawnHostiles = hostilesSpawn(state.difficulty);
128	  for (const [kind, hostile, count, radius] of groups) {
129	    if (hostile && !spawnHostiles) continue;
130	    // Hostiles keep a minimum standoff so nothing (notably a creeper) starts the
131	    // game point-blank; passives may roam right up to the spawn area.
132	    spawnMobGroup(state, { kind, hostile, count, centerX, centerZ, radius, minRadius: hostile ? HOSTILE_SPAWN_MIN_RADIUS : 0 }, rng, surfaceYAt);
133	  }
134	  // Fish school in whatever water lies near spawn; a landlocked spawn gets none
135	  // (the aquatic director repopulates oceans the player sails to later).
136	  spawnAquaticGroup(state, "cod", 6, centerX, centerZ, passiveRadius, rng);
137	  spawnAquaticGroup(state, "salmon", 4, centerX, centerZ, passiveRadius, rng);
138	}

150

164	 * of a populated world restores its residents instead, so they aren't doubled.
165	 */
166	export function spawnVillageResidents(state: GameState, sites: Array<{ x: number; z: number }>, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn): void {

180	export function assignVillagerProfessions(state: GameState): void {

export function tickSpawnerDirector(state: GameState, dt: number, rng: () => number, emit: EmitGameEvent): void {
  if (!hostilesSpawn(state.difficulty)) return; // Peaceful keeps even dungeon spawners inert
  if (state.dungeonSpawnerIndices.size === 0) return;
  state.timers.spawnerTimer += dt;
  if (state.timers.spawnerTimer < SPAWNER_INTERVAL_SECONDS) return;
  state.timers.spawnerTimer = 0;

  const cap = Math.round(HOSTILE_CAP * hostileCapScale(state.difficulty));
  const countHostiles = () => state.mobs.reduce((acc, mob) => acc + (mob.hostile ? 1 : 0), 0);
  if (countHostiles() >= cap) return;

  const { player, world } = state;
  const layer = world.sizeX * world.sizeZ;
  for (const idx of state.dungeonSpawnerIndices) {
    const sy = Math.floor(idx / layer);
    const rem = idx - sy * layer;
    const sz = Math.floor(rem / world.sizeX);
    const sx = rem - sz * world.sizeX;
    if (world.get(sx, sy, sz) !== BlockId.Spawner) continue; // mined out → inert
    if (Math.hypot(player.position.x - (sx + 0.5), player.position.y - (sy + 0.5), player.position.z - (sz + 0.5)) > SPAWNER_ACTIVATION_RADIUS) continue;
    if (countHostiles() >= cap) break;

    const nearby = state.mobs.reduce(
      (acc, mob) => acc + (mob.hostile && Math.hypot(mob.position.x - (sx + 0.5), mob.position.z - (sz + 0.5)) <= SPAWNER_ACTIVATION_RADIUS ? 1 : 0),
      0
    );
    if (nearby >= SPAWNER_LOCAL_CAP) continue;

    const kind = SPAWNER_KINDS[Math.floor(rng() * SPAWNER_KINDS.length)];
    const jx = sx + 0.5 + (rng() * 2 - 1) * 1.2;
    const jz = sz + 0.5 + (rng() * 2 - 1) * 1.2;
    pushMob(state, kind, true, jx, sy, jz, rng);
    emit({ type: "mobSpawned", kind, x: sx + 0.5, y: sy + 0.5, z: sz + 0.5 });
  }
}

  "new_string": "/**\n * The player a spawn wave centers on. One player: that player, with no rng\n * consumed — the single-player stream stays byte-identical to the old code.\n * Several players: a uniformly random one per wave, so spawns spread across\n * the party instead of piling onto whoever is primary. None: null (idle room).\n */\nfunction spawnCenterPlayer(state: GameState, rng: () => number): PlayerState | null {\n  if (state.players.size === 0) return null;\n  if (state.players.size === 1) return state.players.values().next().value ?? null;\n  const all = [...state.players.values()];\n  return all[Math.min(all.length - 1, Math.floor(rng() * all.length))];\n}\n\n/**\n * Scales a global mob cap with the party size: 1–2 players keep the SP cap,\n * and each further pair adds another cap's worth — so 8 players don't starve\n * for mobs, but also don't each drag in a full private horde.\n */\nfunction partyCapScale(state: GameState): number {\n  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil(state.players.size / 2));\n}\n\n/** Trickles hostile mobs in around the player at night, up to the cap. Difficulty scales the cadence and cap; Peaceful spawns none. */\nexport function tickHostileSpawnDirector(state: GameState, dt: number, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn): void {\n  if (!hostilesSpawn(state.difficulty)) return;\n  state.timers.hostileSpawnTimer += dt;\n  const interval = HOSTILE_SPAWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS * hostileSpawnIntervalScale(state.difficulty);\n  if (state.daylight >= HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT || state.timers.hostileSpawnTimer < interval) return;\n  state.timers.hostileSpawnTimer = 0;\n\n  const cap = Math.round(HOSTILE_CAP * hostileCapScale(state.difficulty)) * partyCapScale(state);\n  const livingHostiles = state.mobs.filter((mob) => mob.hostile).length;\n  if (livingHostiles >= cap) return;\n\n  const center = spawnCenterPlayer(state, rng);\n  if (!center) return;\n  const spawnKinds: Array<\"zombie\" | \"skeleton\" | \"spider\" | \"creeper\"> = [\"zombie\", \"skeleton\", \"spider\", \"creeper\"];\n  const kind = spawnKinds[Math.floor(rng() * spawnKinds.length)];\n  // A wave is 1–2 mobs, but never more than the slots left under the cap — so a\n  // 2-pack rolled at cap-1 can't overshoot (especially Easy's tighter cap of 8).\n  spawnMobGroup(\n    state,\n    {\n      kind,\n      hostile: true,\n      count: Math.min(cap - livingHostiles, 1 + (rng() > 0.7 ? 1 : 0)),\n      centerX: center.position.x,\n      centerZ: center.position.z,\n      radius: Math.max(26, RENDER_RADIUS * 0.85),\n      minRadius: HOSTILE_SPAWN_MIN_RADIUS\n    },\n    rng,\n    surfaceYAt\n  );\n}"

  mountVehicle(state, player, vehicle);

export function tickVehicles(state: GameState, player: PlayerState, input: FrameInput, dt: number): void {
  const mounted = player.mountedVehicleId === null ? null : (state.vehicles.find((vehicle) => vehicle.id === player.mountedVehicleId) ?? null);
  if (mounted) {
    if (input.move.crouch && dismountVehicle(state, player, player, mounted)) return;
    const forwardInput = (input.move.forward ? 1 : 0) - (input.move.back ? 1 : 0);
    const turnInput = (input.move.right ? 1 : 0) - (input.move.left ? 1 : 0);
    mounted.yaw -= turnInput * VEHICLE_TURN_RATE * dt;

  "new_string": "export function tickRandomBlocks(state: GameState, dt: number, rng: () => number): void {\n  state.timers.randomTickTimer += dt;\n  if (state.timers.randomTickTimer < RANDOM_TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS) return;\n  state.timers.randomTickTimer = 0;\n\n  const { world } = state;\n  if (state.players.size === 0) return; // an idle server room grows nothing\n  // The sample budget splits across players (each interval stays constant-cost),\n  // so crops grow around everyone. Single-player: the full budget around the\n  // one player — exactly the old behavior, same rng stream.\n  const players = [...state.players.values()];\n  const perPlayer = Math.max(1, Math.floor(RANDOM_TICK_SAMPLES / players.length));\n  for (const player of players) {\n    const px = Math.floor(player.position.x);\n    const pz = Math.floor(player.position.z);\n    for (let i = 0; i < perPlayer; i += 1) {\n      const x = px + Math.floor((rng() * 2 - 1) * RANDOM_TICK_RADIUS);\n      const z = pz + Math.floor((rng() * 2 - 1) * RANDOM_TICK_RADIUS);\n      if (!world.inBounds(x, 0, z)) continue;\n      const y = world.highestSolidY(x, z);\n      const handler = RANDOM_TICK_HANDLERS[world.get(x, y, z) as BlockId];\n      if (handler) handler(state, x, y, z, rng);\n    }\n  }\n}"

326	export type SaveDataV14 = Omit<SaveDataV13, "version"> & {

332	 * Current save shape (v15): villager professions. A persisted villager resident

335	 * professionless (the engine assigns one).

339	 * version, the original version isn't recoverable on load — this flag is what lets
340	 * the engine tell a genuine v15 save (villagers are authoritative; an emptied
341	 * village stays empty) from a fresh world or a pre-village upgrade (which still
342	 * need their residents seeded).
343	 */
344	export type SaveDataV15 = Omit<SaveDataV14, "version"> & {

The live rider\n * link is session-only; saves carry only the placed entity's kind and pose.\n */\nexport type SaveDataV16 = Omit<SaveDataV15, \"version\"> & {\n  version: 16;\n  vehicles?: SavedVehicle[];\n};\n\n/**\n * One persisted player (v17).
