1	import * as THREE from "three";
2	import { GameEngine } from "@/lib/game/engine/GameEngine";
3	import type { Command } from "@/lib/game/engine/commands";
4	import { createIdleInput, type GameEvent, type MobState, type PlayerId } from "@/lib/game/engine/state";
5	import { TICK_SECONDS } from "@/lib/game/engine/tickDriver";
6	import { restoreEffects, restoreEquippedArmor, restoreInventorySlots, restoreSelectedSlot } from "@/lib/game/save";
7	import { MOB_TEMPLATES, mobHalfHeight } from "@/lib/game/mobs";
8	import { FACTION_BY_KIND } from "@/lib/game/mobs";
9	import type { MobKind } from "@/lib/game/types";
10	import { createClockSync } from "./clock";
11	import { decodeServerFrame, encodeClientMessage, gunzipWorldSync } from "./codec";
12	import { createPoseBuffer, INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MS, type PoseBuffer } from "./interpolation";
13	import { PROTOCOL_VERSION, type MobPose, type SelfDelta, type ServerMessage, type WorldSync } from "./protocol";
14	
15	/**
16	 * The client end of a multiplayer world: owns the WebSocket and a REPLICA
17	 * engine the existing renderer/audio/HUD consume unchanged. Outbound, it
18	 * streams the local player's pose at tick rate and routes commands — local
19	 * presentation stays on the replica, gameplay goes to the server (selectSlot
20	 * optimistically does both). Inbound, it applies the server's block journal,
21	 * replays events into the shell's existing event drain, feeds pose buffers
22	 * for ~125 ms-delayed interpolation, and overwrites the local player's
23	 * private state from self-deltas (the server owns your vitals).
24	 */
25	
26	export type NetStatus = "connecting" | "syncing" | "online" | "closed";
27	
28	export type NetworkSessionCallbacks = {
29	  onStatus?(status: NetStatus, detail?: string): void;
30	  onChat?(entry: { from: string; name: string; text: string }): void;
31	  /** Server events the shell's drain should also see (toasts, audio, particles). */
32	  onEvent?(event: GameEvent): void;
33	};
34	
35	/** Commands that never leave the client: pure presentation on the replica. */
36	const LOCAL_COMMANDS = new Set<Command["type"]>(["toggleInventory", "toggleAdvancements", "toggleDebug", "toggleCameraView", "pause", "resume"]);
37	
38	export type NetworkSession = {
39	  readonly engine: GameEngine;
40	  readonly playerId: PlayerId;
41	  /** UI subscriptions (React components mount after connect; unsubscribe on cleanup). */
42	  subscribeChat(listener: (entry: { from: string; name: string; text: string }) => void): () => void;
43	  subscribeStatus(listener: (status: NetStatus) => void): () => void;
44	  status(): NetStatus;
45	  rttMs(): number;
46	  /** Names for remote player ids (name tags, chat). */
47	  playerName(id: PlayerId): string;
48	  dispatch(command: Command): void;
49	  applyLook(deltaYaw: number, deltaPitch: number): void;
50	  sendChat(text: string): void;
51	  /** Server events since the last drain — feed the shell's existing event handler. */
52	  drainEvents(): GameEvent[];
53	  /** Call once per rAF after engine.step: flushes the pose stream and samples interpolation. */
54	  afterFrame(nowMs: number): void;
55	  dispose(): void;
56	};
57	
58	export async function connectNetworkSession(
59	  url: string,
60	  ticket: string,
61	  callbacks: NetworkSessionCallbacks = {},
62	  makeSocket: (url: string) => WebSocket = (u) => new WebSocket(u)
63	): Promise<NetworkSession> {
64	  const ws = makeSocket(`${url.replace(/\/$/, "")}/ws`);
65	  ws.binaryType = "arraybuffer";
66	  let status: NetStatus = "connecting";
67	  const chatListeners = new Set<(entry: { from: string; name: string; text: string }) => void>();
68	  const statusListeners = new Set<(status: NetStatus) => void>();
69	  const setStatus = (next: NetStatus, detail?: string) => {
70	    status = next;
71	    callbacks.onStatus?.(next, detail);
72	    for (const listener of statusListeners) listener(next);
73	  };
74	
75	  const clock = createClockSync();
76	  const pendingEvents: GameEvent[] = [];
77	  const playerBuffers = new Map<string, PoseBuffer>();
78	  const mobBuffers = new Map<number, PoseBuffer>();
79	  const names = new Map<string, string>();
80	
81	  // ── handshake: hello → welcome → binary world sync ─────────────────────────
82	  const welcome = await new Promise<Extract<ServerMessage, { t: "welcome" }>>((resolve, reject) => {
83	    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error("join timed out")), 15000);
84	    ws.onerror = () => reject(new Error("connection failed"));
85	    ws.onclose = (event) => reject(new Error(`refused: ${event.code} ${event.reason}`));
86	    ws.onopen = () => ws.send(encodeClientMessage({ t: "hello", ticket, protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION }));
87	    ws.onmessage = (event) => {
88	      const message = decodeServerFrame(event.data);
89	      if (message?.t === "welcome") {
90	        clearTimeout(timer);
91	        resolve(message);
92	      }
93	    };
94	  });
95	  setStatus("syncing");
96	
97	  // The replica: an empty mirror world generated from the server's seed.
98	  const engine = new GameEngine({
99	    seed: welcome.seed,
100	    worldType: welcome.worldType as never,
101	    difficulty: welcome.difficulty as never,
102	    hardcore: welcome.hardcore,
103	    authority: "local",
104	    replica: true,
105	    bootPlayer: false
106	  });
107	  const state = engine.state;
108	  state.dayClock = welcome.dayClock;
109	  state.primaryPlayerId = welcome.playerId;
110	  const self = engine.addPlayer({ id: welcome.playerId });
111	  self.input = createIdleInput();
112	  engine.consumeEvents(); // drop the join echo
113	  for (const entry of welcome.players) names.set(entry.id, entry.name);
114	  const myRoster = welcome.players.find((entry) => entry.id === welcome.playerId);
115	  if (myRoster) self.position.set(myRoster.x, myRoster.y, myRoster.z);
116	
117	  // Every dispatch from the UI/input controller routes here (see
118	  // GameEngine.routeDispatch): presentation stays local, gameplay goes up.
119	  engine.routeDispatch = (command) => {
120	    if (LOCAL_COMMANDS.has(command.type)) {
121	      engine.dispatch(command, welcome.playerId);
122	      return;
123	    }
124	    if (command.type === "selectSlot") engine.dispatch(command, welcome.playerId); // optimistic
125	    if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) sendCmd(command);
126	  };
127	
128	  const upsertRemotePlayer = (id: string, name: string) => {
129	    if (id === welcome.playerId || state.players.has(id)) return;
130	    engine.addPlayer({ id });
131	    engine.consumeEvents();
132	    names.set(id, name);
133	  };
134	  for (const entry of welcome.players) upsertRemotePlayer(entry.id, entry.name);
135	
136	  const applyWorldSync = (sync: WorldSync) => {
137	    state.blockChanges.applySavedChanges(sync.changes);
138	    state.worldMeshDirty = true;
139	    state.dayClock = sync.dayClock;
140	    state.containers.clear();
141	    for (const entry of sync.blockEntities) {
142	      const restored = restoreInventorySlots({ id: "container", inventorySlots: entry.slots });
143	      if (restored) state.containers.set(entry.index, restored);
144	    }
145	    state.lootedWorldgenChests = new Set(sync.lootedChests);
146	    state.mobs = [];
147	    mobBuffers.clear();
148	    for (const pose of sync.liveMobs) upsertReplicaMob(pose);
149	    for (const entry of sync.players) upsertRemotePlayer(entry.id, entry.name);
150	  };
151	
152	  function upsertReplicaMob(pose: MobPose): MobState {
153	    let mob = state.mobs.find((m) => m.id === pose.id);
154	    if (!mob) {
155	      const kind = (MOB_TEMPLATES[pose.kind as MobKind] ? pose.kind : "zombie") as MobKind;
156	      const template = MOB_TEMPLATES[kind];
157	      mob = {
158	        id: pose.id,
159	        kind,
160	        hostile: pose.hostile,
161	        faction: FACTION_BY_KIND[kind],
162	        targetId: null,
163	        retargetTimer: 0,
164	        hp: pose.hp,
165	        position: new THREE.Vector3(pose.x, pose.y, pose.z),
166	        direction: new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0),
167	        yaw: pose.yaw,
168	        turnTimer: 0,
169	        speed: template.speed,
170	        moveSpeed: pose.moveSpeed,
171	        detectRange: template.detectRange,
172	        attackDamage: 0,
173	        attackCooldown: 1,
174	        attackTimer: 0,
175	        halfHeight: mobHalfHeight(kind),
176	        bobSeed: pose.id * 0.7,
177	        fedTimer: 0,
178	        ageTimer: 0
179	      };
180	      state.mobs.push(mob);
181	    }
182	    mob.hp = pose.hp;
183	    mob.moveSpeed = pose.moveSpeed;
184	    let buffer = mobBuffers.get(pose.id);
185	    if (!buffer) {
186	      buffer = createPoseBuffer();
187	      mobBuffers.set(pose.id, buffer);
188	    }
189	    return mob;
190	  }
191	
192	  const applySelfDelta = (delta: SelfDelta) => {
193	    const shim = { id: self.id, ...delta };
194	    if (delta.inventorySlots) self.inventory = restoreInventorySlots(shim) ?? self.inventory;
195	    if (delta.equippedArmor) self.equippedArmor = restoreEquippedArmor(shim) ?? self.equippedArmor;
196	    if (delta.selectedSlot !== undefined) self.selectedSlot = restoreSelectedSlot(shim) ?? self.selectedSlot;
197	    if (delta.hearts !== undefined) self.hearts = delta.hearts;
198	    if (delta.hunger !== undefined) self.hunger = delta.hunger;
199	    if (delta.oxygen !== undefined) self.oxygen = delta.oxygen;
200	    if (delta.xp !== undefined) self.xp = delta.xp;
201	    if (delta.isDead !== undefined) self.isDead = delta.isDead;
202	    if (delta.respawnSeconds !== undefined) self.respawnTimer = delta.respawnSeconds;
203	    if (delta.gameMode !== undefined) self.gameMode = delta.gameMode as never;
204	    if (delta.sleeping !== undefined) self.sleeping = delta.sleeping;
205	    if (delta.effects) {
206	      self.effects.clear();
207	      for (const { id, remaining } of restoreEffects(shim)) self.effects.set(id, remaining);
208	    }
209	  };
210	
211	  const applyBlocks = (blocks: Array<[number, number]>) => {
212	    const layer = state.world.sizeX * state.world.sizeZ;
213	    for (const [idx, block] of blocks) {
214	      const y = Math.floor(idx / layer);
215	      const rem = idx - y * layer;
216	      const z = Math.floor(rem / state.world.sizeX);
217	      const x = rem - z * state.world.sizeX;
218	      state.blockChanges.set(x, y, z, block as never); // relights locally too
219	    }
220	    if (blocks.length > 0) state.worldMeshDirty = true;
221	  };
222	
223	  let serverTickTimeMs = welcome.tick * TICK_SECONDS * 1000;
224	
225	  ws.onclose = (event) => setStatus("closed", `${event.code} ${event.reason}`);
226	  ws.onerror = () => setStatus("closed", "socket error");
227	  ws.onmessage = async (event) => {
228	    if (typeof event.data !== "string") {
229	      const sync = await gunzipWorldSync(new Uint8Array(event.data as ArrayBuffer));
230	      if (sync) {
231	        applyWorldSync(sync);
232	        setStatus("online");
233	      }
234	      return;
235	    }
236	    const message = decodeServerFrame(event.data);
237	    if (!message) return;
238	    switch (message.t) {
239	      case "tick": {
240	        serverTickTimeMs = message.n * TICK_SECONDS * 1000;
241	        if (message.blocks) applyBlocks(message.blocks);
242	        if (message.day !== undefined) state.dayClock = message.day;
243	        if (message.self) applySelfDelta(message.self);
244	        for (const pose of message.pp) {
245	          upsertRemotePlayer(pose.id, names.get(pose.id) ?? "player");
246	          let buffer = playerBuffers.get(pose.id);
247	          if (!buffer) {
248	            buffer = createPoseBuffer();
249	            playerBuffers.set(pose.id, buffer);
250	          }
251	          buffer.push({ tMs: serverTickTimeMs, ...pose });
252	        }
253	        for (const pose of message.mp) {
254	          upsertReplicaMob(pose);
255	          mobBuffers.get(pose.id)?.push({ tMs: serverTickTimeMs, x: pose.x, y: pose.y, z: pose.z, yaw: pose.yaw });
256	        }
257	        for (const gameEvent of message.ev) {
258	          pendingEvents.push(gameEvent as GameEvent);
259	          callbacks.onEvent?.(gameEvent as GameEvent);
260	        }
261	        return;
262	      }
263	      case "mobsKeyframe": {
264	        const alive = new Set(message.mobs.map((m) => m.id));
265	        state.mobs = state.mobs.filter((m) => alive.has(m.id));
266	        for (const id of [...mobBuffers.keys()]) if (!alive.has(id)) mobBuffers.delete(id);
267	        const tMs = message.n * TICK_SECONDS * 1000;
268	        for (const pose of message.mobs) {
269	          upsertReplicaMob(pose);
270	          mobBuffers.get(pose.id)?.push({ tMs, x: pose.x, y: pose.y, z: pose.z, yaw: pose.yaw });
271	        }
272	        return;
273	      }
274	      case "playerJoined": {
275	        upsertRemotePlayer(message.player.id, message.player.name);
276	        const joined = state.players.get(message.player.id);
277	        joined?.position.set(message.player.x, message.player.y, message.player.z);
278	        return;
279	      }
280	      case "playerLeft": {
281	        if (message.id !== welcome.playerId) engine.removePlayer(message.id);
282	        playerBuffers.delete(message.id);
283	        engine.consumeEvents();
284	        return;
285	      }
286	      case "container": {
287	        const restored = restoreInventorySlots({ id: "container", inventorySlots: message.slots });
288	        if (restored) state.containers.set(message.index, restored);
289	        return;
290	      }
291	      case "chat":
292	        callbacks.onChat?.(message);
293	        for (const listener of chatListeners) listener(message);
294	        return;
295	      case "pong":
296	        clock.onPong(message.tMs, performance.now(), message.serverTick);
297	        return;
298	      case "forcePose":
299	        self.position.set(message.x, message.y, message.z);
300	        self.velocity.set(0, 0, 0);
301	        return;
302	      case "welcome":
303	        return;
304	    }
305	  };
306	
307	  // ── outbound ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
308	  let seq = 0;
309	  let lastPoseSentMs = 0;
310	  let lastPingMs = 0;
311	
312	  const sendCmd = (command: Command) => {
313	    seq += 1;
314	    ws.send(
315	      encodeClientMessage({
316	        t: "cmd",
317	        seq,
318	        cmd: command,
319	        pose: { x: self.position.x, y: self.position.y + 1.62, z: self.position.z, yaw: self.yaw, pitch: self.pitch }
320	      })
321	    );
322	  };
323	
324	  const session: NetworkSession = {
325	    engine,
326	    playerId: welcome.playerId,
327	    subscribeChat(listener) {
328	      chatListeners.add(listener);
329	      return () => chatListeners.delete(listener);
330	    },
331	    subscribeStatus(listener) {
332	      statusListeners.add(listener);
333	      return () => statusListeners.delete(listener);
334	    },
335	    drainEvents: () => pendingEvents.splice(0, pendingEvents.length),
336	    status: () => status,
337	    rttMs: () => clock.rttMs(),
338	    playerName: (id) => names.get(id) ?? "player",
339	
340	    dispatch(command) {
341	      engine.dispatch(command); // routeDispatch handles the local/network split
342	    },
343	
344	    applyLook(deltaYaw, deltaPitch) {
345	      engine.applyLook(deltaYaw, deltaPitch);
346	    },
347	
348	    sendChat(text) {
349	      if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN && text.trim()) ws.send(encodeClientMessage({ t: "chat", text: text.slice(0, 256) }));
350	    },
351	
352	    afterFrame(nowMs) {
353	      // Pose stream at tick rate.
354	      if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN && nowMs - lastPoseSentMs >= TICK_SECONDS * 1000) {
355	        lastPoseSentMs = nowMs;
356	        seq += 1;
357	        ws.send(
358	          encodeClientMessage({
359	            t: "pose",
360	            seq,
361	            x: self.position.x,
362	            y: self.position.y,
363	            z: self.position.z,
364	            yaw: self.yaw,
365	            pitch: self.pitch,
366	            onGround: self.onGround,
367	            move: self.input.move,
368	            mineHeld: self.input.mineHeld
369	          })
370	        );
371	      }
372	      if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN && nowMs - lastPingMs >= 2000) {
373	        lastPingMs = nowMs;
374	        ws.send(encodeClientMessage({ t: "ping", id: seq, tMs: nowMs }));
375	      }
376	      // Interpolation: remote entities render ~125ms in the past.
377	      const renderTime = (clock.ready() ? clock.estimatedServerTimeMs(nowMs) : serverTickTimeMs) - INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MS;
378	      for (const [id, buffer] of playerBuffers) {
379	        const player = state.players.get(id);
380	        const pose = buffer.sample(renderTime);
381	        if (player && pose) {
382	          player.position.set(pose.x, pose.y, pose.z);
383	          player.yaw = pose.yaw;
384	          player.pitch = pose.pitch;
385	        }
386	      }
387	      for (const [id, buffer] of mobBuffers) {
388	        const mob = state.mobs.find((m) => m.id === id);
389	        const pose = buffer.sample(renderTime);
390	        if (mob && pose) {
391	          mob.position.set(pose.x, pose.y, pose.z);
392	          mob.yaw = pose.yaw;
393	        }
394	      }
395	    },
396	
397	    dispose() {
398	      setStatus("closed", "left world");
399	      try {
400	        ws.close(1000, "leaving");
401	      } catch {
402	        /* already closed */
403	      }
404	    }
405	  };
406	  return session;
407	}

import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { db } from "@/db";
import { failureResponse, sessionUser, unauthorized } from "@/lib/online/http";
import { createWorld, listWorlds, type CreateWorldInput } from "@/lib/online/worldsService";

/** GET /api/worlds — every world the signed-in user may play. */
export async function GET(request: Request) {
  const user = await sessionUser(request);
  if (!user) return unauthorized();
  return NextResponse.json({ worlds: await listWorlds(db(), user.id) });
}

/** POST /api/worlds — create a world (sp-cloud or mp); the creator becomes owner. */
export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const user = await sessionUser(request);
  if (!user) return unauthorized();
  const body = (await request.json().catch(() => null)) as CreateWorldInput | null;
  if (!body) return failureResponse("invalid");
  const result = await createWorld(db(), user.id, body);
  if (!result.ok) return failureResponse(result.error);
  return NextResponse.json({ world: result.world }, { status: 201 });
}

6	/**
7	 * Multiplayer chat: a fading bottom-left log plus an input that opens on
8	 * T/Enter (releasing pointer lock while typing) and closes on Escape/send.
9	 * Rendered only for online sessions — single-player has nobody to talk to.
10	 */
11	
12	type ChatEntry = { id: number; name: string; text: string; atMs: number };
13	const LOG_LIMIT = 8;
14	const FADE_AFTER_MS = 8000;
15	
16	export default function ChatPanel({ session, locked, onOpenChange }: { session: NetworkSession; locked: boolean; onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void }) {
17	  const [entries, setEntries] = useState<ChatEntry[]>([]);
18	  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
19	  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
20	  // Render-time clock (the compiler forbids impure reads in render): advanced
21	  // by the fade interval and on each arrival.
22	  const [nowMs, setNowMs] = useState(0);
23	  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
24	  const nextIdRef = useRef(1);
25	
26	  // Subscribe to incoming chat (the session survives re-renders; effect per session).
27	  useEffect(() => {
28	    return session.subscribeChat((entry) => {
29	      // Mint the id OUTSIDE the updater — setState updaters must stay pure.
30	      const id = nextIdRef.current;
31	      nextIdRef.current += 1;
32	      const item = { id, name: entry.name, text: entry.text, atMs: performance.now() };
33	      setEntries((current) => [...current, item].slice(-LOG_LIMIT));
34	      setNowMs(performance.now());
35	    });
36	  }, [session]);
37	
38	  // Entries fade out; advance the render clock at 1 Hz while any are visible.
39	  useEffect(() => {
40	    if (entries.length === 0) return;
41	    const timer = window.setInterval(() => setNowMs(performance.now()), 1000);
42	    return () => window.clearInterval(timer);
43	  }, [entries.length]);
44	
45	  const openChat = useCallback(() => {
46	    setOpen(true);
47	    onOpenChange?.(true);
48	    if (document.pointerLockElement) document.exitPointerLock();
49	    // Focus after the input exists.
50	    window.setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.focus(), 0);
51	  }, [onOpenChange]);
52	
53	  const closeChat = useCallback(() => {
54	    setOpen(false);
55	    setDraft("");
56	    onOpenChange?.(false);
57	  }, [onOpenChange]);
58	
59	  // T / Enter opens while playing (not while another overlay owns the keys).
60	  useEffect(() => {
61	    const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
62	      if (open) return;
63	      if (!locked) return; // only from live gameplay — menus own their keys
64	      if (event.code === "KeyT" || event.code === "Enter") {
65	        event.preventDefault();
66	        openChat();
67	      }
68	    };
69	    document.addEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
70	    return () => document.removeEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
71	  }, [open, locked, openChat]);
72	
73	  const visible = open ? entries : entries.filter((entry) => nowMs - entry.atMs < FADE_AFTER_MS);
74	
75	  return (
76	    <div className={open ? "chat-panel open" : "chat-panel"}>
77	      <ul className="chat-log" aria-live="polite">
78	        {visible.map((entry) => (
79	          <li key={entry.id} className="chat-line">
80	            <span className="chat-name">{entry.name}</span> {entry.text}
81	          </li>
82	        ))}
83	      </ul>
84	      {open && (
85	        <form
86	          className="chat-input-row"
87	          onSubmit={(event) => {
88	            event.preventDefault();
89	            session.sendChat(draft);
90	            closeChat();
91	          }}
92	        >
93	          <input
94	            ref={inputRef}
95	            className="chat-input"
96	            value={draft}
97	            maxLength={256}
98	            placeholder="Say something…"
99	            onChange={(event) => setDraft(event.target.value)}
100	            onKeyDown={(event) => {
101	              if (event.key === "Escape") {
102	                event.preventDefault();
103	                closeChat();
104	              }
105	              event.stopPropagation(); // typing must not move the player
106	            }}
107	          />
108	        </form>
109	      )}
110	    </div>
111	  );

94	/**
95	 * One mounted game = one world played by one profile. The owning shell remounts
96	 * this hook (via a React `key` on the world id) to switch worlds, so the
97	 * per-world save key and the profile are fixed for the hook's lifetime.
98	 */
99	export type UseMinecraftGameOptions = {
100	  world: WorldMeta;
101	  profile: Profile;
102	  /**
103	   * A connected multiplayer session: its replica engine is mounted instead of
104	   * constructing one, dispatch routes through it (GameEngine.routeDispatch),
105	   * localStorage persistence is skipped (the server owns the world), and its
106	   * pose stream flushes each frame. Absent = classic offline single-player.
107	   */
108	  online?: NetworkSession;
109	  /** Leave this world and return to the world list (the shell unmounts us). */
110	  onQuitToWorlds: () => void;
111	  /** Re-read this world from disk by forcing a fresh mount (used by Load/Reset). */
112	  onReloadWorld: () => void;
113	};
114	
115	export function useMinecraftGame(opts: UseMinecraftGameOptions) {
116	  // The owning shell keys this hook by world id, so the world is fixed for the
117	  // mount's life; capturing it once in refs lets the long-lived rAF/autosave
118	  // effect read the save key and seed without re-subscribing.
119	  const saveKeyRef = useRef(worldSaveKey(opts.world.id));

  "content": "import { expect, test, type Page } from \"@playwright/test\";\nimport { acquirePointerLock } from \"./helpers\";\n\n/**\n * The full co-op journey against the real online stack: the Next app backed\n * by an in-process Postgres (DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory) plus the Bun game\n * server, both from playwright.config's webServer list — no Docker, no cloud.\n * Two isolated browser contexts play two guests: the host creates an online\n * world through the menus, the friend joins through the invite link, and the\n * pair must see each other, share block edits, and chat.\n */\n\n/** Console/page errors collected like the smoke fixture does (favicon 404 is noise). */\nfunction watchErrors(page: Page, sink: string[]): void {\n  page.on(\"console\", (message) => {\n    if (message.type() !== \"error\") return;\n    if (message.text().includes(\"Failed to load resource\") && message.location().url.endsWith(\"/favicon.ico\")) return;\n    sink.push(`${message.text()} (${message.location().url})`);\n  });\n  page.on(\"pageerror\", (error) => sink.push(String(error)));\n}\n\n/** Booted, synced, and drawing: the bar every online entry must clear. */\nasync function waitForOnlineGame(page: Page): Promise<void> {\n  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft !== undefined, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });\n  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.net?.status() === \"online\", undefined, { timeout: 30000 });\n  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.renderer.renderedTriangles() > 0, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });\n}\n\ntest(\"two guests share an online world via an invite link\", async ({ browser }) => {\n  // Two production builds of the game plus a WebSocket handshake each; CI\n  // renders with software GL, so the whole journey gets a generous ceiling.\n  test.setTimeout(240000);\n  const errors: string[] = [];\n\n  // ── the host: guest account → online world → in-game ─────────────────────\n  const hostContext = await browser.newContext();\n  const host = await hostContext.newPage();\n  watchErrors(host, errors);\n  // Seed a profile so the menu opens on the profile LIST (where the account\n  // panel lives) instead of the first-run create form.\n  await host.addInitScript(() => {\n    if (!localStorage.getItem(\"minecraft_profiles_v1\")) {\n      localStorage.setItem(\n        \"minecraft_profiles_v1\",\n        JSON.stringify({ version: 1, profiles: [{ id: \"host-profile\", name: \"Hosta\", skinId: \"default\", createdAt: 1 }], activeProfileId: \"host-profile\" })\n      );\n    }\n  });\n  await host.goto(\"/\");\n\n  await host.getByRole(\"button\", { name: \"Play online as guest\" }).click();\n  await expect(host.getByText(\"Playing as guest\")).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 });\n  await host.getByTestId(\"profile-host-profile\").click();\n\n  // Creative, so the host's block breaks are instant on the server side.\n  await host.getByTestId(\"new-online-world\").click();\n  await host.getByLabel(\"World name\").fill(\"Co-op Test\");\n  await host.getByLabel(\"World seed\").fill(\"4242\");\n  await host.getByRole(\"button\", { name: \"Creative mode\" }).click();\n  await host.getByRole(\"button\", { name: \"Create World\" }).click();\n  await waitForOnlineGame(host);\n\n  // Mint the invite with the host's cookies (the menu's Copy button wraps the\n  // same endpoint; the clipboard is out of reach in headless runs).\n  const worldId = await host.evaluate(async () => {\n    const response = await fetch(\"/api/worlds\");\n    const { worlds } = (await response.json()) as { worlds: Array<{ id: string }> };\n    return worlds[0].id;\n  });\n  const inviteToken = await host.evaluate(async (id) => {\n    const response = await fetch(`/api/worlds/${id}/invites`, { method: \"POST\" });\n    const { token } = (await response.json()) as { token: string };\n    return token;\n  }, worldId);\n\n  // ── the friend: invite link → guest account → same world ─────────────────\n  const friendContext = await browser.newContext();\n  const friend = await friendContext.newPage();\n  watchErrors(friend, errors);\n  await friend.goto(`/join/${inviteToken}`);\n  await expect(friend.getByText(/You've joined/)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 });\n  await friend.getByRole(\"link\", { name: \"Open the game\" }).click();\n\n  // First run in this fresh context: create the friend's local profile; the\n  // invited world is already waiting in the Online Worlds section.\n  await friend.getByLabel(\"Profile name\").fill(\"Friend\");\n  await friend.getByRole(\"button\", { name: \"Create\" }).click();\n  await friend.getByTestId(`online-world-${worldId}`).click();\n  await waitForOnlineGame(friend);\n\n  // ── both replicas agree there are two players in the room ────────────────\n  for (const page of [host, friend]) {\n    await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.players.size === 2, undefined, { timeout: 15000 });\n  }\n\n  // ── a block edit crosses the wire ─────────────────────────────────────────\n  // The host digs straight down. The replica's own mining is cosmetic (it\n  // never completes a break locally), so a journal entry appearing on BOTH\n  // clients proves the server decided the break and broadcast it.\n  await acquirePointerLock(host);\n  await host.waitForTimeout(1000); // settle (slow CI renderers need the margin)\n  await host.evaluate(() => {\n    window.__monecraft!.engine.state.player.pitch = -Math.PI / 2 + 0.02;\n  });\n  await host.mouse.down();\n  for (const page of [host, friend]) {\n    await expect\n      .poll(() => page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.blockChanges.changes().length), { timeout: 30000 })\n      .toBeGreaterThan(0);\n  }\n  await host.mouse.up();\n\n  // ── chat round-trips, rendering in the other player's log ────────────────\n  await host.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.net!.sendChat(\"hello from the host\"));\n  await expect(friend.getByText(\"hello from the host\")).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10000 });\n  await friend.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.net!.sendChat(\"hi back\"));\n  await expect(host.getByText(\"hi back\")).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10000 });\n\n  expect(errors, \"no console/page errors during the test\").toEqual([]);\n  await hostContext.close();\n  await friendContext.close();\n});\n"

3	How the online stack fits together, and how to run it. The offline
4	single-player game needs **none** of this: without an online action, the
5	client never makes an auth request (the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage
6	flag gates even the session check).
7	
8	## The pieces
9	
10	```
11	Browser ──(cookies)── Next.js app          ── Neon/Postgres
12	   │                   /api/auth/*   better-auth (guests + accounts)
13	   │                   /api/worlds…  world CRUD, invites, cloud saves
14	   │                   /api/worlds/:id/ticket   mints 60s HS256 join ticket
15	   │
16	   └──(ws + ticket)── Game server (Bun, Fly.io)  ── same Postgres
17	                       one authoritative GameEngine room per world (phase 4)
18	```
19	
20	The web app and the game server never talk to each other at runtime: the
21	join ticket (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, signed with the shared
22	`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`) is the only trust link, and both read the same
23	Postgres.
24	
25	## Identity: guests first
26	
27	- "Play online as guest" (menu → Account panel) creates a real better-auth
28	  user with `isAnonymous` — no form, instant play. Guests own worlds and
29	  memberships like anyone else.
30	- Upgrading (sign-up, or sign-in to an existing account, while holding the
31	  guest session) triggers the anonymous plugin's `onLinkAccount` hook
32	  (`lib/auth/server.ts`): worlds, memberships, and invites re-parent onto the
33	  new account before the guest row is deleted. **This hook is the "guests
34	  keep their worlds" promise** — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts` proves it against
35	  the real better-auth flow on real SQL (PGlite), including the
36	  duplicate-membership collision case.
37	- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.
38	
39	## Worlds, invites, cloud saves
40	
41	`lib/online/worldsService.ts` owns the rules (membership-gated reads that
42	present as `not-found` so ids can't be probed; owner-gated rename/delete/
43	invite; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses). The `app/api`
44	routes are thin HTTP adapters over it.
45	
46	Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
47	cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
48	concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
49	(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the client pulls the newer
50	save before retrying. Wiring the sync into the world list / autosave path
51	lands together with the multiplayer world browser in the online shell phase.
52	
53	## Environment & local development
54	
55	See `.env.example` for every variable (web: `DATABASE_URL`,
56	`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`,
57	`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`; game server adds `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`,
58	`ADMIN_TOKEN`).
59	
60	```bash
61	docker compose up -d          # local Postgres (dev only — tests use PGlite)
62	bunx drizzle-kit migrate      # apply db/migrations once
63	bun run dev                   # web app with accounts + API
64	```
65	
66	Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
67	`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
68	fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
69	no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
70	fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.
71	
72	## Production
73	
74	- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
75	  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
76	- **Fly.io** (game server, phase 4): shares `DATABASE_URL` and
77	  `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` with the web app.
78	
79	## Game server operations
80	
81	`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
82	hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
83	on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
84	persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
85	drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
86	See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.
87	
88	- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this).
89	- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics (players, tick, slowest-tick ms);
90	  requires `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`.
91	- `PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the
92	  Playwright multiplayer spec, and `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (a CLI client
93	  that joins, walks, and tallies traffic — point it at localhost or staging).
94	
95	Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
96	container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
97	with WebSocket ingress works.
98	
```

1	# Architecture
2	
3	Three layers with hard boundaries:
4	
5	```
6	React UI (components/)          declarative HUD/panels; reads snapshots, sends commands
7	    │  useSyncExternalStore + engine commands
8	GameEngine (lib/game/engine/)   headless simulation: all game state, stepped per frame
9	    │  reads/writes
10	Voxel world (lib/world/)        data + generation + meshing + queries
11	    ▲  read every frame by
12	GameRenderer (lib/game/render/) Three.js: maps simulation state → GPU objects
13	AudioDirector (lib/game/audio/)  WebAudio: maps engine events + state → procedural sound
14	```
15	
16	The engine has **no React, no DOM, no rendering** — it runs (and is tested) headlessly in `bun test`. The renderer, the audio director, and the input controller are the only modules touching Three.js scene objects, the `AudioContext`, and DOM listeners respectively.
17	
18	The ONLINE layer (accounts, cloud saves, invites, join tickets) sits beside the shell: better-auth + Postgres behind `app/api` route handlers that adapt the tested rules in `lib/online/worldsService.ts` — see [online.md](online.md). Offline single-player never touches it.
19	
20	## React shell (`lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/`)
21	
22	- `useMinecraftGame` creates the `GameEngine` in the canvas mount's callback ref, then an effect builds the `GameRenderer`, the `AudioDirector`, and `inputController` and drives the `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `engine.step(dt, input)` (in bounded catch-up substeps of ≤50 ms via `createAccumulator` from `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`, so slow frames — e.g. software GL — don't run the simulation in slow motion) → drain engine events (death/respawn handling, `attackSwung` → `renderer.triggerSwing()`, + `renderer.handleEvent` for particle bursts, + `audio.handleEvent`) → `minimap.sync(state)` → `renderer.sync(state)` → `audio.sync(state, dt)` → `renderer.render()`. The minimap must sync **before** the renderer because it reads `state.worldMeshDirty`, which `renderer.sync` clears.
23	- `components/GameShell.tsx` is the menu shell **above** `useMinecraftGame`: a profile-select → world-select → play state machine (profiles own worlds; see [save-format.md](save-format.md)) that runs the one-time legacy migration on mount and renders `MinecraftGame` keyed by `world.id` (+ a reload nonce). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset changes the key, so React unmounts the game subtree — running the effect cleanup that disposes renderer/audio/input and clears the rAF + autosave — and a fresh mount boots the next world, **no page reload**. The tab's active world is remembered in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes it while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. `useMinecraftGame` therefore takes the `world` + `profile` to play and persists to that world's own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key.
24	- UI state arrives as immutable `GameSnapshot`s via `useSyncExternalStore`; the engine replaces the snapshot object only when a visible value changes, so React re-renders are minimal and identity-driven.
25	- UI intents (`craft`, `swapSlots`, `selectSlot`, …) are dispatched as engine `Command`s. The only React state in the shell is pure UI concern: pointer lock, transient save messages, renderer failure.
26	- WebGL init failure is surfaced as `rendererError` and rendered as a fallback panel instead of crashing.
27	- On mount the shell installs a `window.__monecraft` debug handle (`{ engine, renderer, input, audio }`) and deletes it on unmount. The Playwright suite in `e2e/` drives the game through this handle — asserting on engine state and `renderer.renderedTriangles()` rather than pixels (see [testing.md](testing.md)); it's also handy from the browser console.
28	- UI pixel art is procedural: `lib/ui/` generates 16×16 item/HUD sprites as pure pixel buffers (`spritePixels.ts`, `hudPixels.ts` — DOM-free, unit-tested) wrapped by a cached canvas→data-URL layer (`sprites.ts`, falls back to a transparent pixel under happy-dom). `chromeTiles.ts` (`installUiTiles`, idempotent, `document`-guarded) installs the GUI textures as CSS vars: the menu-backdrop noise (`--mc-tile-dirt/stone`) and the chrome grain layered over the flat panel/slot/button colors (`--mc-tile-panel/well/button`, which default to `none` so SSR/pre-install falls back to the solid color). No image assets, no licensing exposure. `lib/ui/` must not import Three.js or the engine.
29	- Item hovers use `useItemTooltip` (`components/game/ItemTooltip.tsx`): a cursor-following, `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events:none` tooltip portaled to `document.body` (so it never clips inside the scrollable inventory or blocks the pointer-lock click), replacing native `title=` on the hotbar, inventory, and recipe entries. Elements keep their `aria-label` for the accessible name.
30	- The one binary asset is the UI pixel font (Monocraft, a Minecraft-style face under SIL OFL 1.1), self-hosted via `next/font/local` from the committed woff2 in `app/fonts/` and exposed as `--mc-font`; the monospace stack stays as the fallback and on the F3 debug readout, and Monocraft's coding ligatures are disabled in `base.css`. This is the single sanctioned exception to "zero binary assets".
31	- Note for the React Compiler lint rules: consume the hook with destructuring (`const { … } = useMinecraftGame()`); property access on the result object can false-positive `react-hooks/refs`.
32	
33	## Game engine (`lib/game/engine/`)
34	
35	- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command, playerId?)` (the id says whose intent it is; the SP shell omits it), advances `step(dt, input?)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`), the world size is overridable for fast headless tests, and two options shape multiplayer hosting: `authority` ("local" honors `pause` and freezes the world while the primary player is dead — the single-player feel; "server" ignores pause and never freezes a shared world) and `headless` (skips snapshot building — a server room has no React shell). `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` are the server join/leave surface (join restores the player's persisted v17 slice; leave serializes it back for the world save); `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` stores each client's latest intent packet.
36	- `state.ts` — `GameState` holds the **players map** (`players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; single-player is the one-entry case) beside the world: mobs, vehicles, and thrown spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, containers, world timers. `PlayerState` owns everything per-player: avatar pose, inventory/armor/hotbar, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player UI flags, per-player timers, live input. Plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
37	- `players.ts` — the alias layer and player queries. The flat legacy fields (`state.player`, `state.inventory`, `state.hearts`, …) are **accessor properties delegating to the primary player**, kept permanently for the SP shell, tests, and `window.__monecraft` — but **engine systems must never read them** (they'd act on "whoever is primary", wrong on a server); an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` guard enforces this under `systems/`. Systems take the acting `PlayerState` explicitly; `nearestPlayerTo`/`nearestTargetablePlayer` are the proximity/hunt queries (mobs hunt the nearest `mobsThreaten` player and anchor flee/follow on the nearest of any mode), and `allEligiblePlayersSleeping` gates the night skip (every non-dead, non-spectator player in bed; the `wakeUp` command climbs out before the fade commits).
38	- `commands.ts` — the `Command` union: every UI/input mutation enters the simulation through exactly this door.
39	- `tickDriver.ts` — how wall time becomes `step(dt)` calls: `createAccumulator` (variable-dt catch-up stepping, the browser shell's driver) and `createFixedTicker` (drift-corrected fixed 20 Hz ticks, the driver for a headless authoritative server). The engine itself stays dt-agnostic; both drivers clamp runaway catch-up identically (≤5 owed steps of ≤50 ms, older debt dropped).
40	- `blockChanges.ts` — the delta tracker behind the save format: tracked block writes against the worldgen baseline; reverted edits drop out of the save.
41	- `systems/` — one module per mechanic, each a function over `GameState`:
42	
43	### Per-frame step order (in `GameEngine.step`)
44	
45	0. Pause gate: while `state.paused`, `step` refreshes the snapshot and returns — mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all freeze (autosave still serializes fine)
46	1. Stuck detection / auto-unstuck (`STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`)
47	2. Death check + respawn countdown (while dead, only mobs tick)
48	3. Sleep gate: while `state.sleepTimer > 0`, `step` decrements the fade and returns (full freeze, like pause); at zero it skips the clock to the next morning
49	4. Player or mounted-vehicle movement (`systems/playerMotion.ts` / `systems/vehicles.ts` — walking derives direction from `yaw`; mounted rafts/ships carry the player and check water support)
50	5. Hunger drain, health regen, continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and oxygen/drowning damage (`systems/playerStats.ts` — `tickWaterExposure`, `tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`, all on the armor-bypassing path)
51	6. Mining progress and block breaking (`systems/mining.ts`; placement also lives here)
52	7. Day-night clock (`systems/dayNight.ts` — `daylightAt()` is the single daylight formula); immediately after, `systems/weather.ts` sets the **transient** `state.weather` (rain/snow/clear) as a pure function of `dayClock` + seed — cosmetic only: never serialized, never touches spawn/daylight balance
53	8. Random block ticks (`systems/randomTicks.ts` — each interval samples columns near the player and runs per-block handlers; drives crop growth and is the extension point for future saplings / grass spread)
54	9. Night hostile spawning (`systems/spawnDirector.ts`, interval/cap in config)
55	10. Dungeon spawners (`systems/spawnDirector.ts` `tickSpawnerDirector` — each interval, every intact dungeon spawner with the player in range drips one hostile onto the room floor, bounded by a local cluster cap and the shared `HOSTILE_CAP`; time-independent)
56	11. Mob AI: wander/aggro/flee, attacks with line-of-sight, daylight burn (`systems/mobAI.ts`). Ranged mobs (skeletons, boss) kite and loose arrows instead of meleeing; the boss also bears down, melees up close, fires a spread, and summons minions
57	12. Projectiles (`systems/projectileAI.ts` `tickProjectiles` — arrows integrate under gravity in capped substeps; block hits reuse the swept world DDA and the entity test is substepped so fast arrows can't tunnel; spent arrows despawn). Also ticked in the dead branch so in-flight arrows clear
58	13. Animal breeding (`systems/breeding.ts` — feed-to-love timers, baby maturity, pairing in-love adults within range; the passive cap bounds the population)
59	
60	**Vehicles.** Rafts and ships are persistent logical entities (`VehicleState`) rather than blocks. `systems/vehicles.ts` owns water-surface placement, right-click boarding for rafts, step-on boarding for ships, mounted steering, dismount selection, water-support checks, and v16 save restore filtering. The rider link is session-only; placed vehicles persist through `SaveData.vehicles`.
61	
62	**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter: player arrows (the bow) hit mobs with knockback, mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated), and neither hits the firer. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.
63	
64	**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new kind requires entries in all seven exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `FACTION_BY_KIND`, `MOB_DROPS`, `MOB_XP`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).
65	
66	**Villages & raids.** Villages generate as house clusters on flat land (`placeVillages`, last in `generateWorld` on its own `villageRand` so other passes stay byte-identical); the engine re-derives their centers on load (`collectVillageSites`) and seeds **resident villagers** there — but only when the world has no villagers yet, so a reload restores them instead of doubling. Residents persist via the v14 `mobs` field (`isPersistentMob` covers `faction === "villager"`); each carries a `profession` (v15) that selects its trade subset (`TRADE_PROFESSION`) and tints its smock. A **raid** is a transient `state.raid` wave machine (`systems/raid.ts`, like the boss — never serialized): a craftable **Ominous Horn** starts it near a village (a `placeBlock`-precedence step mirroring `trySummonBoss`), waves of the `raider` kind spawn until all are cleared (win → emerald + XP) or the residents die (loss). The raider needed no `mobAI` change — its `"raider"` faction was already wired into the enmity/threat/credit tables, so it hunts villagers, your pets defend, and it counts against `HOSTILE_CAP` (Peaceful cancels the raid).
67	
68	**Game modes.** The four modes (`survival`/`creative`/`adventure`/`spectator`, `lib/game/gameModes.ts`) are a single `state.gameMode` axis. Systems gate on **intent predicates** rather than the raw id, so all four share one set of seams: `takesDamage` switches off the three damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts` (covering fall/void/lava/water/drown/mob/poison at once) plus hunger/regen/oxygen in `playerStats.ts`; `canEditBlocks`/`freeBuild` gate breaking and placing in `mining.ts`; `canInteract` gates the interaction commands in `dispatch`; `canFly`/`isNoclip` drive flight and the collision skip in `playerMotion.ts` (and the auto-unstuck skip in `step`); `mobsThreaten` folds into `activeHostile` in `mobAI.ts`; `usesInventory`/`takesDamage` hide HUD elements. `gameMode` rides the per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's **switchable in-game** — `setGameMode` (`GameEngine.switchGameMode`) resets transient hazard timers, bars, flight, and noclip-entombment on the change. The transient `isFlying` is never serialized.
69	
70	**Difficulty.** Orthogonal to the mode, `state.difficulty` (`peaceful`/`easy`/`normal`/`hard`, `lib/game/difficulties.ts`) decides _how hard_ survival is — it follows the same shape as game modes: an enum, an `isDifficulty` guard, `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` for the UI, and **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that systems read instead of the raw id. The seams: `spawnDirector.ts` gates the initial population + night director + dungeon spawners on `hostilesSpawn` and scales the cadence/cap; `mobAI.ts` multiplies every mob hit at the strike (templates untouched); `playerStats.ts` scales regen and runs the new **starvation** tick (hunger 0 chips to a per-level HP floor, lethal only on Hard, routed through the same floored/lethal damage paths as Poison/environment). Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` → a v9 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`) and is switchable in-game — `setDifficulty` (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`) just updates the value the directors read next tick, except dropping to Peaceful, which despawns the hostiles already present (a plain splice — no loot/XP, no false boss victory). The two axes don't cross-couple: spawning keys only on difficulty, threat/damage only on mode.
71	
72	**Hardcore.** A per-world boolean (`state.hardcore`, persisted in save v10 + `WorldMeta`, **immutable** unlike mode/difficulty). The constructor resolves it first so it overrides the other axes — forced to Survival + Hard — and `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` early-return under it (the player-facing switchers are disabled; the engine's own death transition sets the mode directly, bypassing the lock). Death is permanent: the two lethal seams (`applyDamage`, `applyEnvironmentalDamage`) divert to `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()`, which sets the persisted `gameOver` flag and flips the player to **Spectator** (a free-cam over the dead world, invulnerable so mobs can't re-trigger it) instead of arming the respawn countdown — so a reloaded `gameOver` world boots straight into spectating (the constructor resolves `gameMode` to spectator; the existing `!isNoclip` stuck-check leaves it un-teleported). The shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event so a tab-close still persists the dead world; the Game Over screen (`components/game/GameOverScreen.tsx`) owns navigation (spectate / quit / delete), and `pause` is blocked while `gameOver`. The hearts render in a withered palette (`lib/ui/hudPixels.ts`).
73	
74	**Advancements & statistics.** Progression meta (`systems/advancements.ts`) hangs off the **single `GameEngine.emit` chokepoint** every system already emits through: `emit` pushes the event for the shell, then runs `observeProgress` — `recordEvent` folds it into the `state.stats` counters (a `Map<string, number>`), and `evaluateAdvancements` unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed, adding it to `state.advancements` (a `Set`) and emitting `advancementUnlocked` (the one event type `emit` skips, to avoid recursing). The advancement set is a **declarative `{ stat, threshold }` registry**, so unlock is uniform and adding one is a single row with no logic. Tick-driven display stats (distance, play time) bump directly in `step` via `recordTick`, off the unlock path. Both `stats` and `advancements` persist in save v13 and, like `xp` and unlike `effects`, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). The L-key overlay (`AdvancementsPanel`) reads detail through `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render — only the open flag and the unlocked **count** ride the snapshot, so play never churns it with stat values the HUD doesn't show.
75	
76	Combat (`systems/combat.ts`) runs on the `attack` command rather than per frame: a held bow branches to `tryFireBow` (instant click-to-fire, no draw-charge), a spear melees at its longer `weaponReach`, and otherwise `tryAttackMob` swings. The `placeBlock` command runs a fixed right-click precedence (`systems/interact.ts` + engine): throw the selected spear (`tryThrowSelectedSpear`) → feed/tame/sit/trade aimed mobs → board an aimed vehicle → interact with the aimed block (`tryInteractBlock`, e.g. bed/furnace/chest/door) → summon the boss / start a raid → fish → place a held vehicle on water → use the held item (`tryUseHeldItem`, e.g. hoe tills soil, seeds plant a crop) → `placeSelectedBlock` — so each interaction consumes the click instead of getting a block placed against it. New mechanics get a new system module and a slot in this sequence — don't grow the engine class with inline logic.
77	
78	**Block-entities (chest contents).** Blocks are bare `BlockId`s, but a chest needs attached storage, so `state.containers: Map<voxelIndex, InventorySlot[]>` holds each placed chest's slots (keyed by `world.index`, the same space as the block diff). Placing a chest creates an empty entry; opening one (`interactChest`) sets `state.openContainerIndex` and `inventoryOpen` so the panel renders its grid; the `moveStack` command shuttles slots across the inventory/chest boundary (chest indices offset by `CONTAINER_SLOT_BASE`); breaking a chest spills its contents into the inventory via `inventory.tryInsertSlots` (refused if they don't fit). `serialize()` persists non-empty containers as `blockEntities`; see [save-format.md](save-format.md).
79	
80	**Dungeon loot chests.** Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents can't ride the block-diff baseline. The engine instead keeps two session-only sets — `dungeonChestIndices` / `dungeonSpawnerIndices` — rebuilt each boot from the seed via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`, which replays the dungeon placement math without writing blocks), plus a **persisted** `lootedDungeonChests` set. On a dungeon chest's first open or break, `systems/dungeon.ts` `fillDungeonChestIfUnlooted` rolls loot seeded from `world.seed ^ voxelIndex` (`lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`) and marks the index looted. Gating on the looted set — not on whether the chest is currently non-empty — is what stops an emptied-then-reloaded chest from re-rolling (an empty container is dropped from `blockEntities`).
81	
82	## Renderer (`lib/game/render/`)
83	
84	- `GameRenderer.ts` — scene/camera/WebGL/lighting; `sync(state)` maps simulation state to visuals each frame; `dispose()` frees every GPU resource. WebGL creation returns `{ ok: false, error }` instead of throwing.
85	- **Camera modes**: `state.cameraMode` (session-only, V key) selects first-person or a third-person rear/front boom. Pose math is pure (`cameraView.ts`); the boom is clamped each frame by a `voxelRaycast` from the eye so walls never occlude the player. Gameplay stays eye-relative in every mode — mining/combat raycasts and audio panning read player yaw/pitch, never the camera.
86	- **World mesh**: one mesh covers the visible region (not chunked), rebuilt when the player crosses a `RENDER_GRID` (20-block) boundary or when the engine sets `state.worldMeshDirty` (block edits, respawn, unstuck). Old geometry is disposed on rebuild.
87	- **Per-voxel lighting**: the world/glass materials are patched via `onBeforeCompile` (`patchVoxelLighting`) to consume the baked `aLight` attribute — they gate the scene-lit colour by sky exposure (caves go dark) and add block light back as an albedo-tinted glow (torches/lava light the dark). **Day/night needs no uniform and no re-mesh**: the scene sun + hemisphere already scale with `daylight` in `syncDayNight`, so a sky-exposed surface dims at night through the scene lights while caves stay dark regardless. The patch anchors on stable `ShaderChunk` includes; the e2e "renders without errors" smoke test guards it against a Three.js bump.
88	- `mobVisuals.ts` — mob id → model map; creates/removes models as mobs spawn/die and animates bob + leg gait from mob state (the simulation knows nothing about legs).
89	- `vehicleVisuals.ts` — vehicle id → procedural raft/ship meshes; creates/removes models as placed vehicles appear/disappear and mirrors their pose.
90	- `projectileVisuals.ts` — projectile id → mesh map for in-flight arrows; one extruded-sprite geometry + material is shared across every arrow (only transforms differ), each oriented so its long axis points along its velocity. Freed once in `dispose()`.
91	- `heldItem.ts` / `crackOverlay.ts` — first-person item model and the 8-stage mining crack box (stage = progress / hardness). Held blocks stay cubes; everything else is the item's 16×16 inventory sprite extruded into a pixel-thick voxel mesh (`extrudedSprite.ts`, vertex colors, silhouette-only side faces) — the render layer imports `lib/ui/spritePixels` for this, which is legal because spritePixels is pure pixel-buffer code with no DOM. The holder group is posed every frame by `heldItemPose.ts` (pure math): a one-shot swing on the `attackSwung` event (the shell calls `renderer.triggerSwing()` from the event drain), a looping swing while mining, a walk bob scaled by horizontal speed, an equip dip on slot switch, and a faint idle sway.
92	- `spearVisuals.ts` mirrors transient thrown spear state into procedural shaft/tip
93	  meshes keyed by projectile id.
94	- `playerModel.ts` / `playerPose.ts` / `playerVisuals.ts` — the player's own humanoid body, visible only in third person: box meshes with pivot groups at the joints, walk gait + attack/mining chop from pure pose math (mirroring `heldItemPose.ts`), the look pitch applied to the head only, and the held hotbar item in the right hand via the shared `itemModel.ts` builder (also used by `heldItem.ts`).
95	- **Atmosphere** (all procedural, zero assets, freed in `dispose()`): `particleSystem.ts` + the pure, unit-tested `particlePool.ts` draw event-driven bursts (block shards from `BLOCK_COLORS`, mob-death puffs, eat crumbs, jump/land/footstep dust) as one `THREE.Points` with a soft-sprite shader, spawned via `GameRenderer.handleEvent(event, state)` (wired into the event drain beside `audio.handleEvent`). `skyView.ts` + the pure `starField.ts` layer camera-following stars, a moon, a sun disc, and drifting canvas-noise clouds over the day-night sky lerp, ramped by `daylight`. `precipitation.ts` is the camera-following rain/snow field driven by `state.weather`, and `syncDayNight` adds the matching overcast sky tint + dimmed light + nearer fog.
96	- **Skins**: the body is colored by a `PlayerPalette` from `lib/game/playerSkins.ts` (six presets); `GameRenderer.setPlayerSkin(palette)` recolors the named materials in place. The choice persists on the active **profile** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`; `updateSkin` calls `setProfileSkin`) — identity, not world state — and both the create-profile and pause-menu pickers' bust portraits (`lib/ui/skinPortrait.ts`) derive from the same palettes. (The legacy global `minecraft_skin_v1` key, still defined in `lib/game/skinSettings.ts`, is read only once by the save migration to seed the default profile's skin.)
97	- `minimap.ts` / `minimapColors.ts` — the top-right minimap: pure column sampling (top non-air block, height-shaded `BLOCK_COLORS`) feeding a 2D canvas that rebuilds its 128×128 base only when the player crosses a 16-block grid boundary or `worldMeshDirty` is set (read-only — the renderer owns clearing it), then blits with a yaw-rotated player arrow at ~10 Hz.
98	
99	## Audio (`lib/game/audio/`)
100	
101	All sound is procedural — no audio files, mirroring the sprite system. SFX are synthesized by [ZZFX](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/ZzFX) parameter arrays; music is a generative ambient pad over raw WebAudio nodes.
102	
103	- `audioDirector.ts` — the shell-side observer, exactly parallel to the renderer: `handleEvent(GameEvent)` plays one-shots (block break/place by material, hurt/eat/jump/land, mob attacks, death/respawn stingers) and `sync(state, dt)` drives everything continuous (footsteps, mining hit ticks, mob ambience, music mood, and the weather rain bed). Music follows `state.daylight` immediately and the biome with 5 s hysteresis, and ducks while paused. The rain bed (`rainLoop.ts`) is a looping filtered-noise source on the graph, off the SFX voice budget, whose gain tracks `state.weather` rain intensity (silent for snow / while paused). The engine never imports this module.
104	- `synth.ts` — `SynthBackend`, **the only seam that touches WebAudio for SFX**: renders each `SoundDef` to an `AudioBuffer` once via `ZZFX.buildSamples` and plays it through gain/pan nodes with playback-rate jitter, a 10-voice cap, and per-sound retrigger throttling (which also de-dupes catch-up substep event bursts). Tests inject a recording fake instead.
105	- `soundParams.ts` / `materials.ts` — pure data: ZZFX parameter tables per `MaterialGroup`/`MobKind` (tune by ear in the [ZZFX designer](https://killedbyapixel.github.io/ZzFX/)) and the exhaustive `BlockId → MaterialGroup` mapping.
106	- `footsteps.ts` / `mobAmbience.ts` / `musicBrain.ts` — pure schedulers/composer (distance-accumulator strides, per-mob randomized call timers with distance gain + look-relative stereo pan, pentatonic random-walk note generation). `musicPlayer.ts` renders notes as detuned pad voices through a lowpass and a procedural convolution reverb.
107	- **Lazy unlock invariant**: no `AudioContext` exists until the first user gesture calls `unlock()` — including the `zzfx` import itself, which instantiates one at module scope and is therefore only ever imported dynamically inside `unlock()`. This satisfies the browser autoplay policy, keeps SSR/`bun test` import-safe, and keeps the console clean for the E2E fixture.
108	- Volume settings (`settings.ts`) persist under their own localStorage key (`minecraft_audio_v1`) — never part of the world save.
109	
110	## Input (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`)
111	
112	Owns every DOM listener **and the DOM→intent mapping**: raw key codes, CapsLock, and pointer lock never leave this module. Continuous input is reduced to the abstract `FrameInput` (`move.{forward,back,left,right,jump,sprint,crouch}` + `mineHeld`) the engine reads each step — the engine has no notion of key bindings or the cursor (`mineHeld` already folds in "left mouse held **and** pointer locked"), which is what lets any input source (keyboard, future gamepad/keybinding screen, a network client's intent packets, replays) drive the same simulation. Discrete actions (hotbar, inventory toggle, place, eat, attack, unstuck, pause, F3 debug, V camera view) become commands; mouse-look calls `engine.applyLook`. The first click only acquires pointer lock; `KeyI` exits it. Tests build inputs via `frameInput` (`lib/game/engine/testSupport.ts`), which still speaks key-code names ("hold KeyW") but emits intents; the E2E pointer-lock fallback uses the controller's `forcePointerLock` test hook.
113	
114	**Pause ↔ pointer lock**: the browser consumes Escape to exit pointer lock, so Esc never reaches keydown while locked — losing the lock during plain gameplay is the pause trigger (`pointerlockchange` dispatches `pause`). The inventory (`KeyI`) and death paths set their state flags _before_ the async `pointerlockchange` fires, and the engine's `pause` command additionally ignores those states, so they don't open the menu. While unlocked, Escape toggles pause directly (and closes the inventory). "Back to Game" resumes and re-requests the lock; Chrome's ~1.25 s cooldown after Esc can reject that request — the rejection is swallowed and the player just clicks the canvas.
115	
116	## Inventory and items (`lib/game/`)
117	
118	- `inventory.ts` — pure slot algebra (`adjustSlotCount`, `craft`, durability, armor); every function returns a new array or `null` for "no change". Crafting refuses when the result doesn't fit rather than destroying overflow. Equipped armor is **dedicated storage**: `state.equippedArmor` (`Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot | null>`) holds the worn pieces themselves — `toggleEquipArmor`/`unequipArmor` move a piece between the inventory and the record, and `equippedDefense`/`armorReduction`/`consumeEquippedArmorDurability` (and Mending's `mendXp`) read/wear/repair those instances directly rather than re-finding them in the inventory by id.
119	- `items.ts` — `ITEM_DEFS`, `BLOCK_TO_SLOT`, `BREAK_HARDNESS`, armor slots, slot factories. `recipes.ts` — `RECIPES` (each with an optional `station`, e.g. `"furnace"` for smelting).
120	- Drop tables: `mobLoot.ts` (`rollMobDrops` — per-`MobKind` loot) and `items.ts` (`rollBlockDrops` — block drops, e.g. grass→occasional seed, mature wheat→wheat + 1–2 seeds). Both take an injectable `rng`, so tests get deterministic counts.
121	- `config.ts` — every gameplay tunable, named: physics, hunger rules, daylight thresholds, mob director, mining reach, autosave interval, the legacy `SAVE_KEY`, and `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (the worldgen baseline each world records).
122	- `save.ts` — versioned (de)serialization with an injectable `Storage` and a per-world save key (`worldSaveKey`, `lib/game/worlds.ts`); `profiles.ts` / `worlds.ts` hold the profile and world manifests, `legacyMigration.ts` folds an old single save into them; `spawn.ts` — deterministic spawn search + random land points.
123	
124	## World layer (`lib/world/`)
125	
126	One module per concern, behind an `index.ts` barrel — consumers always import from `@/lib/world`:
127	
128	- `blocks.ts` — `BlockId`, `BiomeId`, `WORLD_SIZE_*`, and both block palettes (`BLOCK_COLORS` paints the atlas; `HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` tints the held-item model — intentionally different values). Door facing/open/half states are ordinary IDs so they persist in the existing block diff.
129	- `doors.ts` — door-state encoding helpers and the thin panel bounds shared by meshing and collision.
130	- `voxelWorld.ts` — `VoxelWorld` stores voxels in a flat `Uint8Array` (index = `x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) plus a parallel `light` array and cheap queries (`get`/`set`/`isSolid`/`highestSolidY`/`getBiome`/`getSky`/`getBlockLight`).
131	- `lighting.ts` — per-voxel light (sky + block, packed 0–15 each into `world.light`). `computeFullLight` bakes the whole field from the blocks at load (top-down sunlight column pass + BFS bleed; block-light BFS from emitters); `applyEdit` patches it locally on each block edit with a Minecraft-style remove/refill flood. **Derived cache, never serialized** — a pure function of `world.blocks`. `opacity`/`emission` classify each block (air/glass transmit, water/leaves attenuate, torches/lava emit).
132	- `generation.ts` — `generateWorld(world)`: deterministic terrain, caves, lava, water, ores, trees, houses, and underground dungeons (`placeDungeons`, last in the pipeline). `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` (so it can't shift ore RNG) and before `placeDungeons` (so rooms overwrite lava). `collectDungeonSites(world)` re-derives dungeon chest/spawner indices from the seed for the engine. Constants live in the frozen `GEN` object. **Byte-identical output per seed is a save-format contract**, pinned by `generation.test.ts` hash tests — fix code, never hashes.
133	- `noise.ts` — bit-portable noise/trig (`portableSin`/`portableCos`, integer `hash2D`/`hash01`) built only from IEEE-exact operations, so worldgen bytes are identical on every JS engine (Bun server ≡ browser client; `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it). **All seed-determined code must take its noise/trig from here** — the biome fields (`voxelWorld.getBiome`), terrain waves, cave walks, weather windows, and the daylight curve all do; native `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` are fine only for frame-local gameplay math (aiming, mob steering, doors) that never feeds seed-determined bytes.
134	- `meshing.ts` — `buildGeometryRegion(world, …)` with face culling, baked ambient occlusion, atlas UVs, and a per-vertex `aLight` (sky-exposure, block-light) sampled from the faced voxel; `buildGeometryLayersRegion` splits opaque terrain from clear glass for the renderer.
135	- `atlas.ts` — runtime canvas block atlas (`createBlockAtlasTexture`); tiles are generated from `BLOCK_COLORS`, no image assets. The only world module that touches the DOM.
136	- `queries.ts` — `voxelRaycast` (DDA), `collidesAt`, `hasSupportUnderPlayer`.
137	
138	## Engine invariants & gotchas
139	
140	Hard-won invariants — easy to silently break:
141	
142	- **Transparent blocks are explicit render layers**: `buildGeometryLayersRegion` sends glass to a blended, non-depth-writing material while opaque terrain keeps normal depth writes. Glass-to-glass and water-to-water internal faces are culled; opaque faces touching glass remain visible through it. Water still uses the opaque layer and all world materials are `THREE.DoubleSide` so water is visible from inside. New transparent blocks must extend both the layer routing and face-visibility rules. **Lava is the exception that proves the rule**: it is a normal _solid_ block, so the default opaque face-culling already shows only its surface — it needs no special routing. (It does need a lighting class — see below.)
143	
144	- **Lighting is a derived cache, never serialized**: `world.light` is a pure function of `world.blocks`, baked once at load (`computeFullLight`) and patched per edit (`applyEdit`), both in `lib/world/lighting.ts`. The bake/patch is wired in the **engine** (the constructor and `blockChanges.set`, the single chokepoint all gameplay edits flow through) — never the renderer — so the minimap-before-renderer `worldMeshDirty` ordering stays intact. Every new block needs a lighting class in `opacity`/`emission` (the default is opaque, no emission); sky light falls straight down a clear column for free at any level, so the bake's column pass and the incremental flood must agree (see `propagated`). `applyEdit`'s correctness is pinned by whole-array equivalence tests against a from-scratch bake.
145	
146	- **Lava and the head/body damage split**: lava is solid, so contact damage (`tickLavaExposure`) samples the block underfoot/at body height rather than immersion. Drowning (`tickOxygen`) keys on the _head_ (eye cell) and is deliberately separate from the body-keyed 60 s water-exposure timer — they coexist (one models holding your breath, the other prolonged immersion). All three transient timers/state reset on reload/respawn and are never serialized.
147	- **Doors are multi-cell state machines encoded as blocks**: four facings × open/closed × upper/lower produce 16 internal `BlockId`s. Placement and breaking update both cells atomically; interaction validates the matching pair before toggling. `doorBounds` drives both thin mesh geometry and AABB collision. `highestSolidY` ignores doors so mob surface-following cannot climb over them; mob movement still checks their panel collision and never calls the player-only interaction handler.
148	- **Being in water is not "stuck"**: the unstuck teleport fires only on solid-block overlap or falling below the world (y < 2). Don't make water count as a collision in `collidesAt` — players may stay submerged, though `tickWaterExposure` starts armor-bypassing damage after 60 continuous seconds. Its transient timers reset on exit and are never serialized.
149	- **Water is replaceable during placement**: the normal raycast still ignores water and targets the solid surface behind it; `placeSelectedBlock` accepts the resulting destination when it contains air or water. Failed self-overlap placement must restore the original cell (including water), not blindly write air.
150	- **Daylight thresholds** (daylight ranges 0.04–1.0, named in `config.ts`): hostiles night-spawn below 0.28; spiders are hostile only below 0.42 (passive in twilight); zombies/skeletons burn above 0.72. The game boots at dawn (~0.05), so initial hostiles aggro immediately — headless tests use a `calmDaytime` helper.
151	- **DDA boundary ambiguity**: a raycast origin exactly on a cell boundary (integer coordinate) may target a diagonal neighbor — relevant for tests that aim at specific blocks.
152	- **Pointer lock**: the first left-click only acquires pointer lock (no mining); `KeyI` explicitly exits lock; right-click places without requiring lock.
153	- **Client-only**: never touch `window`/`document`/localStorage at module top level — everything runs behind `"use client"` and mounts via the callback ref/effect. The engine itself must stay DOM-free so it keeps running under `bun test`.
154

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Multiplayer game server (groundwork)**: a Bun process hosting authoritative world rooms over WebSocket — protocol v1 (JSON envelopes + one gzipped world-sync frame; total validation of hostile input with a per-command allow-list), 20 Hz fixed-tick rooms with client-pose clamping (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport rejection → forcePose) that keeps hunger/stats/fall-damage server-authoritative, change-only per-player self-deltas, deadbanded 10 Hz mob replication with 5 s keyframes, chat with rate limits, backpressure shedding + slow-client kicks, join-restore/leave-persist through the v17 save, 60 s dirty persistence + SIGTERM drain, idle room eviction, /health + token-guarded /rooms diagnostics, PERSISTENCE=memory for DB-less runs, a netProbe CLI client, and Dockerfile + fly.toml. The engine gains authority-aware remote-pose application and can construct playerless rooms (bootPlayer: false).
- **Online accounts, cloud saves & invites (groundwork)**: better-auth identities with instant anonymous guests — upgrading to a real account (sign-up or sign-in while playing as guest) re-parents the guest's worlds/memberships/invites onto the new account, proven by an integration test against real better-auth + real SQL (PGlite). Drizzle/Postgres schema for worlds, memberships, and invite links; membership-gated world CRUD; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses; gzipped single-player cloud-save blobs with last-write-wins conflict detection; and 60-second HS256 join tickets — the only trust link the future game server needs (it never sees cookies). Menu gains an Account panel. Fully offline-first: until the player takes an online action, the client makes no auth requests at all.

### Changed

- **Multi-player engine core** (save **v16→v17**; single-player behavior unchanged — the full e2e suite passes as before): the engine now models N players in one world, with single-player as the one-entry case of the same state. `GameState.players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>` absorbs every per-player field (inventory, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player timers); the old flat fields remain as accessor aliases onto the primary player for the shell/tests/console, with an ESLint guard banning them inside engine systems. All 23 systems take the acting player explicitly: mobs hunt the nearest targetable player (Creative/Spectator excluded) and anchor flee/pet-follow on the nearest of any mode; arrows/explosions hit any/all players in range; spawn directors center waves on a random party member and scale the hostile cap by `ceil(players/2)`; dungeon spawners arm for any player in radius; random ticks split their budget across players; raid rewards pay every living player. The night skips only when **every** eligible player is in bed (new `wakeUp` command backs out pre-fade). `dispatch`/`applyLook` take the commanding player's id; `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` (join restores the persisted v17 slice, leave serializes it back), `setPlayerInput`, and the `authority`/`headless` engine options are the surface a multiplayer server drives. Saves migrate automatically (v16 flat fields wrap into `players: [{id:"local",…}]`; pet owners become real player ids).
- **Input intents** (no behavior change): the engine's `FrameInput` no longer carries DOM key codes, CapsLock, or pointer-lock state — the input controller reduces them to abstract movement intents (`forward/back/left/right/jump/sprint/crouch` + `mineHeld`). Key bindings and cursor capture now live entirely in `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`; the engine simulates the same regardless of input source, which is what a multiplayer client's per-tick intent packets (and a future keybinding screen) require.
- **Tick driver extraction** (no behavior change): the rAF loop's catch-up substepping moved from `useMinecraftGame` into `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts` (`createAccumulator`), alongside a new drift-corrected `createFixedTicker` — the 20 Hz driver a headless multiplayer server will step worlds with. Unit-tested with a fake clock (catch-up, debt-drop cap, no drift under chronically-late callbacks).
- **Portable worldgen noise** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` **10→11**, save schema stays v16): all seed-determined noise — terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, underground speckle/flora hashes, weather windows, the daylight curve — moved from engine-defined `Math.sin` to bit-portable implementations (`lib/world/noise.ts`), so the same seed now generates **byte-identical worlds on every JS engine**. This is the groundwork for online multiplayer (a Bun server and browser clients must agree on the generated baseline to sync worlds as seed + block diff) and retires the fragile "worldgen hashes are only valid on the pinned Bun" caveat.
