  - **Locked to Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces the game mode to Survival and the difficulty to Hard and **disables both pause-menu switchers** (immutable for the world's life), so there's no flipping to Creative or lowering the difficulty to cheat death. Its hearts render in a darker **withered** variant (a recolour of the procedural heart sprite)
  - **Death is permanent → spectate the dead world.** On death there is no respawn: the player flips to a **Spectator** free camera over their dead world (mobs keep roaming but can't touch them) and a **Game Over** screen offers _Spectate World_ (minimizes so you can fly around), _Back to Worlds_, or _Delete World_. 1	# Player Manual
2	
3	A complete guide to playing Monecraft — a single-player, browser-based voxel
4	sandbox. Mine, build, craft, farm, fight off the night, and survive.
5	
6	This page is the prose guide; for the exact numbers (every recipe, block, mob, and
7	item stat) see the [reference tables](reference.md). Just want the keys? They're in
8	the [README](../README.md#controls).
9	
10	> Everything you see and hear is generated from code at runtime — there are no
11	> image or audio files anywhere in the game.
12	
13	## Worlds & profiles
14	
15	The game opens to a menu rather than dropping you straight into a world:
16	
17	1. **Pick a profile.** A profile is a player — a name and an appearance (skin). On a
18	   shared browser everyone can have their own. Create one with **New Profile**, choose
19	   a skin, and you're in; rename or delete profiles from the same screen.
20	2. **Pick a world.** Each profile keeps its **own** list of worlds. **New World** lets
21	   you name it, choose a **world type** (Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands —
22	   see [the reference](reference.md#world-types)), and optionally enter a **seed** —
23	   type a number or a word to get the same world every time, or leave it blank for a
24	   random one. Worlds you've played show most-recent first; rename or delete them here too.
25	3. **Play.** Choosing a world drops you in. From the pause menu (**Esc**), **Save &
26	   Quit to Worlds** takes you back to the list, and reloading the page resumes the
27	   world you were in.
28	
29	Everything is saved in your browser (localStorage). Deleting a world removes its save;
30	deleting a profile removes all of its worlds.
31	
32	## Getting started: your first day
33	
34	You spawn at dawn on solid ground with a small starter kit: stacks of grass, dirt,
35	stone, wood, planks, cobble, and sand, plus a **wood pickaxe** and a **knife**.
36	
37	The day-night cycle is short — **four minutes per full day** — so the first night
38	comes fast. A good opening:
39	
40	1. **Look around.** Double-click the game to lock the mouse (the starting gesture
41	   doesn't mine). Move with `W A S D`, look with the mouse.
42	2. **Gear up from your kit.** Open the inventory with **`I`**. You already have
43	   cobble and wood, so craft a **stone pickaxe** (2 cobble + 1 wood) and a **stone
44	   sword** (2 cobble + 1 wood) — both upgrades over your starting wood pickaxe and
45	   knife.
46	3. **Mine and gather.** Hold **left-click** to break trees, stone, and dirt for
47	   more materials; craft **2 wood → 4 planks** whenever you need them.
48	4. **Shelter before dark.** Wall yourself in with blocks (**right-click** or `E`
49	   to place the selected hotbar item), or craft a **bed** and skip the night
50	   entirely. Hostile mobs spawn once it gets dark, so don't be caught in the open.
51	
52	From there it's a sandbox: dig for ores, build, farm, breed animals, and gear up.
53	
54	## Controls
55	
56	| Key / input        | Action                                                                                                        |
57	| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
58	| `W` `A` `S` `D`    | Move (walk / strafe)                                                                                          |
59	| `Space`            | Jump                                                                                                          |
60	| `C`                | Crouch (slower, careful movement)                                                                             |
61	| `W` + `CapsLock`   | Sprint — faster, but drains hunger                                                                            |
62	| Double-tap `Space` | Toggle flight in Creative (Spectator always flies); `Space` / `C` rise/descend while flying                   |
63	| Mouse              | Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)                                                 |
64	| Left-click (hold)  | Break the targeted block / attack a mob                                                                       |
65	| Right-click or `E` | Place/interact, or throw a selected spear                                                                     |
66	| `1`–`9`            | Select a hotbar slot                                                                                          |
67	| `I`                | Open / close inventory & crafting                                                                             |
68	| `L`                | Open / close advancements & statistics                                                                        |
69	| `F`                | Eat the selected food, or drink a selected potion                                                             |
70	| `V`                | Cycle camera: first-person → third-person rear → third-person front                                           |
71	| `Shift` + `U`      | Emergency unstuck (teleport to safe ground if wedged)                                                         |
72	| `Esc`              | Pause menu — Game (save / load / reset / quit, Game Mode, Difficulty), Options (volume, skins), Controls tabs |
73	| `F3`               | Debug overlay (FPS, position, daylight, mob counts)                                                           |
74	
75	Gameplay is always **eye-relative**: even in third person, your reach, aim, and
76	audio follow where your eyes point, and the crosshair stays centered.
77	
78	## Game modes
79	
80	Pick a mode when you create a world (next to the name, world type, and seed), and
```

commit 55f7da94c13e8319699c8473ac3abd54d64693c9
Author: John Hu <huziyong@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Jul 3 17:48:55 2026 +0800

    feat(net): NetworkSession — the client end of a multiplayer world
    
    Owns the WebSocket and a replica engine the existing renderer/audio/HUD
    consume unchanged. Handshake: hello → welcome → construct the replica
    from the server's seed (bit-identical worldgen) → apply the gzipped
    world sync. Outbound: the local player's pose + intents at tick rate,
    pings every 2s, and command routing — presentation commands stay on the
    replica, gameplay goes up the wire (selectSlot optimistically both).
    Inbound: the per-tick block journal mutates the replica world (the
    blockChanges tracker now journals every write since the last drain,
    because events alone can't reconstruct an explosion crater or a kelp
    stalk's water refill — the server broadcasts exactly that journal),
    self-deltas overwrite the local player's server-owned vitals through
    the same restore validators saves use, pose buffers feed ~125ms
    interpolation for remote players and mobs (keyframes prune the dead),
    and world events replay into the shell's existing event drain.

9	function mulberry32(seed: number): () => number {
10	  let t = seed >>> 0;
11	  return () => {
12	    t += 0x6d2b79f5;
13	    let r = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), 1 | t);
14	    r ^= r + Math.imul(r ^ (r >>> 7), 61 | r);
15	    return ((r ^ (r >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
16	  };
17	}

617	## Beds and sleeping
618	
619	Craft a **bed** (3 wool + 3 planks) and place it. Right-click it **at night** to
620	sleep: the screen fades to black, time skips to a fresh morning, and the bed
621	becomes your **respawn point**. Sleeping is refused during the day or when a
622	hostile mob is within **12 blocks**, with an on-screen reason. (Wool comes from
623	sheep, or from crafting 4 string — a spider drop — into 1 wool.)
624	
625	## Sound and music
626	
627	All audio is synthesized live — there are no sound files. Block breaks, footsteps,
628	mob calls, and combat all have procedural effects keyed to the material or
629	creature. The ambient music is generative: it shifts between brighter major-key
630	moods by day and darker minor-key moods at night, and changes flavor by biome
631	(desert, ocean, forest, mountains). Adjust **master** and **music** volume — and
632	pick your **player skin** — from the pause menu (`Esc`).
633	
634	## Saving
635	
636	Your world autosaves to the browser's `localStorage` every **15 seconds**, and you
637	can **Save**, **Load**, or **Reset** manually from the pause menu. A save stores the
638	world seed plus your edits, inventory, armor, stats, time of day, bed spawn, and the
639	contents of every chest — so the world regenerates identically and picks up where
640	you left off. Because saves
641	live in the browser, they're tied to that browser on that device; "Reset" starts a
642	fresh world.
```

Because saves\nlive in the browser, they're tied to that browser on that device; \"Reset\" starts a\nfresh world.",
  "new_string": "## Saving\n\nYour world autosaves to the browser's `localStorage` every **15 seconds**, and you\ncan **Save**, **Load**, or **Reset** manually from the pause menu. A save stores the\nworld seed plus your edits, inventory, armor, stats, time of day, bed spawn, and the\ncontents of every chest — so the world regenerates identically and picks up where\nyou left off. Because saves\nlive in the browser, they're tied to that browser on that device; \"Reset\" starts a\nfresh world.\n\n## Playing online\n\nOnline worlds are shared worlds that live on a server and hold **2–8 players** —\nprivate co-op with people you invite, not public matchmaking. Everything offline\nstays exactly as it is: local worlds never need an account or a connection.\n\n**Getting an identity.** The first online action signs you in as a **guest** —\none click, no form, from the **Account** panel on the profile screen (or\nautomatically when you accept an invite). Guests are real accounts: the worlds\nyou create and join are yours. When you want to keep them across browsers,\n**Create account** upgrades the guest in place — your worlds come with you.\n\n**Hosting.** On the world list, the **Online Worlds** section appears once\nyou've gone online. **New Online World** uses the same form as a local world\n(name, seed, world type, mode, difficulty); creating it connects you straight\nin. Press **Copy invite** on your world's card to put a join link on the\nclipboard — send it to your friends. Invite links expire after a while; copy a\nfresh one any time.\n\n**Joining.** Opening an invite link shows the world's name, signs you in (as a\nguest if you're new), and adds the world to your **Online Worlds** list — click\nits card to play. The world is yours to rejoin from that list from then on;\nthe link is only needed once.\n\n**Playing together.** Everyone shares one world: block edits, mobs, chests,\nday and night. You'll see the other players in the world with their names\noverhead. Press **`T`** (or `Enter`) to chat; a ping badge shows your\nconnection quality, and losing the connection pops a notice with the option to\nleave. The **server** owns the world — your mining completes when it confirms\nthe break (a barely-noticeable beat on a good connection), and your health,\nhunger, and inventory are its word, not the client's.\n\nA few things work differently online, and the rest is the same game:\n\n- **Pause is personal.** `Esc` opens your menu but the world keeps running —\n  nobody can stop a shared world. \"Save & Quit\" becomes **Leave world**.\n- **Sleeping needs everyone.** The night skips only when **all** players are\n  in bed (dead and Spectator players excepted) — climb back out to cancel.\n- The world saves on the server automatically; there's nothing to manage.\n- **Rafts and ships can't be boarded** in online worlds yet."
}

35	- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command, playerId?)` (the id says whose intent it is; the SP shell omits it), advances `step(dt, input?)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`), the world size is overridable for fast headless tests, and two options shape multiplayer hosting: `authority` ("local" honors `pause` and freezes the world while the primary player is dead — the single-player feel; "server" ignores pause and never freezes a shared world) and `headless` (skips snapshot building — a server room has no React shell). `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` are the server join/leave surface (join restores the player's persisted v17 slice; leave serializes it back for the world save); `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` stores each client's latest intent packet.
36	- `state.ts` — `GameState` holds the **players map** (`players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; single-player is the one-entry case) beside the world: mobs, vehicles, and thrown spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, containers, world timers. `PlayerState` owns everything per-player: avatar pose, inventory/armor/hotbar, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player UI flags, per-player timers, live input. Plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
37	- `players.ts` — the alias layer and player queries. The flat legacy fields (`state.player`, `state.inventory`, `state.hearts`, …) are **accessor properties delegating to the primary player**, kept permanently for the SP shell, tests, and `window.__monecraft` — but **engine systems must never read them** (they'd act on "whoever is primary", wrong on a server); an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` guard enforces this under `systems/`. Systems take the acting `PlayerState` explicitly; `nearestPlayerTo`/`nearestTargetablePlayer` are the proximity/hunt queries (mobs hunt the nearest `mobsThreaten` player and anchor flee/follow on the nearest of any mode), and `allEligiblePlayersSleeping` gates the night skip (every non-dead, non-spectator player in bed; the `wakeUp` command climbs out before the fade commits).
38	- `commands.ts` — the `Command` union: every UI/input mutation enters the simulation through exactly this door.
39	- `tickDriver.ts` — how wall time becomes `step(dt)` calls: `createAccumulator` (variable-dt catch-up stepping, the browser shell's driver) and `createFixedTicker` (drift-corrected fixed 20 Hz ticks, the driver for a headless authoritative server). The engine itself stays dt-agnostic; both drivers clamp runaway catch-up identically (≤5 owed steps of ≤50 ms, older debt dropped).
40	- `blockChanges.ts` — the delta tracker behind the save format: tracked block writes against the worldgen baseline; reverted edits drop out of the save.
```

  "new_string": "## Multiplayer client (`lib/net/`)\n\nOnline play mounts the **same** shell/renderer/audio/input stack on a different engine: `connectNetworkSession(url, ticket)` (`NetworkSession.ts`) performs the hello → welcome → gzipped world-sync handshake, then constructs a **replica** engine (`replica: true, bootPlayer: false` — worldgen from the server's seed is byte-identical thanks to `lib/world/noise.ts`, the world sync applies the block diff/containers/mobs on top). `useMinecraftGame` accepts the session via its `online` option: the replica engine is mounted instead of constructing one, localStorage persistence is skipped (the server owns the world), replicated server events join the local event drain (so toasts/audio/particles treat them like local ones), and `session.afterFrame` runs each rAF.\n\n- **Command routing** rides the engine's `routeDispatch` hook: presentation commands (`pause`, toggles, camera) run on the replica; gameplay commands go up the wire as `cmd` envelopes carrying the claimed eye pose (`selectSlot` optimistically does both). The input controller and every UI panel dispatch exactly as in single-player — they can't tell the difference.\n- **Own movement is client-owned** (the one hybrid concession): the local player simulates normally for zero-latency feel, streaming pose + intents at tick rate; the server clamps (speed/vertical/teleport → `forcePose` snap-back) and owns the consequences (hunger, fall damage, stats). Everything else is server-authoritative — the replica's own mining is **cosmetic** (progress caps just short of breaking; the true break arrives via the block journal), and `self` deltas overwrite the local player's vitals/inventory through the same validators saves use.\n- **Remote entities render in the past**: per-entity pose ring buffers (`interpolation.ts`) are sampled at estimated-server-time − 125 ms (clamp, never extrapolate), fed by 20 Hz player poses and deadbanded 10 Hz mob poses + 5 s keyframes; `clock.ts` keeps the server-time estimate via ping/pong RTT EWMA.\n- **UI**: `ChatPanel.tsx` (T/Enter, exits pointer lock while typing) and `ConnectionStatus.tsx` (ping badge, disconnect modal) subscribe to the session; `GameShell` owns the connect flow (guest sign-in → join ticket → session) and `app/join/[token]` is the invite landing page. See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format and [online.md](online.md) for the account/world plumbing.\n\n## Inventory and items (`lib/game/`)"
}

1	# Testing
2	
3	Two runners, three layers:
4	
5	- **`bun test`** — unit, integration, and component tests, colocated as `*.test.ts[x]` next to the code they cover. The shared setup (`tests/setup.ts`, preloaded via `bunfig.toml`) registers happy-dom so React component tests run under the same runner; the game engine itself needs no DOM (see [architecture.md](architecture.md)).
6	- **`bun run test:e2e`** — Playwright browser smoke tests in `e2e/*.e2e.ts` against the production build. The file suffix matters: `bun test` auto-collects `*.test.ts` AND `*.spec.ts`, so E2E files must use `.e2e.ts`.
7

54	## Running the E2E suite
55	
56	```bash
57	bunx playwright install chromium   # once
58	bun run test:e2e                   # builds and starts the prod server itself
59	```
60	
61	E2E tests assert through `window.__monecraft` (the live engine/renderer/input handle — also handy in the browser console) instead of pixels; the one render check uses `renderer.renderedTriangles()`. The shared `gamePage` fixture seeds a default profile + world and enters it through the menu (reloads auto-resume the tab's world), then fails any test that logs a console error; `menu.e2e.ts` instead drives the menus from empty storage with the plain Playwright `test`.
62	
63	**happy-dom has no 2D canvas context**: generated sprites degrade to a transparent data URL in component tests — assert sprite pixels in the pure `lib/ui` tests and component structure via roles/labels/`data-icon` attributes, not image sources.
64	
65	**happy-dom has no `AudioContext`** (and the `zzfx` package instantiates one at import): everything above the `SynthBackend` seam is pure and tested with a recording fake (see `audioDirector.test.ts`); the WebAudio glue itself (`synth.ts`, `musicPlayer.ts`, `rainLoop.ts`) plus real synthesis quality belong to the manual gameplay pass.
66	
67	**Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.
68	
69	## The worldgen hash policy
70	
71	Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.
72	
73	**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**
74	
75	Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly one case: a **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.
76	
77	To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` in the same commit as the cause.
78	
79	The digests are also an **engine-portability contract**: since worldgen v11, every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts` (polynomial sine, integer hashes — only IEEE-exact operations), so the same seed generates identical bytes on every JS engine. `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it in CI by recomputing the full-size world digest inside Chromium/V8 and asserting it equals the Bun/JSC baseline in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` — this is what lets a browser client and a multiplayer Bun server share worlds by seed + block diff. `lib/world/noise.test.ts` additionally pins exact golden doubles of the noise primitives. New worldgen code must import its noise/trig from `lib/world/noise.ts`, never `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` (engine-defined per ECMA-262 — the reason the old digests were only valid on a pinned Bun).
80	
81	The **portable-noise worldgen (v10 → v11)** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline: same wave formulas on `portableSin`/`portableCos`, plus an integer-hash `hash2D`. All seven digests re-rolled; **every structural probe passed unchanged** — the polynomial sine tracks the real one within ~6e-8, so terrain structure is preserved and only scattered single-block flips (cobble speckle, cave edges, flora patterns) moved the hashes. This bump also retired the old "case 2" (a Bun version bump could shift `Math.sin` results): the CI Bun pin is no longer load-bearing for worldgen, though it stays pinned for plain reproducibility.
82	
83	The **deep-cave lava worldgen** was the prior re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.
84	
85	The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was an earlier re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.
86	
87	## Writing new tests
88	
89	- Pure logic (inventory, spawn rules, a new system): unit-test the module directly.
90	- Gameplay behavior: boot a small engine — `new GameEngine({ seed, rng, worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } })` — and step it with synthetic `FrameInput`. Inject a seeded `rng` (see `mulberry32` in the engine tests) for determinism.
91	- The world boots at dawn with hostiles nearby; use the `calmDaytime` pattern from the engine tests when testing unrelated mechanics.
92	- A ray origin exactly on a voxel boundary may target a diagonal neighbor (DDA ambiguity) — center positions in cells when aiming at specific blocks.
93

1	# Monecraft (Next.js + TypeScript + Three.js + Bun)
2	
3	[![CI](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
4	[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/hutusi/monecraft?label=release&sort=semver)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/tags)
5	
6	A playable, Minecraft-inspired voxel game that runs entirely in your browser. Explore procedural terrain across five biomes, cross water by **raft** or **ship** — over living oceans with **fish**, **kelp**, sunken **shipwrecks** to dive, and **buried treasure** to hunt by map — and dig into **dark caves** — lit only by the torches you craft and place, where lava pools and mobs lurk. Mine ores, raid **underground dungeons** for loot, build and farm, breed animals, craft through seven gear tiers up to a **bow** and throwable **spears**, and take on an **endgame boss** for a true win condition — all across a day-night cycle with hunger, drowning, and lava hazards.
7	
8	The twist: **everything is procedural — zero binary assets.** Block textures and item sprites are painted from pixel code, all sound and music is synthesized at runtime, and lighting is computed per voxel. Single-player and client-only: keep **multiple worlds** under **multiple player profiles**, all saved to localStorage.
9	
10	## Run
11	
12	```bash
13	bun install
14	bun run dev
15	```
16	
17	Then open `http://localhost:3000`.
18	
19	The game opens to a menu: pick or create a **profile** (your name and look), then create or choose a **world** to play. New worlds let you pick a **type** — Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands — a **game mode**, a **difficulty** (Peaceful · Easy · Normal · Hard), an optional **Hardcore** toggle (permadeath, locked to Survival + Hard), and a seed. Each profile keeps its own list of worlds, so several players can share one browser. Inside the game, **Esc → Save & Quit to Worlds** returns to the world list.
20	
21	## Controls
22	
23	- `W A S D`: Move · `Space`: Jump · `C`: Crouch
24	- `W + CapsLock`: Sprint (drains hunger)
25	- Double-tap `Space`: Toggle flight in Creative (Spectator always flies); then `Space` / `C` to rise / descend
26	- `Mouse`: Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)
27	- `Left click` (hold): Break block / attack mobs
28	- `Right click` or `E`: Place/interact, board rafts, place water vehicles, or throw a selected spear
29	- `1..9`: Select hotbar slot
30	- `I`: Inventory & crafting · `L`: Advancements & statistics · `F`: Eat food · `Shift+U`: Emergency unstuck
31	- `V`: Camera view (first-person → third-person rear → third-person front)
32	- `Esc`: Pause menu — three tabs: **Game** (save / load / reset, **Save & Quit to Worlds**, the **Game Mode** and **Difficulty** switchers), **Options** (sound/music volume, Appearance skins), and **Controls** · `F3`: Debug overlay
33	
34	New here? The [player manual](docs/manual.md) walks through your first day, survival, crafting, farming, mobs, and more.
35	
36	## Development
37	
38	```bash
39	bun run lint        # ESLint
40	bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
41	bun test            # unit + integration + component tests
42	bun run build       # production build
43	bun run test:e2e    # Playwright browser smoke tests
44	bun run format      # Prettier
45	```
46	
47	All of these are enforced by CI on every PR. The game simulation is a headless engine (no DOM), so gameplay logic is covered by real simulation tests, and a Playwright smoke suite exercises the browser layers — see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md).
48	
49	## Docs
50	
51	- [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md) — player guide: getting started, survival, crafting, mobs, farming
52	- [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md) — scannable tables: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item stats
53	- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — engine/renderer/shell layering and invariants
54	- [docs/adding-content.md](docs/adding-content.md) — add a block, item, recipe, mob, or mechanic
55	- [docs/save-format.md](docs/save-format.md) — save schema and compatibility rules
56	- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — workflow and verification baseline
57	
```

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Multiplayer game server (groundwork)**: a Bun process hosting authoritative world rooms over WebSocket — protocol v1 (JSON envelopes + one gzipped world-sync frame; total validation of hostile input with a per-command allow-list), 20 Hz fixed-tick rooms with client-pose clamping (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport rejection → forcePose) that keeps hunger/stats/fall-damage server-authoritative, change-only per-player self-deltas, deadbanded 10 Hz mob replication with 5 s keyframes, chat with rate limits, backpressure shedding + slow-client kicks, join-restore/leave-persist through the v17 save, 60 s dirty persistence + SIGTERM drain, idle room eviction, /health + token-guarded /rooms diagnostics, PERSISTENCE=memory for DB-less runs, a netProbe CLI client, and Dockerfile + fly.toml. The engine gains authority-aware remote-pose application and can construct playerless rooms (bootPlayer: false).
10	- **Online accounts, cloud saves & invites (groundwork)**: better-auth identities with instant anonymous guests — upgrading to a real account (sign-up or sign-in while playing as guest) re-parents the guest's worlds/memberships/invites onto the new account, proven by an integration test against real better-auth + real SQL (PGlite). Drizzle/Postgres schema for worlds, memberships, and invite links; membership-gated world CRUD; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses; gzipped single-player cloud-save blobs with last-write-wins conflict detection; and 60-second HS256 join tickets — the only trust link the future game server needs (it never sees cookies). Menu gains an Account panel. Fully offline-first: until the player takes an online action, the client makes no auth requests at all.
11	
12	### Changed
13	
14	- **Multi-player engine core** (save **v16→v17**; single-player behavior unchanged — the full e2e suite passes as before): the engine now models N players in one world, with single-player as the one-entry case of the same state. `GameState.players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>` absorbs every per-player field (inventory, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player timers); the old flat fields remain as accessor aliases onto the primary player for the shell/tests/console, with an ESLint guard banning them inside engine systems. All 23 systems take the acting player explicitly: mobs hunt the nearest targetable player (Creative/Spectator excluded) and anchor flee/pet-follow on the nearest of any mode; arrows/explosions hit any/all players in range; spawn directors center waves on a random party member and scale the hostile cap by `ceil(players/2)`; dungeon spawners arm for any player in radius; random ticks split their budget across players; raid rewards pay every living player. The night skips only when **every** eligible player is in bed (new `wakeUp` command backs out pre-fade). `dispatch`/`applyLook` take the commanding player's id; `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` (join restores the persisted v17 slice, leave serializes it back), `setPlayerInput`, and the `authority`/`headless` engine options are the surface a multiplayer server drives. Saves migrate automatically (v16 flat fields wrap into `players: [{id:"local",…}]`; pet owners become real player ids).
15	- **Input intents** (no behavior change): the engine's `FrameInput` no longer carries DOM key codes, CapsLock, or pointer-lock state — the input controller reduces them to abstract movement intents (`forward/back/left/right/jump/sprint/crouch` + `mineHeld`). Key bindings and cursor capture now live entirely in `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`; the engine simulates the same regardless of input source, which is what a multiplayer client's per-tick intent packets (and a future keybinding screen) require.
16	- **Tick driver extraction** (no behavior change): the rAF loop's catch-up substepping moved from `useMinecraftGame` into `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts` (`createAccumulator`), alongside a new drift-corrected `createFixedTicker` — the 20 Hz driver a headless multiplayer server will step worlds with. Unit-tested with a fake clock (catch-up, debt-drop cap, no drift under chronically-late callbacks).
17	- **Portable worldgen noise** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` **10→11**, save schema stays v16): all seed-determined noise — terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, underground speckle/flora hashes, weather windows, the daylight curve — moved from engine-defined `Math.sin` to bit-portable implementations (`lib/world/noise.ts`), so the same seed now generates **byte-identical worlds on every JS engine**. This is the groundwork for online multiplayer (a Bun server and browser clients must agree on the generated baseline to sync worlds as seed + block diff) and retires the fragile "worldgen hashes are only valid on the pinned Bun" caveat. Terrain is visually unchanged (same formulas; every structural probe passed the re-baseline untouched), but exact bytes shift: **existing worlds reboot from their seed and discard block edits**, per the standard worldgen-bump policy. Digests re-baselined into the new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`; a new Playwright spec (`e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`) proves Chromium/V8 regenerates the exact Bun/JSC baseline.
18	
19	## [0.12.0] - 2026-07-03
20	
21	### Added
22	
23	- **The aquatic update**: the ocean the new rafts and ships sail is now worth sailing — fish, flora, wrecks to dive, and treasure to hunt, all on **zero binary assets**. Bumps **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10** (kelp/coral/wrecks/buried chests write generated blocks, so existing worlds reboot from their seed and every worldgen/world-type/meshing digest except flat was re-baselined per docs/testing.md) with **no save-schema change** — the schema stays **v16**.
24	  - **Kelp & coral**: the sandy ocean floor grows swaying **kelp stalks** and pink/blue **reef coral** (a new hash-gated `placeOceanFlora` pass that consumes no shared PRNG). Kelp is a solid cube painted to read as a plant (the wheat trick — no new geometry): stalks always keep a **3-block clear-water band** below the surface so boats and fishing casts never snag, growth via the existing random-tick sampler enforces the same cap, and **breaking a cell breaks the stalk above it, refilling submerged cells with water — never air**. Kelp smelts **3-at-a-time into dried kelp** (a 2-hunger snack); corals are decorative salvage. New `BlockId`s **appended** (55–57)
25	  - **Cod & salmon**: the first water-dwelling mobs. A dedicated **aquatic AI branch** (3D wander/flee, every move gated on the destination cell being water, no ground clamp) runs before any land logic; a beached fish flops and suffocates. Both drop **raw fish** — the recipe-book hint for it now reads "Hunt a cod". Fish are fungible (never persisted; old saves load cleanly), spawn as schools in whatever water lies near spawn, and a new **aquatic spawn director** trickles them in around the player (up to `AQUATIC_CAP` 24) so far-flung oceans are stocked too — failing closed on dry worlds (Superflat spawns none). Legless "fish" model variant on `createMobModel`, bubble-blip ZZFX calls
26	  - **Shipwrecks**: flooded plank hulls (broken walls, snapped mast, always fully submerged) sink onto the deep ocean floor on their own decoupled PRNG, holding 1–2 chests of nautical salvage — and the **treasure map** at a 40% roll. The dungeon lazy-fill generalizes to `fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted`: the site set holding a chest's index picks both the loot table and a family-distinct seed constant, and **all families share the persisted `lootedChests` field unchanged** (no re-roll exploit, no save bump)
27	  - **Buried treasure & the treasure map**: hold a map (wreck loot, or a rare fishing catch) and a **compass pill** points at the _nearest_ unearthed hoard while red **X**s mark the minimap; dig two blocks under the beach sand for the richest chest table in the game (emeralds guaranteed). The map is deliberately **stateless** — no per-item target, no save field: the compass derives everything from the seed and retargets automatically after each dig. Chests place on a fourth decoupled PRNG with a **seed-pure beach proxy** (terrain-height band + a below-sea neighbor column — never post-water block reads), sand-capped so a breaching cave can't expose them. First dig fires the new **treasureUnearthed** event → **X Marks the Spot** advancement + a **Treasures Unearthed** statistic
28	- **Rafts and ships**: craftable water vehicles on **zero binary assets**. Hold a **raft** (4 planks + 2 wood) or **ship** (8 planks + 3 wood + 2 string), right-click a water surface to place it, then travel without swimming. Rafts are smaller and slower and require right-click to board; ships are larger/faster and auto-board when you step onto the deck. Movement uses the existing WASD controls while mounted, and crouch dismounts to a nearby safe spot. Placed vehicles persist across reloads, so the save schema bumps **v15 → v16** with an additive `vehicles` field; vehicle items are string ids and vehicles are entities, not blocks, so **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). Rafts and ships live in their own **Vehicles** crafting category; placing plays a wooden thunk and a failed placement (no open water, blocked, or at the **`MAX_VEHICLES`** (64) per-world cap) plays a "can't place here" denial cue. A saved boat is never dropped on reload even if the water beneath it was later removed, and boat travel no longer inflates the walked-distance statistic.
29	- **Generated villages, villager professions & raids** (Living World, PR 2 of 2): the world is now inhabited and contested.
30	  - **Villages**: clusters of houses generate on flat, dry land — terraced and built so they're actually visible (the old loose houses rarely fit natural terrain, so they barely appeared). Villager **residents** spawn and live there and **persist with the world**; villagers no longer scatter loosely (a village-less seed falls back to a few wandering ones near spawn, so trading is always available). Bumps **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** — existing worlds of the old version reboot from their seed, and the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined — with no save-schema change for the villages themselves (residents ride the v14 `mobs` field). Villages run on their own decoupled PRNG (`villageRand`) placed last, so every other generation pass stays byte-identical to a village-less world of the same seed.
```

The client mounts the **same** renderer/audio/HUD/input stack on a *replica* engine (`NetworkSession`, `lib/net/`): it worldgens byte-identically from the server's seed, applies the gzipped world sync, predicts only its own movement (streamed at tick rate; the server clamps speed/teleports and owns hunger/health/inventory via change-only self-deltas), renders remote players and mobs ~125 ms in the past from interpolation buffers, and reroutes gameplay commands up the wire through the engine's `routeDispatch` hook — so the input controller and every UI panel behave exactly as in single-player. Pause is personal (the world keeps running; \"Save & Quit\" becomes \"Leave world\"), the night skips only when everyone's in bed, and mining is server-confirmed (~1 RTT). A full-stack Playwright spec (`e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`) drives two browsers through invite → join → shared edit → chat against the real Next app (on an in-process `pglite://memory` Postgres) and Bun game server, no external services. **v1 scope cuts**: rafts/ships aren't boardable online, in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only their hits), and advancements/stats accrue to the room's primary player only.\n- **Multiplayer game server (groundwork)**: a Bun process hosting authoritative world rooms over WebSocket"

17	    const timer = window.setInterval(() => setRtt(Math.round(session.rttMs())), 1000);
18	    return () => {
19	      unsubscribe();
20	      window.clearInterval(timer);
21	    };
22	  }, [session]);
23	
24	  if (status === "closed") {
25	    return (
26	      <div className="net-modal" role="alertdialog" aria-label="Disconnected">
27	        <div className="net-modal-box">
28	          <p>Disconnected from the server.</p>
29	          <button type="button" className="mc-button" onClick={onLeave}>
30	            Back to worlds
31	          </button>
32	        </div>
33	      </div>
34	    );
35	  }
36	
37	  return (
38	    <div className="net-status" aria-live="off">
39	      {status === "online" ? `${rtt} ms` : status}
40	    </div>
41	  );
42	}

1	import * as THREE from "three";
2	import { WALK_SPEED } from "@/lib/game/config";
3	import type { PlayerId, PlayerState } from "@/lib/game/engine/state";
4	import { DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE, SKIN_PRESETS, type SkinId } from "@/lib/game/playerSkins";
5	import { applyPalette, createPlayerModel, type PlayerModel } from "./playerModel";
6	import { computePlayerPose } from "./playerPose";
7	
8	/**
9	 * Other players' bodies in a multiplayer world: one humanoid per remote
10	 * PlayerState (the same procedural model/pose math as the local third-person
11	 * body) plus a floating name tag — a canvas-drawn sprite, in line with the
12	 * zero-asset rule (mirrors the renderer's hostile health bars). Poses arrive
13	 * already interpolated (NetworkSession writes them into state.players), so
14	 * this layer only mirrors state → scene, estimating gait from frame-to-frame
15	 * movement.
16	 */
17	
18	export type RemotePlayerInfo = { name: string; skinId: string | null };
19	
20	export type RemotePlayerVisuals = {
21	  /** Reconciles models with state.players (minus the primary). Call once per frame. */
22	  sync(players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>, primaryId: PlayerId, info: (id: PlayerId) => RemotePlayerInfo, timeMs: number): void;
23	  dispose(): void;
24	};
25	
26	function makeNameTag(name: string): { sprite: THREE.Sprite; texture: THREE.Texture; material: THREE.SpriteMaterial } {
27	  const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
28	  canvas.width = 256;
29	  canvas.height = 48;
30	  const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d")!;
31	  ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45)";
32	  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
33	  ctx.font = "28px monospace";
34	  ctx.textAlign = "center";
35	  ctx.textBaseline = "middle";
36	  ctx.fillStyle = "#ffffff";
37	  ctx.fillText(name.slice(0, 16), canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2);
38	  const texture = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas);
39	  texture.magFilter = THREE.NearestFilter;
40	  const material = new THREE.SpriteMaterial({ map: texture, depthTest: false, transparent: true });
41	  const sprite = new THREE.Sprite(material);
42	  sprite.scale.set(1.6, 0.3, 1);
43	  sprite.position.y = 1.35; // above the head (model origin is the body center)
44	  return { sprite, texture, material };
45	}
46	
47	type RemoteEntry = {
48	  model: PlayerModel;
49	  tag: ReturnType<typeof makeNameTag>;
50	  lastPosition: THREE.Vector3;
51	  lastTimeMs: number;
52	  skinKey: string;
53	};
54	
55	export function createRemotePlayerVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): RemotePlayerVisuals {
56	  const entries = new Map<PlayerId, RemoteEntry>();
57	
58	  const remove = (id: PlayerId) => {
59	    const entry = entries.get(id);
60	    if (!entry) return;
61	    scene.remove(entry.model.group);
62	    for (const material of entry.model.materials) material.dispose();
63	    for (const geometry of entry.model.geometries) geometry.dispose();
64	    entry.tag.texture.dispose();
65	    entry.tag.material.dispose();
66	    entries.delete(id);
67	  };
68	
69	  return {
70	    sync(players, primaryId, info, timeMs) {
71	      for (const [id, player] of players) {
72	        if (id === primaryId) continue;
73	        let entry = entries.get(id);
74	        if (!entry) {
75	          const model = createPlayerModel();
76	          const meta = info(id);
77	          const tag = makeNameTag(meta.name);
78	          model.group.add(tag.sprite);
79	          scene.add(model.group);
80	          entry = { model, tag, lastPosition: player.position.clone(), lastTimeMs: timeMs, skinKey: "" };
81	          entries.set(id, entry);
82	        }
83	        const meta = info(id);
84	        if (entry.skinKey !== (meta.skinId ?? "default")) {
85	          entry.skinKey = meta.skinId ?? "default";
86	          const preset = SKIN_PRESETS.find((p) => p.id === (entry!.skinKey as SkinId));
87	          applyPalette(entry.model, preset?.palette ?? DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE);
88	        }
89	
90	        entry.model.group.position.copy(player.position);
91	        entry.model.group.rotation.y = player.yaw;
92	        entry.model.head.rotation.x = player.pitch;
93	
94	        // Gait from observed movement (poses are interpolated, velocity is unknown).
95	        const dtMs = Math.max(1, timeMs - entry.lastTimeMs);
96	        const speed = (entry.lastPosition.distanceTo(player.position) / dtMs) * 1000;
97	        entry.lastPosition.copy(player.position);
98	        entry.lastTimeMs = timeMs;
99	        const pose = computePlayerPose({
100	          timeMs,
101	          moveFactor: Math.min(1, speed / WALK_SPEED),
102	          miningActive: player.mining.targetKey !== "",
103	          swingStartMs: -Infinity,
104	          castStartMs: -Infinity,
105	          reelStartMs: -Infinity,
106	          fishingActive: false
107	        });
108	        entry.model.leftArm.rotation.x = pose.leftArmX;
109	        entry.model.rightArm.rotation.x = pose.rightArmX;
110	        entry.model.leftLeg.rotation.x = pose.leftLegX;
111	        entry.model.rightLeg.rotation.x = pose.rightLegX;
112	        entry.model.group.visible = !player.isDead;
113	      }
114	
115	      // Gone players drop their models.
116	      for (const id of [...entries.keys()]) {
117	        if (!players.has(id) || id === primaryId) remove(id);
118	      }
119	    },
120	
121	    dispose() {
122	      for (const id of [...entries.keys()]) remove(id);
123	    }
124	  };
125	}
126

1	import { decodeClientFrame } from "@/lib/net/codec";
2	import { CLOSE_BAD_TICKET, CLOSE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH, CLOSE_ROOM_FULL, PROTOCOL_VERSION } from "@/lib/net/protocol";
3	import { verifyTicket } from "@/lib/net/tickets";
4	import { createDrizzlePersistence, createMemoryPersistence } from "./persistence";
5	import { RoomRegistry } from "./roomRegistry";
6	import type { Room, ClientSink } from "./room";
7	
8	/**
9	 * The game server: one Bun process hosting many world rooms over WebSocket.
10	 * Run with `bun server/index.ts`. Environment:
11	 *
12	 *   PORT               listen port (default 8080)
13	 *   GAME_TICKET_SECRET shared with the web app — REQUIRED (tickets are the door)
14	 *   PERSISTENCE        "postgres" (default; needs DATABASE_URL) or "memory"
15	 *   MAX_ROOMS          concurrent worlds in this process (default 6)
16	 *   ADMIN_TOKEN        guards GET /rooms diagnostics (optional)
17	 *
18	 * The socket handshake: the FIRST frame must be a valid `hello` carrying a
19	 * live ticket (minted by the web app) and a matching protocol version, within
20	 * 5 seconds — anything else closes the socket with a 4xxx code.
21	 */
22	
23	const PORT = Number.parseInt(process.env.PORT ?? "8080", 10);
24	const SECRET = process.env.GAME_TICKET_SECRET;
25	const MAX_ROOMS = Number.parseInt(process.env.MAX_ROOMS ?? "6", 10);
26	const HELLO_DEADLINE_MS = 5000;
27	
28	if (!SECRET) {
29	  console.error("GAME_TICKET_SECRET is required (see .env.example)");
30	  process.exit(1);
31	}
32	
33	const persistence = process.env.PERSISTENCE === "memory" ? createMemoryPersistence() : createDrizzlePersistence();
34	const registry = new RoomRegistry(persistence, MAX_ROOMS);
35	registry.startSweeper();
36	
37	type SocketData = {
38	  helloTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null;
39	  room: Room | null;
40	  playerId: string | null;
41	};
42	
43	const server = Bun.serve<SocketData>({
44	  port: PORT,
45	  fetch(request, bunServer) {
46	    const url = new URL(request.url);
47	    if (url.pathname === "/health") return Response.json({ ok: true, rooms: registry.diagnostics().length });
48	    if (url.pathname === "/rooms") {
49	      const token = request.headers.get("authorization")?.replace(/^Bearer /, "");
50	      if (!process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN || token !== process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN) return new Response("forbidden", { status: 403 });
51	      return Response.json({ rooms: registry.diagnostics() });
52	    }
53	    if (url.pathname === "/ws") {
54	      const upgraded = bunServer.upgrade(request, { data: { helloTimer: null, room: null, playerId: null } satisfies SocketData });
55	      if (upgraded) return undefined as unknown as Response;
56	      return new Response("expected a websocket", { status: 426 });
57	    }
58	    return new Response("not found", { status: 404 });
59	  },
60	  websocket: {
61	    open(ws) {
62	      ws.data.helloTimer = setTimeout(() => ws.close(CLOSE_BAD_TICKET, "no hello"), HELLO_DEADLINE_MS);
63	    },
64	    async message(ws, raw) {
65	      const message = decodeClientFrame(typeof raw === "string" ? raw : null);
66	      if (!message) return;
67	
68	      // Pre-admission: only a valid hello gets past this block.
69	      if (!ws.data.room) {
70	        if (message.t !== "hello") return;
71	        if (ws.data.helloTimer) clearTimeout(ws.data.helloTimer);
72	        if (message.protocol !== PROTOCOL_VERSION) return ws.close(CLOSE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH, `server speaks v${PROTOCOL_VERSION}`);
73	        const claims = await verifyTicket(message.ticket, SECRET!);
74	        if (!claims || claims.pv !== PROTOCOL_VERSION) return ws.close(CLOSE_BAD_TICKET, "invalid ticket");
75	        const room = await registry.getOrLoad(claims.wid);
76	        if (!room) return ws.close(CLOSE_ROOM_FULL, "no room available");
77	        const sink: ClientSink = {
78	          send: (data) => void ws.send(data),
79	          close: (code, reason) => ws.close(code, reason),
80	          bufferedAmount: () => ws.getBufferedAmount()
81	        };
82	        if (await room.join(claims, sink)) {
83	          ws.data.room = room;
84	          ws.data.playerId = claims.sub;
85	        }
86	        return;
87	      }
88	
89	      if (ws.data.playerId) await ws.data.room.handleMessage(ws.data.playerId, message);
90	    },
91	    close(ws) {
92	      if (ws.data.helloTimer) clearTimeout(ws.data.helloTimer);
93	      if (ws.data.room && ws.data.playerId) ws.data.room.leave(ws.data.playerId);
94	    }
95	  }
96	});
97	
98	console.log(`monecraft game server on :${server.port} (${process.env.PERSISTENCE === "memory" ? "memory" : "postgres"} persistence, ≤${MAX_ROOMS} rooms)`);
99	
100	// Fly sends SIGTERM on deploy/stop: drain every room (persist + close) first.
101	for (const signal of ["SIGTERM", "SIGINT"] as const) {
102	  process.on(signal, () => {
103	    void registry.shutdownAll().then(() => process.exit(0));
104	  });
105	}

169	    this.emptySinceMs = null;
170	
171	    sink.send(
172	      encodeServerMessage({
173	        t: "welcome",
174	        protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION,
175	        playerId: claims.sub,
176	        worldId: this.worldId,
177	        seed: this.engine.state.world.seed,
178	        worldType: this.engine.worldTypeName,
179	        difficulty: this.engine.state.difficulty,
180	        hardcore: this.engine.state.hardcore,
181	        dayClock: this.engine.state.dayClock,
182	        tick: this.tickCount,
183	        players: this.roster()
184	      })
185	    );
186	    sink.send(await gzipWorldSync(this.buildWorldSync()));
187	    this.broadcast({ t: "playerJoined", player: this.rosterEntry(player, conn) }, claims.sub);
188	    return true;
189	  }
190	
191	  /** Removes a player (socket closed or kicked); persists their slice into the offline set. */
192	  leave(playerId: string): void {
193	    const conn = this.clients.get(playerId);
194	    if (!conn) return;
195	    this.clients.delete(playerId);
196	    const saved = this.engine.removePlayer(playerId);
197	    if (saved) this.offlinePlayers.set(playerId, saved);
198	    this.dirtySinceStore = true;
199	    this.broadcast({ t: "playerLeft", id: playerId });
200	    if (this.clients.size === 0) this.emptySinceMs = this.now();
201	  }
202	
203	  /** One validated client frame. */
204	  async handleMessage(playerId: string, message: ClientMessage): Promise<void> {
205	    const conn = this.clients.get(playerId);
206	    if (!conn) return;
207	    switch (message.t) {
208	      case "pose": {
209	        if (message.seq <= conn.poseSeq) return; // stale or replayed
210	        conn.poseSeq = message.seq;
211	        const elapsed = Math.max(1, this.tickCount - conn.lastPoseTick) * TICK_SECONDS;
212	        const { accepted } = this.engine.applyRemotePose(playerId, message, elapsed);
213	        this.engine.setPlayerInput(playerId, { move: message.move, mineHeld: message.mineHeld });
214	        if (accepted) {
215	          conn.lastPoseTick = this.tickCount;
216	        } else {
217	          const player = this.engine.state.players.get(playerId);
218	          if (player) {
219	            conn.sink.send(
220	              encodeServerMessage({
221	                t: "forcePose",
222	                x: player.position.x,
223	                y: player.position.y,
224	                z: player.position.z,
225	                yaw: player.yaw,
226	                pitch: player.pitch
227	              })
228	            );
229	          }
230	        }
231	        return;
232	      }
233	      case "cmd": {
234	        if (conn.budget.cmd >= 60) return; // per-second flood guard
235	        conn.budget.cmd += 1;
236	        // Apply the claimed eye pose (same clamps as the stream) so the
237	        // command's raycast happens from where the client actually aimed.
238	        const elapsed = Math.max(1, this.tickCount - conn.lastPoseTick) * TICK_SECONDS;
239	        this.engine.applyRemotePose(playerId, { ...message.pose, onGround: this.engine.state.players.get(playerId)?.onGround ?? false }, elapsed);
240	        this.engine.dispatch(message.cmd, playerId);
241	        return;
242	      }
243	      case "chat": {
244	        if (conn.budget.chat >= 3) return;
245	        conn.budget.chat += 1;
246	        this.broadcast({ t: "chat", from: playerId, name: conn.name, text: message.text });
247	        return;
248	      }
249	      case "ping": {
250	        conn.sink.send(encodeServerMessage({ t: "pong", id: message.id, tMs: message.tMs, serverTick: this.tickCount }));
251	        return;
252	      }
253	      case "resync": {
254	        conn.sink.send(await gzipWorldSync(this.buildWorldSync()));
255	        conn.shadow = null; // resend the full self-delta next tick
256	        return;
257	      }
258	      case "hello":
259	        return; // already admitted; ignore
260	    }
261	  }
262	
263	  /** Drains the room for shutdown: persist + close every socket. */
264	  async shutdown(): Promise<void> {
265	    this.ticker?.stop();
266	    for (const conn of this.clients.values()) conn.sink.close(CLOSE_SERVER_SHUTDOWN, "server restarting");
267	    for (const playerId of [...this.clients.keys()]) this.leave(playerId);
268	    await this.persist();
269	  }
270	
271	  /** Persists the full world (live players merged with offline slices). */
272	  async persist(): Promise<void> {
273	    const save = this.engine.serialize();
274	    for (const [id, saved] of this.offlinePlayers) {
275	      if (!save.players.some((p) => p.id === id)) save.players.push(saved);
276	    }
277	    const bun = Bun as unknown as { gzipSync(d: Uint8Array): Uint8Array };
278	    const blob = bun.gzipSync(new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(save)));
279	    await this.persistence.storeWorld(this.worldId, blob, save.version);
280	    this.dirtySinceStore = false;
281	  }
282	
283	  // ── internals ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
284	
285	  private tick(dt: number): void {
286	    const started = this.now();
287	    this.tickCount += 1;
288	    if (this.tickCount % 20 === 0) {
289	      for (const conn of this.clients.values()) conn.budget = { cmd: 0, chat: 0 };
290	    }
291	
292	    this.engine.step(dt);
293	    const events = this.engine.consumeEvents();
294	    const blocks = this.engine.state.blockChanges.drainEdits();
295	    if (events.some((e) => e.type === "blockPlaced" || e.type === "blockBroken" || e.type === "explosion")) this.dirtySinceStore = true;
296	
297	    const mobPoses = this.collectMobPoses(false);
298	    const day = this.tickCount % DAY_INTERVAL_TICKS === 0 ? this.engine.state.dayClock : undefined;
299	
300	    for (const conn of this.clients.values()) {
301	      const buffered = conn.sink.bufferedAmount();
302	      if (buffered > BACKPRESSURE_KICK_BYTES) {
303	        conn.slowStrikes += 1;
304	        if (conn.slowStrikes > BACKPRESSURE_KICK_STRIKES) {
305	          conn.sink.close(CLOSE_SLOW_CLIENT, "client cannot keep up");
306	          this.leave(conn.playerId);
307	        }
308	        continue;
309	      }
310	      conn.slowStrikes = 0;
311	      const shed = buffered > BACKPRESSURE_SOFT_BYTES;
312	      const message: TickMessage = {
313	        t: "tick",
314	        n: this.tickCount,
315	        ...(blocks.length > 0 ? { blocks } : {}),
316	        ev: events,
317	        pp: shed ? [] : this.collectPlayerPoses(conn.playerId),
318	        mp: shed ? [] : mobPoses,
319	        ...(day !== undefined ? { day } : {}),
320	        ...(this.buildSelfDelta(conn) ?? {})
321	      };
322	      conn.sink.send(encodeServerMessage(message));
323	    }
324	
325	    if (this.tickCount % KEYFRAME_INTERVAL_TICKS === 0 && this.clients.size > 0) {
326	      this.broadcast({ t: "mobsKeyframe", n: this.tickCount, mobs: this.collectMobPoses(true) });
327	    }
328	    if (this.tickCount % PERSIST_INTERVAL_TICKS === 0 && this.dirtySinceStore) {
329	      void this.persist();
330	    }
331	    this.slowestTickMs = Math.max(this.slowestTickMs * 0.99, this.now() - started);
332	  }
333	
334	  private roster(): RosterEntry[] {
335	    const out: RosterEntry[] = [];
336	    for (const conn of this.clients.values()) {
337	      const player = this.engine.state.players.get(conn.playerId);
338	      if (player) out.push(this.rosterEntry(player, conn));
339	    }
340	    return out;
341	  }
342	
343	  private rosterEntry(player: PlayerState, conn: ClientConn): RosterEntry {
344	    return {
345	      id: player.id,
346	      name: conn.name,
347	      skinId: conn.skinId,
348	      x: player.position.x,
349	      y: player.position.y,
350	      z: player.position.z,
351	      yaw: player.yaw
352	    };
353	  }
354	
355	  private buildWorldSync(): WorldSync {
356	    const state = this.engine.state;
357	    return {
358	      t: "worldSync",
359	      tick: this.tickCount,
360	      dayClock: state.dayClock,
361	      changes: state.blockChanges.changes(),
362	      blockEntities: serializeContainers(state.containers),
363	      lootedChests: serializeLootedChests(state.lootedWorldgenChests),
364	      mobs: serializeMobs(state.mobs),
365	      liveMobs: this.collectMobPoses(true),
366	      vehicles: serializeVehicles(state.vehicles),
367	      players: this.roster()
368	    };
369	  }
370	
371	  private collectPlayerPoses(except: string): PlayerPose[] {
372	    const out: PlayerPose[] = [];
373	    for (const player of this.engine.state.players.values()) {
374	      if (player.id === except) continue;
375	      out.push({ id: player.id, x: player.position.x, y: player.position.y, z: player.position.z, yaw: player.yaw, pitch: player.pitch });
376	    }
377	    return out;
378	  }
379	
380	  private collectMobPoses(keyframe: boolean): MobPose[] {
381	    const out: MobPose[] = [];
382	    for (const mob of this.engine.state.mobs) {
383	      const shadow = this.mobShadow.get(mob.id);
384	      const moved =
385	        !shadow ||
386	        (mob.position.x - shadow.x) ** 2 + (mob.position.y - shadow.y) ** 2 + (mob.position.z - shadow.z) ** 2 > MOB_DEADBAND_SQ ||
387	        mob.hp !== shadow.hp;
388	      // Delta frames go at half rate (10 Hz) — keyframes always carry everything.
389	      if (!keyframe && (!moved || this.tickCount % 2 !== 0)) continue;
390	      this.mobShadow.set(mob.id, { x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z, hp: mob.hp });
391	      out.push({
392	        id: mob.id,
393	        kind: mob.kind,
394	        hostile: mob.hostile,
395	        x: mob.position.x,
396	        y: mob.position.y,
397	        z: mob.position.z,
398	        yaw: mob.yaw,
399	        hp: mob.hp,
400	        moveSpeed: mob.moveSpeed
401	      });
402	    }
403	    if (keyframe) {
404	      const alive = new Set(this.engine.state.mobs.map((m) => m.id));
405	      for (const id of this.mobShadow.keys()) if (!alive.has(id)) this.mobShadow.delete(id);
406	    }
407	    return out;
408	  }
409	
410	  private buildSelfDelta(conn: ClientConn): { self: SelfDelta } | null {
411	    const player = this.engine.state.players.get(conn.playerId);
412	    if (!player) return null;
413	    const effectsKey = JSON.stringify(serializeEffects(player.effects));
414	    const respawnSeconds = Math.ceil(player.respawnTimer);
415	    const previous = conn.shadow;
416	    const delta: SelfDelta = {};
417	    if (!previous || previous.inventory !== player.inventory) delta.inventorySlots = inventorySlotsSnapshot(player.inventory);
418	    if (!previous || previous.equippedArmor !== player.equippedArmor) delta.equippedArmor = serializeEquippedArmor(player.equippedArmor);
419	    if (!previous || previous.selectedSlot !== player.selectedSlot) delta.selectedSlot = player.selectedSlot;
420	    if (!previous || previous.hearts !== player.hearts) delta.hearts = player.hearts;
421	    if (!previous || previous.hunger !== player.hunger) delta.hunger = player.hunger;
422	    if (!previous || Math.abs(previous.oxygen - player.oxygen) > 0.24) delta.oxygen = player.oxygen;
423	    if (!previous || previous.xp !== player.xp) delta.xp = player.xp;
424	    if (!previous || previous.isDead !== player.isDead) delta.isDead = player.isDead;
425	    if (!previous || previous.respawnSeconds !== respawnSeconds) delta.respawnSeconds = respawnSeconds;
426	    if (!previous || previous.gameMode !== player.gameMode) delta.gameMode = player.gameMode;
427	    if (!previous || previous.sleeping !== player.sleeping) delta.sleeping = player.sleeping;
428	    if (!previous || previous.effectsKey !== effectsKey) delta.effects = serializeEffects(player.effects);
429	    conn.shadow = {
430	      inventory: player.inventory,
431	      equippedArmor: player.equippedArmor,
432	      selectedSlot: player.selectedSlot,
433	      hearts: player.hearts,
434	      hunger: player.hunger,
435	      oxygen: player.oxygen,
436	      xp: player.xp,
437	      isDead: player.isDead,
438	      respawnSeconds,
439	      gameMode: player.gameMode,
440	      sleeping: player.sleeping,
441	      effectsKey
442	    };
443	    return Object.keys(delta).length > 0 ? { self: delta } : null;
444	  }
445	
446	  private broadcast(message: ServerMessage, except?: string): void {
447	    const encoded = encodeServerMessage(message);
448	    for (const conn of this.clients.values()) {
449	      if (conn.playerId === except) continue;
450	      conn.sink.send(encoded);
451	    }
452	  }
453	}

1	import { Room } from "./room";
2	import type { Persistence } from "./persistence";
3	
4	/**
5	 * The rooms this process hosts: loaded on first join, evicted (persist +
6	 * stop) after sitting empty. MAX_ROOMS bounds memory (~74 MB of world per
7	 * room); joins beyond it are refused at the door so an overloaded process
8	 * degrades by rejecting, never by thrashing.
9	 */
10	
11	const IDLE_EVICT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
12	
13	export class RoomRegistry {
14	  private readonly rooms = new Map<string, Room>();
15	  private readonly loading = new Map<string, Promise<Room | null>>();
16	  private sweeper: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
17	
18	  constructor(
19	    private readonly persistence: Persistence,
20	    private readonly maxRooms: number,
21	    private readonly now: () => number = () => Date.now()
22	  ) {}
23	
24	  startSweeper(): void {
25	    this.sweeper ??= setInterval(() => void this.sweepIdle(), 30_000);
26	  }
27	
28	  /** The room for a world, loading it from persistence on first use. Null: unknown world or at capacity. */
29	  async getOrLoad(worldId: string): Promise<Room | null> {
30	    const existing = this.rooms.get(worldId);
31	    if (existing) return existing;
32	    const inFlight = this.loading.get(worldId);
33	    if (inFlight) return inFlight;
34	    if (this.rooms.size >= this.maxRooms) return null;
35	
36	    const promise = (async (): Promise<Room | null> => {
37	      const record = await this.persistence.loadWorld(worldId);
38	      if (!record) return null;
39	      const room = new Room(record, this.persistence, this.now);
40	      room.start();
41	      this.rooms.set(worldId, room);
42	      return room;
43	    })().finally(() => this.loading.delete(worldId));
44	    this.loading.set(worldId, promise);
45	    return promise;
46	  }
47	
48	  diagnostics(): Array<ReturnType<Room["diagnostics"]>> {
49	    return [...this.rooms.values()].map((room) => room.diagnostics());
50	  }
51	
52	  async sweepIdle(): Promise<void> {
53	    for (const [worldId, room] of this.rooms) {
54	      if (room.playerCount() === 0 && room.emptySinceMs !== null && this.now() - room.emptySinceMs > IDLE_EVICT_MS) {
55	        this.rooms.delete(worldId);
56	        await room.shutdown();
57	      }
58	    }
59	  }
60	
61	  async shutdownAll(): Promise<void> {
62	    if (this.sweeper) clearInterval(this.sweeper);
63	    const rooms = [...this.rooms.values()];
64	    this.rooms.clear();
65	    await Promise.all(rooms.map((room) => room.shutdown()));
66	  }
67	}
68

1	import type { Command } from "@/lib/game/engine/commands";
2	import type { GameEvent } from "@/lib/game/engine/state";
3	import type { SavedContainer, SavedMob, SavedPlayer, SavedVehicle } from "@/lib/game/types";
4	
5	/**
6	 * The client↔game-server wire protocol. Versioned as a whole: a client built
7	 * against a different PROTOCOL_VERSION is refused at the door (its join
8	 * ticket carries the number), so mid-session format drift can't happen.
9	 *
10	 * v1 is JSON envelopes discriminated on `t`, except the one big payload —
11	 * the join world-sync — which travels as a gzipped binary frame (see
12	 * codec.ts). The envelope layout deliberately leaves room to move the hot
13	 * paths (pose/tick) to packed binary later without renegotiating anything.
14	 *
15	 * Validation is hand-rolled and TOTAL (the save.ts house style): the server
16	 * feeds hostile bytes through these readers and gets a typed message or
17	 * null — never an exception, never a partially-checked object.
18	 */
19	export const PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1;
20	
21	// ── close codes (WebSocket application range) ────────────────────────────────
22	export const CLOSE_BAD_TICKET = 4000;
23	export const CLOSE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH = 4001;
24	export const CLOSE_ROOM_FULL = 4002;
25	export const CLOSE_KICKED = 4003;

31	export const ROOM_CAPACITY = 8;
32	
33	// ── client → server ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
34	
35	/** First frame on the socket: the join ticket (minted by the web API) + the client's protocol. */
36	export type HelloMessage = { t: "hello"; ticket: string; protocol: number };

155	export type ServerMessage =

166	// ── validators (client → server only: the server is the hostile-input side) ──
167	
168	const isNum = (v: unknown): v is number => typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v);
169	const isBool = (v: unknown): v is boolean => typeof v === "boolean";

172	function readMove(v: unknown): PoseMessage["move"] | null {
173	  if (!v || typeof v !== "object") return null;
174	  const m = v as Record<string, unknown>;
175	  const keys = ["forward", "back", "left", "right", "jump", "sprint", "crouch"] as const;
176	  const out = {} as Record<(typeof keys)[number], boolean>;
177	  for (const key of keys) {
178	    if (!isBool(m[key])) return null;
179	    out[key] = m[key] as boolean;
180	  }
181	  return out;

184	function readEyePose(v: unknown): CmdMessage["pose"] | null {
185	  if (!v || typeof v !== "object") return null;

187	  if (!isNum(p.x) || !isNum(p.y) || !isNum(p.z) || !isNum(p.yaw) || !isNum(p.pitch)) return null;

191	/**
192	 * Command allow-list: every dispatchable type with per-field checks. Unknown
193	 * or malformed commands are dropped here — dispatch never sees them. Local-
194	 * presentation commands (pause/debug/camera) are deliberately absent: they
195	 * have no business on a wire.
196	 */
197	export function readCommand(v: unknown): Command | null {
198	  if (!v || typeof v !== "object") return null;
199	  const c = v as Record<string, unknown>;
200	  switch (c.type) {
201	    case "selectSlot":
202	      return isNum(c.index) ? { type: "selectSlot", index: Math.floor(c.index) } : null;
203	    case "craft":
204	      return isStr(c.recipeId) ? { type: "craft", recipeId: c.recipeId } : null;
205	    case "swapSlots":
206	      return isNum(c.from) && isNum(c.to) ? { type: "swapSlots", from: Math.floor(c.from), to: Math.floor(c.to) } : null;
207	    case "moveStack":
208	      return isNum(c.from) && isNum(c.to) ? { type: "moveStack", from: Math.floor(c.from), to: Math.floor(c.to) } : null;
209	    case "toggleEquipArmor":
210	      return isNum(c.index) ? { type: "toggleEquipArmor", index: Math.floor(c.index) } : null;
211	    case "unequipArmor":
212	      return c.slot === "helmet" || c.slot === "chestplate" || c.slot === "leggings" || c.slot === "boots" ? { type: "unequipArmor", slot: c.slot } : null;
213	    case "anvilRename":
214	      return isStr(c.name) ? { type: "anvilRename", name: c.name.slice(0, 64) } : null;
215	    case "enchant":
216	      return isStr(c.enchant) ? ({ type: "enchant", enchant: c.enchant } as Command) : null;
217	    case "creativeGiveItem":
218	      return isStr(c.itemId) ? { type: "creativeGiveItem", itemId: c.itemId } : null;
219	    case "setGameMode":
220	      return isStr(c.mode) ? ({ type: "setGameMode", mode: c.mode } as Command) : null;
221	    case "setDifficulty":
222	      return isStr(c.difficulty) ? ({ type: "setDifficulty", difficulty: c.difficulty } as Command) : null;
223	    case "toggleInventory":
224	    case "toggleAdvancements":
225	    case "eatFood":
226	    case "drinkPotion":
227	    case "anvilCombine":
228	    case "anvilRepair":
229	    case "grindstoneStrip":
230	    case "placeBlock":
231	    case "attack":
232	    case "toggleFlight":
233	    case "unstuck":
234	    case "respawn":

239	      return null;

244	export function readClientMessage(v: unknown): ClientMessage | null {
245	  if (!v || typeof v !== "object") return null;

247	  switch (m.t) {

250	    case "pose": {

1	/**
2	 * Join tickets: the only trust link between the web app and the game server.
3	 *
4	 * The Next.js API (which can read the browser's session cookie) mints a
5	 * short-lived HS256 token naming the player and the world; the game server
6	 * (which never sees cookies) verifies the signature with the shared
7	 * GAME_TICKET_SECRET and admits the socket. Stateless by design — the two
8	 * deployments never talk to each other at runtime.
9	 *
10	 * Web Crypto only (no jwt dependency): runs identically on Vercel's Node
11	 * runtime, Bun, and the browser-adjacent test environments.
12	 */
13	
14	export const TICKET_TTL_SECONDS = 60;
15	
16	export type TicketClaims = {
17	  /** The player's user id (becomes their PlayerId in the world). */
18	  sub: string;
19	  /** The world (= room) this ticket admits into. */
20	  wid: string;
21	  /** Display name at mint time. */
22	  name: string;
23	  /** Skin palette id, if the account has one. */
24	  skinId: string | null;
25	  /** Room role — the owner may kick/close. */
26	  role: "owner" | "member";
27	  /** Protocol version the client was built against. */
28	  pv: number;
29	  iat: number;
30	  exp: number;
31	};
32	
33	const encoder = new TextEncoder();
34	
35	function base64url(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
36	  let binary = "";
37	  for (const b of bytes) binary += String.fromCharCode(b);
38	  return btoa(binary).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
39	}
40	
41	function fromBase64url(text: string): Uint8Array {
42	  const padded = text
43	    .replace(/-/g, "+")
44	    .replace(/_/g, "/")
45	    .padEnd(Math.ceil(text.length / 4) * 4, "=");
46	  const binary = atob(padded);
47	  const out = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
48	  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i += 1) out[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
49	  return out;
50	}
51	
52	async function hmacKey(secret: string): Promise<CryptoKey> {
53	  return crypto.subtle.importKey("raw", encoder.encode(secret), { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" }, false, ["sign", "verify"]);
54	}
55	
56	/** Mints a signed ticket. `now` is injectable for expiry tests. */
57	export async function signTicket(claims: Omit<TicketClaims, "iat" | "exp">, secret: string, now: number = Date.now()): Promise<string> {
58	  const iat = Math.floor(now / 1000);
59	  const full: TicketClaims = { ...claims, iat, exp: iat + TICKET_TTL_SECONDS };
60	  const header = base64url(encoder.encode(JSON.stringify({ alg: "HS256", typ: "JWT" })));
61	  const payload = base64url(encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(full)));
62	  const signature = await crypto.subtle.sign("HMAC", await hmacKey(secret), encoder.encode(`${header}.${payload}`));
63	  return `${header}.${payload}.${base64url(new Uint8Array(signature))}`;
64	}
65	
66	/**
67	 * Verifies signature and expiry, returning the claims — or null for anything
68	 * malformed, tampered, or stale. Total: never throws on hostile input.
69	 */
70	export async function verifyTicket(ticket: string, secret: string, now: number = Date.now()): Promise<TicketClaims | null> {
71	  try {
72	    const parts = ticket.split(".");
73	    if (parts.length !== 3) return null;
74	    const [header, payload, signature] = parts;
75	    const valid = await crypto.subtle.verify(
76	      "HMAC",
77	      await hmacKey(secret),
78	      fromBase64url(signature) as unknown as ArrayBuffer,
79	      encoder.encode(`${header}.${payload}`)
80	    );
81	    if (!valid) return null;
82	    const claims = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(fromBase64url(payload))) as TicketClaims;
83	    if (typeof claims.sub !== "string" || !claims.sub) return null;
84	    if (typeof claims.wid !== "string" || !claims.wid) return null;
85	    if (claims.role !== "owner" && claims.role !== "member") return null;
86	    if (typeof claims.pv !== "number") return null;
87	    if (typeof claims.exp !== "number" || Math.floor(now / 1000) >= claims.exp) return null;
88	    return claims;
89	  } catch {
90	    return null;
91	  }
92	}
