   }\n    if (blocks.length > 0) state.worldMeshDirty = true;\n  };\n\n  // ── inbound frame processing (latency-shifted) ──────────────────────────────\n  const onServerFrame = (data: unknown) => {\n    if (simulatedLatencyMs > 0) {\n      setTimeout(() => void processServerFrame(data), simulatedLatencyMs);\n      return;\n    }\n    void processServerFrame(data);\n  };\n\n  async function processServerFrame(data: unknown): Promise<void> {\n    if (typeof data !== \"string\") {\n      const sync = await gunzipWorldSync(new Uint8Array(data as ArrayBuffer));\n      if (sync) {\n        applyWorldSync(sync);\n        setStatus(\"online\");\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n    const message = decodeServerFrame(data);\n    if (!message) return;\n    switch (message.t) {\n      case \"tick\": {\n        serverTickTimeMs = message.n * TICK_SECONDS * 1000;\n        if (message.blocks) applyBlocks(message.blocks);\n        if (message.day !== undefined) state.dayClock = message.day;\n        if (message.self) applySelfDelta(message.self);\n        for (const pose of message.pp) {\n          upsertRemotePlayer(pose.id, names.get(pose.id) ?? \"player\");\n          let buffer = playerBuffers.get(pose.id);\n          if (!buffer) {\n            buffer = createPoseBuffer();\n            playerBuffers.set(pose.id, buffer);\n          }\n          buffer.push({ tMs: serverTickTimeMs, ...pose });\n        }\n        for (const pose of message.mp) {\n          upsertReplicaMob(pose);\n          mobBuffers.get(pose.id)?.push({ tMs: serverTickTimeMs, x: pose.x, y: pose.y, z: pose.z, yaw: pose.yaw });\n        }\n        for (const gameEvent of message.ev) {\n          pendingEvents.push(gameEvent as GameEvent);\n          callbacks.onEvent?.(gameEvent as GameEvent);\n        }\n        return;\n      }\n      case \"mobsKeyframe\": {\n        const alive = new Set(message.mobs.map((m) => m.id));\n        state.mobs = state.mobs.filter((m) => alive.has(m.id));\n        for (const id of [...mobBuffers.keys()]) if (!alive.has(id)) mobBuffers.delete(id);\n        const tMs = message.n * TICK_SECONDS * 1000;\n        for (const pose of message.mobs) {\n          upsertReplicaMob(pose);\n          mobBuffers.get(pose.id)?.push({ tMs, x: pose.x, y: pose.y, z: pose.z, yaw: pose.yaw });\n        }\n        return;\n      }\n      case \"playerJoined\": {\n        upsertRemotePlayer(message.player.id, message.player.name);\n        const joined = state.players.get(message.player.id);\n        joined?.position.set(message.player.x, message.player.y, message.player.z);\n        return;\n      }\n      case \"playerLeft\": {\n        if (message.id !== playerId) engine.removePlayer(message.id);\n        playerBuffers.delete(message.id);\n        engine.consumeEvents();\n        return;\n      }\n      case \"container\": {\n        const restored = restoreInventorySlots({ id: \"container\", inventorySlots: message.slots });\n        if (restored) state.containers.set(message.index, restored);\n        return;\n      }\n      case \"chat\":\n        callbacks.onChat?.(message);\n        for (const listener of chatListeners) listener(message);\n        return;\n      case \"pong\":\n        clock.onPong(message.tMs, performance.now(), message.serverTick);\n        return;\n      case \"forcePose\":\n        self.position.set(message.x, message.y, message.z);\n        self.velocity.set(0, 0, 0);\n        return;\n      case \"welcome\":\n        return;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // ── reconnect ladder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  let reconnectAttempt = 0;\n  let reconnectTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;\n\n  const onSocketClosed = (code: number, reason: string) => {\n    if (disposed) return;\n    if (FATAL_CLOSES.has(code) || !options.reconnect) {\n      setStatus(\"closed\", `${code} ${reason}`);\n      return;\n    }\n    scheduleReconnect();\n  };\n\n  const scheduleReconnect = () => {\n    if (disposed) return;\n    if (reconnectAttempt >= RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS.length) {\n      setStatus(\"closed\", \"could not reconnect\");\n      return;\n    }\n    const delay = RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS[reconnectAttempt];\n    reconnectAttempt += 1;\n    setStatus(\"reconnecting\", `attempt ${reconnectAttempt}`);\n    reconnectTimer = setTimeout(() => void tryReconnectOnce(), delay);\n  };\n\n  async function tryReconnectOnce(): Promise<void> {\n    if (disposed || !options.reconnect) return;\n    const grant = await options.reconnect();\n    if (disposed) return;\n    if (!grant) {\n      scheduleReconnect();\n      return;\n    }\n    try {\n      const resumed = await handshake(grant.ticket, grant.url);\n      if (disposed) return;\n      // Same room, same id: keep the replica; the world-sync that follows\n      // re-seeds it. Just refresh the roster and the server-time anchor.\n      serverTickTimeMs = resumed.tick * TICK_SECONDS * 1000;\n      applyRoster(resumed.players);\n      reconnectAttempt = 0;\n      setStatus(\"syncing\");\n    } catch {\n      scheduleReconnect();\n    }\n  }\n\n  // ── outbound ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n  let seq = 0;\n  let lastPoseSentMs = 0;\n  let lastPingMs = 0;\n\n  const sendCmd = (command: Command) => {\n    seq += 1;\n    delayedSend(\n      encodeClientMessage({\n        t: \"cmd\",\n        seq,\n        cmd: command,\n        pose: { x: self.position.x, y: self.position.y + 1.62, z: self.position.z, yaw: self.yaw, pitch: self.pitch }\n      })\n    );\n  };\n\n  const session: NetworkSession = {\n    engine,\n    playerId,\n    subscribeChat(listener) {\n      chatListeners.add(listener);\n      return () => chatListeners.delete(listener);\n    },\n    subscribeStatus(listener) {\n      statusListeners.add(listener);\n      return () => statusListeners.delete(listener);\n    },\n    drainEvents: () => pendingEvents.splice(0, pendingEvents.length),\n    status: () => status,\n    rttMs: () => clock.rttMs(),\n    playerName: (id) => names.get(id) ?? \"player\",\n\n    dispatch(command) {\n      engine.dispatch(command); // routeDispatch handles the local/network split\n    },\n\n    applyLook(deltaYaw, deltaPitch) {\n      engine.applyLook(deltaYaw, deltaPitch);\n    },\n\n    sendChat(text) {\n      if (text.trim()) delayedSend(encodeClientMessage({ t: \"chat\", text: text.slice(0, 256) }));\n    },\n\n    setSimulatedLatency(ms) {\n      simulatedLatencyMs = Math.max(0, Math.floor(ms));\n    },\n    simulatedLatency: () => simulatedLatencyMs,\n\n    afterFrame(nowMs) {\n      const open = ws?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN;\n      // Pose stream at tick rate.\n      if (open && nowMs - lastPoseSentMs >= TICK_SECONDS * 1000) {\n        lastPoseSentMs = nowMs;\n        seq += 1;\n        delayedSend(\n          encodeClientMessage({\n            t: \"pose\",\n            seq,\n            x: self.position.x,\n            y: self.position.y,\n            z: self.position.z,\n            yaw: self.yaw,\n            pitch: self.pitch,\n            onGround: self.onGround,\n            move: self.input.move,\n            mineHeld: self.input.mineHeld\n          })\n        );\n      }\n      if (open && nowMs - lastPingMs >= 2000) {\n        lastPingMs = nowMs;\n        delayedSend(encodeClientMessage({ t: \"ping\", id: seq, tMs: nowMs }));\n      }\n      // Interpolation: remote entities render ~125ms in the past.\n      const renderTime = (clock.ready() ? clock.estimatedServerTimeMs(nowMs) : serverTickTimeMs) - INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MS;\n      for (const [id, buffer] of playerBuffers) {\n        const player = state.players.get(id);\n        const pose = buffer.sample(renderTime);\n        if (player && pose) {\n          player.position.set(pose.x, pose.y, pose.z);\n          player.yaw = pose.yaw;\n          player.pitch = pose.pitch;\n        }\n      }\n      for (const [id, buffer] of mobBuffers) {\n        const mob = state.mobs.find((m) => m.id === id);\n        const pose = buffer.sample(renderTime);\n        if (mob && pose) {\n          mob.position.set(pose.x, pose.y, pose.z);\n          mob.yaw = pose.yaw;\n        }\n      }\n    },\n\n    dispose() {\n      disposed = true;\n      if (reconnectTimer) clearTimeout(reconnectTimer);\n      setStatus(\"closed\", \"left world\");\n      try {\n        ws?.close(1000, \"leaving\");\n      } catch {\n        /* already closed */\n      }\n    }\n  };\n  return session;\n}\n"

3	/**
4	 * Frame encoding. v1: JSON text frames for everything except the join
5	 * world-sync, which is one gzipped binary frame (a fresh world's block diff
6	 * is tiny, but a terraformed one isn't — and block diffs gzip extremely
7	 * well). Both runtimes are covered: Bun's native zlib on the server,
8	 * CompressionStream/DecompressionStream in the browser.
9	 */

11	export function encodeServerMessage(message: ServerMessage): string {
12	  return JSON.stringify(message);
13	}

15	export function encodeClientMessage(message: ClientMessage): string {
16	  return JSON.stringify(message);
17	}

19	/** Parses + validates one client text frame; null for binary/garbage/off-spec. */
20	export function decodeClientFrame(data: unknown): ClientMessage | null {
21	  if (typeof data !== "string") return null;
22	  try {
23	    return readClientMessage(JSON.parse(data));
24	  } catch {
25	    return null;
26	  }
27	}

29	/** Parses one server text frame (the client trusts its server; shape only). */
30	export function decodeServerFrame(data: unknown): ServerMessage | null {
31	  if (typeof data !== "string") return null;
32	  try {
33	    const parsed = JSON.parse(data) as ServerMessage;
34	    return parsed && typeof parsed === "object" && typeof parsed.t === "string" ? parsed : null;
35	  } catch {
36	    return null;
37	  }
38	}

40	type BunGlobal = { gzipSync(data: Uint8Array): Uint8Array; gunzipSync(data: Uint8Array): Uint8Array };
41	const bunZlib = (): BunGlobal | null => (typeof Bun !== "undefined" ? (Bun as unknown as BunGlobal) : null);

43	/** Gzips the world-sync payload into the one binary frame of the protocol. */
44	export async function gzipWorldSync(sync: WorldSync): Promise<Uint8Array> {
45	  const json = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(sync));
46	  const bun = bunZlib();
47	  if (bun) return bun.gzipSync(json);
48	  const stream = new Blob([json]).stream().pipeThrough(new CompressionStream("gzip"));
49	  return new Uint8Array(await new Response(stream).arrayBuffer());
50	}
51	
52	/** Reverses gzipWorldSync. Null for garbage (a client should resync, not crash). */
53	export async function gunzipWorldSync(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<WorldSync | null> {
54	  try {
55	    const bun = bunZlib();
56	    let json: Uint8Array;
57	    if (bun) {
58	      json = bun.gunzipSync(bytes);
59	    } else {
60	      const stream = new Blob([bytes as BlobPart]).stream().pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream("gzip"));
61	      json = new Uint8Array(await new Response(stream).arrayBuffer());
62	    }
63	    const parsed = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(json)) as WorldSync;
64	    return parsed && parsed.t === "worldSync" && Array.isArray(parsed.changes) ? parsed : null;
65	  } catch {
66	    return null;
67	  }
68	}
69	
```

import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { PROTOCOL_VERSION, type ServerMessage, type WorldSync } from "@/lib/net/protocol";
import { gunzipWorldSync } from "@/lib/net/codec";
import type { TicketClaims } from "@/lib/net/tickets";
import { createMemoryPersistence, parseSaveBlob } from "./persistence";
import { Room, type ClientSink } from "./room";

/**
 * The room's contracts, exercised through fake sockets against the in-memory
 * persistence — every joined client is a scripted sink, every tick is driven
 * by hand (no real timers), and the world is a real (small… no — full-size)
 * engine. Room construction takes a couple of seconds (worldgen); the suite
 * shares one room per describe where isolation allows.
 */

type Frame = { kind: "text"; message: ServerMessage } | { kind: "binary"; sync: Promise<WorldSync | null> } | { kind: "close"; code: number };

function fakeSink(): ClientSink & { frames: Frame[]; messagesOf<T extends ServerMessage["t"]>(t: T): Array<Extract<ServerMessage, { t: T }>> } {
  const frames: Frame[] = [];
  return {
    frames,
    send(data) {
      if (typeof data === "string") frames.push({ kind: "text", message: JSON.parse(data) as ServerMessage });
      else frames.push({ kind: "binary", sync: gunzipWorldSync(data) });
    },
    close(code) {
      frames.push({ kind: "close", code });
    },
    bufferedAmount: () => 0,
    messagesOf<T extends ServerMessage["t"]>(t: T) {
      return frames
        .filter((f): f is Extract<Frame, { kind: "text" }> => f.kind === "text")
        .map((f) => f.message)
        .filter((m): m is Extract<ServerMessage, { t: T }> => m.t === t);
    }
  };
}

function claimsFor(id: string, wid: string, role: "owner" | "member" = "member"): TicketClaims {
  return { sub: id, wid, name: id.toUpperCase(), skinId: null, role, pv: PROTOCOL_VERSION, iat: 0, exp: 9999999999 };
}

const move = { forward: false, back: false, left: false, right: false, jump: false, sprint: false, crouch: false };

async function makeRoom(worldId = "w1") {
  const persistence = createMemoryPersistence();
  const record = await persistence.loadWorld(worldId);
  const room = new Room(record!, persistence, () => 0);
  return { room, persistence };
}

describe("room lifecycle", () => {
  test("join → welcome + gzipped world sync; a second join is announced to the first", async () => {
    const { room } = await makeRoom();
    const a = fakeSink();
    expect(await room.join(claimsFor("alice", "w1", "owner"), a)).toBe(true);

    const welcome = a.messagesOf("welcome")[0];
    expect(welcome).toMatchObject({ protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION, playerId: "alice", worldId: "w1" });
    expect(welcome.seed).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    const binary = a.frames.find((f) => f.kind === "binary");
    expect(binary).toBeTruthy();
    const sync = await (binary as Extract<Frame, { kind: "binary" }>).sync;
    expect(sync).toMatchObject({ t: "worldSync" });
    expect(Array.isArray(sync!.changes)).toBe(true);

    const b = fakeSink();
    await room.join(claimsFor("bob", "w1"), b);
    expect(a.messagesOf("playerJoined")[0]?.player.id).toBe("bob");
```

/**
 * A tiny CLI game client for poking a live game server (local or staging)
 * without a browser:
 *
 *   GAME_TICKET_SECRET=… bun scripts/netProbe.ts ws://localhost:8080 my-world
 *
 * Mints its own ticket (so the secret must match the server's), joins, walks
 * forward for a few seconds, and logs every message class it sees.
 */
import { PROTOCOL_VERSION } from "@/lib/net/protocol";
import { gunzipWorldSync } from "@/lib/net/codec";
import { signTicket } from "@/lib/net/tickets";

const [, , urlArg, worldArg] = process.argv;
const url = urlArg ?? "ws://localhost:8080";
const worldId = worldArg ?? "probe-world";
const secret = process.env.GAME_TICKET_SECRET;
if (!secret) {
  console.error("GAME_TICKET_SECRET required (must match the server)");
  process.exit(1);
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/scripts/replay.ts",
  "content": "/**\n * Offline replay of a room's command log — reconstructs the deterministic,\n * player-driven half of a world's state without a live server, for debugging\n * \"how did we get here?\" from a `/rooms/:id/log` dump:\n *\n *   curl -H \"authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \\\n *     http://localhost:8080/rooms/my-world/log > dump.json\n *   bun scripts/replay.ts dump.json\n *\n * It boots a fresh authoritative engine from the dump's seed/world settings,\n * seats every player that appears, and steps tick-by-tick, applying each\n * logged command from its claimed eye pose (exactly as the room did) and each\n * pose anchor. It then prints the resulting player positions, inventory\n * fingerprints, and block-edit count.\n *\n * Caveat: mob/spawn behavior is NOT reproduced — the live room uses an\n * unseeded RNG, so only command-driven state (edits, inventory, movement) is\n * deterministic. That is exactly the state this tool is for.\n */\nimport { GameEngine } from \"@/lib/game/engine/GameEngine\";\nimport type { CommandLogEntry, RoomLogDump } from \"@/server/room\";\n\nconst path = process.argv[2];\n\nasync function readDump(): Promise<RoomLogDump> {\n  const text = path ? await Bun.file(path).text() : await new Response(Bun.stdin.stream()).text();\n  return JSON.parse(text) as RoomLogDump;\n}\n\nfunction inventoryFingerprint(engine: GameEngine, playerId: string): string {\n  const player = engine.state.players.get(playerId);\n  if (!player) return \"(gone)\";\n  const items = player.inventory.filter((slot) => slot).map((slot) => `${slot!.id}×${slot!.count}`);\n  return items.length ? items.join(\", \") : \"(empty)\";\n}\n\nconst dump = await readDump();\nconsole.log(`replaying room ${dump.worldId}: seed=${dump.seed} type=${dump.worldType} diff=${dump.difficulty} hardcore=${dump.hardcore}`);\nconsole.log(`${dump.entries.length} log entries up to tick ${dump.tick}`);\n\nconst engine = new GameEngine({\n  seed: dump.seed,\n  worldType: dump.worldType as never,\n  difficulty: dump.difficulty as never,\n  hardcore: dump.hardcore,\n  authority: \"server\",\n  headless: true,\n  bootPlayer: false\n});\n\nconst playerIds = [...new Set(dump.entries.map((e) => e.playerId))];\nfor (const id of playerIds) engine.addPlayer({ id });\nconsole.log(`seated ${playerIds.length} player(s): ${playerIds.join(\", \")}`);\n\nconst entries = [...dump.entries].sort((a, b) => a.tick - b.tick);\nif (entries.length === 0) {\n  console.log(\"no entries to replay\");\n  process.exit(0);\n}\n\nconst TICK_DT = 0.05;\nconst applyPose = (entry: CommandLogEntry) => {\n  const onGround = engine.state.players.get(entry.playerId)?.onGround ?? true;\n  engine.applyRemotePose(entry.playerId, { ...entry.pose, onGround }, TICK_DT);\n};\n\nlet cursor = 0;\nlet commandsApplied = 0;\nfor (let tick = entries[0].tick; tick <= entries[entries.length - 1].tick; tick += 1) {\n  engine.step(TICK_DT);\n  while (cursor < entries.length && entries[cursor].tick === tick) {\n    const entry = entries[cursor++];\n    applyPose(entry);\n    if (\"cmd\" in entry) {\n      engine.dispatch(entry.cmd, entry.playerId);\n      commandsApplied += 1;\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nconsole.log(`\\nreplayed ${commandsApplied} command(s); ${engine.state.blockChanges.changes().length} block edit(s) vs the worldgen baseline`);\nfor (const id of playerIds) {\n  const player = engine.state.players.get(id);\n  if (!player) continue;\n  const { x, y, z } = player.position;\n  console.log(`  ${id}: pos=(${x.toFixed(1)}, ${y.toFixed(1)}, ${z.toFixed(1)}) hearts=${player.hearts} xp=${player.xp} inv=[${inventoryFingerprint(engine, id)}]`);\n}\n"
}

48

54	      ws.onmessage = (event) => {

1	import { and, eq } from "drizzle-orm";
2	import type { Db } from "@/db";
3	import { schema } from "@/db";
4	import { WORLDGEN_VERSION } from "@/lib/game/config";
5	import { PROTOCOL_VERSION } from "@/lib/net/protocol";
6	import { signTicket } from "@/lib/net/tickets";
7	
8	/**
9	 * The online worlds domain: every rule the API routes enforce, as pure
10	 * functions over a drizzle Db — unit-tested against PGlite, adapted to HTTP by
11	 * the thin handlers in app/api. All read access is membership-gated; writes
12	 * that shape the world (rename/delete/invite) are owner-gated.
13	 *
14	 * Results use a discriminated `ok` so handlers map failures to status codes
15	 * without exceptions crossing the seam.
16	 */
17	
18	export type WorldSummary = {
19	  id: string;
20	  name: string;
21	  kind: "sp-cloud" | "mp";
22	  seed: number;
23	  worldType: string;
24	  gameMode: string;
25	  difficulty: string;
26	  hardcore: boolean;
27	  worldgenVersion: number;
28	  role: "owner" | "member";
29	  updatedAt: string;
30	};
31	
32	type Failure = { ok: false; error: "not-found" | "forbidden" | "conflict" | "invalid" | "expired" };
33	const fail = (error: Failure["error"]): Failure => ({ ok: false, error });
34	
35	function toSummary(world: typeof schema.worlds.$inferSelect, role: "owner" | "member"): WorldSummary {
36	  return {
37	    id: world.id,
38	    name: world.name,
39	    kind: world.kind,
40	    seed: world.seed,
41	    worldType: world.worldType,
42	    gameMode: world.gameMode,
43	    difficulty: world.difficulty,
44	    hardcore: world.hardcore,
45	    worldgenVersion: world.worldgenVersion,
46	    role,
47	    updatedAt: world.updatedAt.toISOString()
48	  };
49	}
50	
51	/** The caller's membership row for a world, or null. */
52	async function membership(db: Db, userId: string, worldId: string) {
53	  const rows = await db
54	    .select()
55	    .from(schema.worldMembers)
56	    .where(and(eq(schema.worldMembers.worldId, worldId), eq(schema.worldMembers.userId, userId)));
57	  return rows[0] ?? null;
58	}
59	
60	/** Every world the user may play, owner first then most recently updated. */
61	export async function listWorlds(db: Db, userId: string): Promise<WorldSummary[]> {
62	  const rows = await db
63	    .select({ world: schema.worlds, role: schema.worldMembers.role })
64	    .from(schema.worldMembers)
65	    .innerJoin(schema.worlds, eq(schema.worldMembers.worldId, schema.worlds.id))
66	    .where(eq(schema.worldMembers.userId, userId));
67	  return rows
68	    .map(({ world, role }) => toSummary(world, role))
69	    .sort((a, b) => (a.role !== b.role ? (a.role === "owner" ? -1 : 1) : b.updatedAt.localeCompare(a.updatedAt)));
70	}
71	
72	export type CreateWorldInput = {
73	  name: string;
74	  kind: "sp-cloud" | "mp";
75	  seed: number;
76	  worldType?: string;
77	  gameMode?: string;
78	  difficulty?: string;
79	  hardcore?: boolean;
80	};
81	
82	export async function createWorld(db: Db, userId: string, input: CreateWorldInput): Promise<{ ok: true; world: WorldSummary } | Failure> {
83	  const name = input.name?.trim();
84	  if (!name || name.length > 64) return fail("invalid");
85	  if (input.kind !== "sp-cloud" && input.kind !== "mp") return fail("invalid");
86	  if (!Number.isFinite(input.seed)) return fail("invalid");
87	  const id = crypto.randomUUID();
88	  const [world] = await db
89	    .insert(schema.worlds)
90	    .values({
91	      id,
92	      ownerId: userId,
93	      kind: input.kind,
94	      name,
95	      seed: Math.floor(input.seed),
96	      worldType: input.worldType ?? "default",
97	      gameMode: input.gameMode ?? "survival",
98	      difficulty: input.difficulty ?? "normal",
99	      hardcore: input.hardcore ?? false,
100	      worldgenVersion: WORLDGEN_VERSION
101	    })
102	    .returning();
103	  await db.insert(schema.worldMembers).values({ worldId: id, userId, role: "owner" });
104	  return { ok: true, world: toSummary(world, "owner") };
105	}
106	
107	export async function getWorld(db: Db, userId: string, worldId: string): Promise<{ ok: true; world: WorldSummary } | Failure> {
108	  const member = await membership(db, userId, worldId);
109	  if (!member) return fail("not-found"); // membership-gated: outsiders can't probe ids
110	  const [world] = await db.select().from(schema.worlds).where(eq(schema.worlds.id, worldId));
111	  if (!world) return fail("not-found");
112	  return { ok: true, world: toSummary(world, member.role) };
113	}
114	
115	export async function renameWorld(db: Db, userId: string, worldId: string, name: string): Promise<{ ok: true } | Failure> {
116	  const trimmed = name?.trim();
117	  if (!trimmed || trimmed.length > 64) return fail("invalid");
118	  const member = await membership(db, userId, worldId);
119	  if (!member) return fail("not-found");
120	  if (member.role !== "owner") return fail("forbidden");
121	  await db.update(schema.worlds).set({ name: trimmed, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(schema.worlds.id, worldId));
122	  return { ok: true };
123	}
124	
125	export async function deleteWorld(db: Db, userId: string, worldId: string): Promise<{ ok: true } | Failure> {
126	  const member = await membership(db, userId, worldId);
127	  if (!member) return fail("not-found");
128	  if (member.role !== "owner") return fail("forbidden");
129	  await db.delete(schema.worlds).where(eq(schema.worlds.id, worldId)); // members/invites cascade
130	  return { ok: true };
131	}
132	
133	/** The gzipped SaveData blob plus its concurrency stamp. */
134	export async function getSaveBlob(
135	  db: Db,
136	  userId: string,
137	  worldId: string
138	): Promise<{ ok: true; blob: Uint8Array | null; saveVersion: number | null; updatedAt: string } | Failure> {
139	  const member = await membership(db, userId, worldId);
140	  if (!member) return fail("not-found");
141	  const [world] = await db.select().from(schema.worlds).where(eq(schema.worlds.id, worldId));
142	  if (!world) return fail("not-found");
143	  return { ok: true, blob: world.saveBlob ?? null, saveVersion: world.saveVersion, updatedAt: world.updatedAt.toISOString() };
144	}
145	
146	/**
147	 * Last-write-wins with a stale guard: the client sends the `updatedAt` it
148	 * last saw; a mismatch means someone else (another device) wrote in between —
149	 * 409, and the client picks the newer save. `baseUpdatedAt: null` means
150	 * "first upload", accepted only while the world has no blob yet.
151	 */
152	export async function putSaveBlob(
153	  db: Db,
154	  userId: string,
155	  worldId: string,
156	  blob: Uint8Array,
157	  saveVersion: number,
158	  baseUpdatedAt: string | null
159	): Promise<{ ok: true; updatedAt: string } | Failure> {
160	  const member = await membership(db, userId, worldId);
161	  if (!member) return fail("not-found");
162	  const [world] = await db.select().from(schema.worlds).where(eq(schema.worlds.id, worldId));
163	  if (!world) return fail("not-found");
164	  if (!Number.isInteger(saveVersion) || blob.byteLength === 0) return fail("invalid");
165	  const current = world.updatedAt.toISOString();
166	  const stale = baseUpdatedAt === null ? world.saveBlob !== null : baseUpdatedAt !== current;
167	  if (stale) return fail("conflict");
168	  const now = new Date();
169	  await db.update(schema.worlds).set({ saveBlob: blob, saveVersion, updatedAt: now }).where(eq(schema.worlds.id, worldId));
170	  return { ok: true, updatedAt: now.toISOString() };
171	}
172	
173	export async function createInvite(db: Db, userId: string, worldId: string): Promise<{ ok: true; token: string } | Failure> {
174	  const member = await membership(db, userId, worldId);
175	  if (!member) return fail("not-found");
176	  if (member.role !== "owner") return fail("forbidden");
177	  const token = base64urlToken();
178	  await db.insert(schema.worldInvites).values({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), worldId, token, createdBy: userId });
179	  return { ok: true, token };
180	}
181	
182	/** 128 bits of URL-safe randomness. */
183	function base64urlToken(): string {
184	  const bytes = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
185	  let binary = "";
186	  for (const b of bytes) binary += String.fromCharCode(b);
187	  return btoa(binary).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
188	}
189	
190	export async function resolveInvite(db: Db, token: string): Promise<{ ok: true; worldId: string; worldName: string } | Failure> {
191	  const [invite] = await db.select().from(schema.worldInvites).where(eq(schema.worldInvites.token, token));
192	  if (!invite) return fail("not-found");
193	  if (invite.expiresAt && invite.expiresAt.getTime() < Date.now()) return fail("expired");
194	  if (invite.maxUses !== null && invite.uses >= invite.maxUses) return fail("expired");
195	  const [world] = await db.select().from(schema.worlds).where(eq(schema.worlds.id, invite.worldId));
196	  if (!world) return fail("not-found");
197	  return { ok: true, worldId: world.id, worldName: world.name };
198	}
199	
200	/** Accepting twice is fine (idempotent); each NEW membership consumes one use. */
201	export async function acceptInvite(db: Db, userId: string, token: string): Promise<{ ok: true; worldId: string } | Failure> {
202	  const resolved = await resolveInvite(db, token);
203	  if (!resolved.ok) return resolved;
204	  const existing = await membership(db, userId, resolved.worldId);
205	  if (existing) return { ok: true, worldId: resolved.worldId };
206	  await db.insert(schema.worldMembers).values({ worldId: resolved.worldId, userId, role: "member" }).onConflictDoNothing();
207	  const [invite] = await db.select().from(schema.worldInvites).where(eq(schema.worldInvites.token, token));
208	  await db
209	    .update(schema.worldInvites)
210	    .set({ uses: invite.uses + 1 })
211	    .where(eq(schema.worldInvites.id, invite.id));
212	  return { ok: true, worldId: resolved.worldId };
213	}
214	
215	/** Mints the 60s join ticket the game server trusts. Membership required; mp worlds only. */
216	export async function mintTicket(
217	  db: Db,
218	  user: { id: string; name: string; skinId?: string | null },
219	  worldId: string,
220	  secret: string
221	): Promise<{ ok: true; ticket: string } | Failure> {
222	  const member = await membership(db, user.id, worldId);
223	  if (!member) return fail("not-found");
224	  const [world] = await db.select().from(schema.worlds).where(eq(schema.worlds.id, worldId));
225	  if (!world) return fail("not-found");
226	  if (world.kind !== "mp") return fail("invalid");
227	  const ticket = await signTicket(
228	    { sub: user.id, wid: worldId, name: user.name, skinId: user.skinId ?? null, role: member.role, pv: PROTOCOL_VERSION },
229	    secret
230	  );
231	  return { ok: true, ticket };
232	}
233

1	/**
2	 * A tiny CLI game client for poking a live game server (local or staging)
3	 * without a browser:
4	 *
5	 *   GAME_TICKET_SECRET=… bun scripts/netProbe.ts ws://localhost:8080 my-world
6	 *
7	 * Mints its own ticket (so the secret must match the server's), joins, walks
8	 * forward for a few seconds, and logs every message class it sees.
9	 */
10	import { PROTOCOL_VERSION } from "@/lib/net/protocol";
11	import { gunzipWorldSync } from "@/lib/net/codec";
12	import { signTicket } from "@/lib/net/tickets";
13	
14	const [, , urlArg, worldArg] = process.argv;
15	const url = urlArg ?? "ws://localhost:8080";
16	const worldId = worldArg ?? "probe-world";
17	const secret = process.env.GAME_TICKET_SECRET;
18	if (!secret) {
19	  console.error("GAME_TICKET_SECRET required (must match the server)");
20	  process.exit(1);
21	}
22	
23	const ticket = await signTicket(
24	  { sub: `probe-${Date.now() % 100000}`, wid: worldId, name: "Probe", skinId: null, role: "member", pv: PROTOCOL_VERSION },
25	  secret
26	);
27	const ws = new WebSocket(`${url}/ws`);
28	ws.binaryType = "arraybuffer";
29	
30	let seq = 0;
31	let pose: { x: number; y: number; z: number } | null = null;
32	const counts = new Map<string, number>();
33	
34	ws.onopen = () => {
35	  console.log("connected — sending hello");
36	  ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "hello", ticket, protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION }));
37	};
38	ws.onclose = (event) => {
39	  console.log(`closed: ${event.code} ${event.reason}`);
40	  console.log("message counts:", Object.fromEntries(counts));
41	  process.exit(0);
42	};
43	ws.onmessage = async (event) => {
44	  if (typeof event.data !== "string") {
45	    const sync = await gunzipWorldSync(new Uint8Array(event.data as ArrayBuffer));
46	    console.log(`worldSync: ${sync?.changes.length} block changes, ${sync?.players.length} players, ${sync?.liveMobs.length} mobs`);
47	    counts.set("worldSync", (counts.get("worldSync") ?? 0) + 1);
48	    return;
49	  }
50	  const message = JSON.parse(event.data) as { t: string } & Record<string, unknown>;
51	  counts.set(message.t, (counts.get(message.t) ?? 0) + 1);
52	  if (message.t === "welcome") {
53	    console.log("welcome:", message.playerId, "world seed", message.seed);
54	  }
55	  if (message.t === "tick" && !pose) {
56	    // Adopt whatever spawn the server gave us, then start walking.
57	    const self = message.self as { hearts?: number } | undefined;
58	    if (self) console.log("self:", JSON.stringify(self).slice(0, 120));
59	    pose = { x: 256, y: 80, z: 256 };
60	  }
61	};
62	
63	const move = { forward: true, back: false, left: false, right: false, jump: false, sprint: false, crouch: false };
64	setInterval(() => {
65	  if (ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN || !pose) return;
66	  pose.z -= 0.2; // amble north at ~4 blocks/s
67	  seq += 1;
68	  ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "pose", seq, ...pose, yaw: 0, pitch: 0, onGround: true, move, mineHeld: false }));
69	  if (seq % 40 === 0) ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: "ping", id: seq, tMs: Date.now() }));
70	}, 50);
71	
72	setTimeout(() => {
73	  console.log("probe done");
74	  ws.close();
75	}, 8000);

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/scripts/loadSim.ts",
  "content": "/**\n * Soak load: drives N synthetic clients into one room and reports the server's\n * tick budget and bandwidth so MAX_ROOMS and the deadbands can be tuned from\n * numbers, not guesses:\n *\n *   GAME_TICKET_SECRET=… ADMIN_TOKEN=… \\\n *     bun scripts/loadSim.ts ws://localhost:8080 my-world 8 30\n *                            └ url            └ world └ clients └ seconds\n *\n * Each client joins, streams a 20 Hz pose walking a small circle plus an\n * occasional block break, and tallies bytes received. Meanwhile it polls the\n * admin /rooms endpoint (ADMIN_TOKEN) once a second for the server's own\n * players/tick/slowest-tick/bandwidth counters, then prints per-client and\n * server-side p95 tick time and aggregate throughput.\n */\nimport { PROTOCOL_VERSION } from \"@/lib/net/protocol\";\nimport { signTicket } from \"@/lib/net/tickets\";\n\nconst [, , urlArg, worldArg, clientsArg, secondsArg] = process.argv;\nconst wsUrl = urlArg ?? \"ws://localhost:8080\";\nconst httpUrl = wsUrl.replace(/^ws/, \"http\");\nconst worldId = worldArg ?? \"loadsim-world\";\nconst clientCount = Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(clientsArg ?? \"8\", 10));\nconst durationMs = Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(secondsArg ?? \"30\", 10)) * 1000;\n\nconst secret = process.env.GAME_TICKET_SECRET;\nif (!secret) {\n  console.error(\"GAME_TICKET_SECRET required (must match the server)\");\n  process.exit(1);\n}\nconst adminToken = process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN;\n\ntype ClientStat = { id: string; bytesIn: number; frames: number; connected: boolean };\n\nasync function spawnClient(index: number): Promise<ClientStat> {\n  const stat: ClientStat = { id: `sim-${index}`, bytesIn: 0, frames: 0, connected: false };\n  const ticket = await signTicket({ sub: stat.id, wid: worldId, name: `Sim${index}`, skinId: null, role: index === 0 ? \"owner\" : \"member\", pv: PROTOCOL_VERSION }, secret!);\n  const ws = new WebSocket(`${wsUrl}/ws`);\n  ws.binaryType = \"arraybuffer\";\n\n  let seq = 0;\n  const center = { x: 256, y: 80, z: 256 };\n  const phase = (index / clientCount) * Math.PI * 2;\n\n  ws.onopen = () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: \"hello\", ticket, protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION }));\n  ws.onmessage = (event) => {\n    stat.frames += 1;\n    stat.bytesIn += typeof event.data === \"string\" ? event.data.length : (event.data as ArrayBuffer).byteLength;\n    if (typeof event.data === \"string\") {\n      const message = JSON.parse(event.data) as { t: string };\n      if (message.t === \"welcome\") stat.connected = true;\n    }\n  };\n  ws.onclose = () => {\n    stat.connected = false;\n  };\n\n  const move = { forward: true, back: false, left: false, right: false, jump: false, sprint: false, crouch: false };\n  const poser = setInterval(() => {\n    if (ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return;\n    seq += 1;\n    const t = seq / 20;\n    const x = center.x + Math.cos(t + phase) * 6;\n    const z = center.z + Math.sin(t + phase) * 6;\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: \"pose\", seq, x, y: center.y, z, yaw: t, pitch: 0, onGround: true, move, mineHeld: seq % 40 < 10 }));\n    if (seq % 20 === 0) ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: \"ping\", id: seq, tMs: Date.now() }));\n    // A block break every ~3s so the edit/journal path is exercised under load.\n    if (seq % 60 === 0) ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: \"cmd\", seq, cmd: { type: \"attack\" }, pose: { x, y: center.y + 1.6, z, yaw: t, pitch: -1.4 } }));\n  }, 50);\n\n  setTimeout(() => {\n    clearInterval(poser);\n    try {\n      ws.close();\n    } catch {\n      /* already closed */\n    }\n  }, durationMs);\n  return stat;\n}\n\nasync function pollRooms(): Promise<{ players: number; tick: number; slowestTickMs: number; kbOutPerSec: number } | null> {\n  if (!adminToken) return null;\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(`${httpUrl}/rooms`, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${adminToken}` } });\n    if (!response.ok) return null;\n    const body = (await response.json()) as { rooms: Array<{ worldId: string; players: number; tick: number; slowestTickMs: number; kbOutPerSec: number }> };\n    return body.rooms.find((r) => r.worldId === worldId) ?? null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nconsole.log(`loadSim: ${clientCount} clients → ${worldId} for ${durationMs / 1000}s`);\nconst stats = await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: clientCount }, (_, i) => spawnClient(i)));\n\nconst slowestSamples: number[] = [];\nlet peakKbOut = 0;\nconst sampler = setInterval(async () => {\n  const room = await pollRooms();\n  if (!room) return;\n  slowestSamples.push(room.slowestTickMs);\n  peakKbOut = Math.max(peakKbOut, room.kbOutPerSec);\n  console.log(`  t=${(room.tick / 20).toFixed(0)}s players=${room.players} slowestTick=${room.slowestTickMs}ms out=${room.kbOutPerSec}KB/s`);\n}, 1000);\n\nawait new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, durationMs + 500));\nclearInterval(sampler);\n\nconst connected = stats.filter((s) => s.connected || s.frames > 0).length;\nconst totalKbIn = stats.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.bytesIn, 0) / 1024;\nconst p95 = slowestSamples.length ? [...slowestSamples].sort((a, b) => a - b)[Math.min(slowestSamples.length - 1, Math.floor(slowestSamples.length * 0.95))] : null;\n\nconsole.log(`\\n── results ──`);\nconsole.log(`clients that joined: ${connected}/${clientCount}`);\nconsole.log(`downstream received: ${totalKbIn.toFixed(0)} KB total, ${(totalKbIn / (durationMs / 1000)).toFixed(1)} KB/s aggregate`);\nif (p95 !== null) console.log(`server tick p95: ${p95}ms (budget is 50ms); peak downstream: ${peakKbOut} KB/s`);\nelse console.log(`(set ADMIN_TOKEN to sample server-side tick/bandwidth stats)`);\nprocess.exit(0);\n"
}

=== protocol close ===
## Close codes

| Code | Meaning                                           |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          |
| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         |
| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      |
| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) |
| 4004 | idle timeout                                      |
| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) |
| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              |

## Trust model

The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes
in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned
thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly). The
claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for
invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side
rewind validation would need.

  "old_string": "Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events\nand `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.\n\n## Close codes\n\n| Code | Meaning                                           |\n| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          |\n| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         |\n| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      |\n| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) |\n| 4004 | idle timeout                                      |\n| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) |\n| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              |",
  "new_string": "Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events\nand `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.\n\n## Reconnect\n\nThe replica engine outlives the socket. On a **non-fatal** drop the client\nwalks a back-off ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` = 1/2/4/8/8 s), minting a\n**fresh** ticket each rung (the 60 s TTL kills a stale one) and doing a whole\nnew `hello` → `welcome` → world-sync — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a\nnew socket, not a special frame, so the server's `join` already re-syncs the\nsame room in place. The server closes the player's *previous* socket with\n`4003` when the new one lands (see the table). `resync` stays the same-socket\npath (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh\nworld-sync + keyframe). Fatal closes are not retried; after the ladder is\nexhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.\n\n## Close codes\n\n| Code | Meaning                                           | Client retries? |\n| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |\n| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          | no (fatal)      |\n| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         | no (fatal)      |\n| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      | no (fatal)      |\n| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) | no (fatal)      |\n| 4004 | idle timeout                                      | yes (ladder)    |\n| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) | yes (ladder)    |\n| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              | no (fatal)      |\n| 1006 | abnormal close (network drop)                     | yes (ladder)    |"
}

98	Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
99	`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
100	fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
101	no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
102	fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.
103	
104	## Production
105	
106	- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
107	  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
108	- **Fly.io** (game server, phase 4): shares `DATABASE_URL` and
109	  `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` with the web app.
110	
111	## Game server operations
112	
113	`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
114	hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
115	on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
116	persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
117	drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
118	See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.
119	
120	- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this).
121	- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics (players, tick, slowest-tick ms);
122	  requires `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`.
123	- `PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the
124	  Playwright multiplayer spec, and `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (a CLI client
125	  that joins, walks, and tallies traffic — point it at localhost or staging).
126	
127	Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
128	container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
129	with WebSocket ingress works.
130

434	## Inventory
435	
436	`HOTBAR_SLOTS`, `INVENTORY_SLOTS`, `MAX_STACK_SIZE`. **Save-sensitive** — see below.
437	
438	`CHEST_SLOTS` (27) is the storage capacity of a placed chest, read by the interact,
439	mining, and save paths (`lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`, `…/mining.ts`,
440	`lib/game/save.ts`) and the inventory panel grid. It is **soft** save-sensitive:
441	shrinking it after chests have been saved with items past the new limit would drop
442	those overflow slots on load (`readContainers` rebuilds a `CHEST_SLOTS`-length array).
443	
444	## Persistence & rendering
445	
446	`AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS`, `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, `SAVE_KEY` (legacy), `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`,
447	`RENDER_RADIUS`, `RENDER_GRID`, `THIRD_PERSON_DISTANCE`, `THIRD_PERSON_MARGIN`.
448	
449	`RENDER_RADIUS` is the biggest **performance** lever: the renderer meshes one region
450	of this radius around the player, so larger values draw more terrain at higher cost;
451	`RENDER_GRID` is how far the player moves before that mesh rebuilds (smaller = more
452	frequent rebuilds, fresher view). `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS` is how long an overlap is
453	tolerated before the auto-unstuck teleport fires.
454	
455	## Save- and worldgen-sensitive tunables
456	
457	Change these only with care:
458	
459	- **`WORLDGEN_VERSION`** (`10`) is the worldgen baseline each world records at
460	  creation. When a deliberate terrain change invalidates old block-diffs, bump this:
461	  every world whose recorded version differs discards its stale diffs and reboots from
462	  its seed — per-world, without renaming any key (see [save-format.md](save-format.md)).
463	  This replaced the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump, which reset _every_ world at once.
464	  It's versioned independently of the save **schema** (currently v16); don't bump it to
465	  express a schema change — add a migration instead.
466	- **`SAVE_KEY`** (`"minecraft_save_v7"`) is now **legacy**: each world has its own
467	  `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key, and `SAVE_KEY` is read only once by the one-time
468	  migration. Leave it alone.
469	- **`INVENTORY_SLOTS` / `HOTBAR_SLOTS` / `MAX_STACK_SIZE`** affect the saved
470	  inventory layout. `save.ts` already migrates the v1 (40-slot) → v2 (36-slot)
471	  change; altering these again needs a matching migration or old saves break.
472	- **Daylight thresholds and `WAKE_DAY_PHASE`** shape the persisted `dayClock`'s
473	  meaning but are not save-format-breaking on their own.

  "new_string": "## Multiplayer networking\n\nServer-side constants live in `server/room.ts` and `lib/net/protocol.ts` (not\n`config.ts` — they shape the wire and the room budget, not gameplay balance).\nNone affect single-player, and none are save-sensitive.\n\n- **`ROOM_CAPACITY`** (`8`, protocol.ts) — max players per world. The v1 co-op\n  scale the whole design assumes; raising it grows the per-tick pose/self fan-out\n  quadratically, so re-measure with `loadSim` before nudging it.\n- **`MAX_ROOMS`** (env, default `6`) — worlds one process hosts (memory: ~74 MB\n  each). Joins beyond it are refused at the door, not thrashed. Tune from\n  `/rooms` p95 tick + peak memory.\n- **Tick rate** — `TICK_SECONDS` (`0.05` = 20 Hz, `tickDriver.ts`) is the room\n  sim + pose-stream cadence. The whole latency budget hangs off it; not a\n  casual dial.\n- **Replication cadence** — `KEYFRAME_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`100` = 5 s, full mob\n  keyframe / drift correction), mob delta frames at **10 Hz** (half tick rate)\n  with `MOB_DEADBAND_SQ` (`0.05²` — smaller = more mob updates, more bandwidth),\n  `DAY_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`20` = 1 s day-clock sync), `POSE_CHECKPOINT_TICKS`\n  (`20` = 1 s replay-log pose anchors). `INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MS` (`125`,\n  `lib/net/interpolation.ts`) is how far in the past remote entities render —\n  larger absorbs more jitter at the cost of visible lag.\n- **Backpressure** — `BACKPRESSURE_SOFT_BYTES` (256 KB → shed `pp`/`mp`),\n  `BACKPRESSURE_KICK_BYTES` (1 MB) + `BACKPRESSURE_KICK_STRIKES` (~5 s sustained\n  → `4008` kick).\n- **Persistence** — `PERSIST_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`1200` = 60 s dirty-persist; also\n  the crash-loss bound), idle-evict at 5 min (`roomRegistry.ts`).\n- **Reconnect** — `RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` (`[1,2,4,8,8] s`, protocol.ts) is the\n  client back-off ladder; the join ticket TTL is `TICKET_TTL_SECONDS` (`60`,\n  `tickets.ts`).\n- **Replay log** — `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE` (env, default `4096`) bounds each room's\n  in-memory command ring dumped by `/rooms/:id/log`.\n- **Latency sim** — `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` (env, default `0`) seeds\n  the client's artificial one-way delay; `window.__monecraft.net.setSimulatedLatency(ms)`\n  overrides it live.\n\n## Save- and worldgen-sensitive tunables"
}

Net constants are documented in tuning.md and an ops runbook in online.md.\n- **Online co-op multiplayer**: 2–8 players in one shared, server-hosted world via a private invite link"

Bun exits **99** when every test passes but the run leaked an unhandled rejection (e.g. an unclosed PGlite/WASM handle) — and CI's `verify` job gates on the exit code, so it goes red while a piped local run looks green.\n\n**Why:** In this repo, PR #43's `verify` was red for exactly this while `e2e`/CodeRabbit passed; the cause was PGlite test fixtures never `.close()`d (see [[multiplayer-project]] commit ad6f55e). A `bun test | tail -6` shows \"0 fail\" and the pipe's exit code is `tail`'s (0), so the 99 was invisible for several phases.\n\n**How to apply:** Run `bun test > log 2>&1; echo \"EXIT $?\"` (or without a pipe) and require exit 0 — not just \"0 fail\". Any PGlite fixture (`createTestDb`) must be closed in `afterEach`/`afterAll` via `closeTestDb(db)`.\n"
}

**Wrap the account-link re-parenting in a transaction.** The four writes can partially succeed today; if a later statement fails, the anonymous user is still deleted afterward and the remaining rows will cascade away. `db.transaction` is available on both the postgres-js runtime driver and the PGlite test driver, so this can be made atomic.

FILE: lib/online/worldsService.ts:171

---

**Make the save update atomic**   
The stale check can race: two writers with the same `baseUpdatedAt` may both pass, and the later write silently overwrites the earlier one. Fold the compare into the `update` predicate and fail when no row is affected; `.returning()` is supported on both `postgres-js` and `pglite`, so the same pattern works in both drivers.

`resolveInvite` + `acceptInvite` is a check-then-act sequence: two concurrent accepts can both pass `maxUses`, admit extra members, and the current `invite.uses + 1` update can also lose increments. Make the accept path atomic and enforce the cap at write time.

FILE: server/room.ts:202
ID: 3519441000
---
_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Reconnecting players can be wrongly rejected as "room full".**
The capacity check (`this.clients.size >= ROOM_CAPACITY`) runs *before* the stale-connection lookup/replacement for the same `claims.sub`. When the room is already at capacity, an already-connected member trying to reconnect (e.g. after a dropped socket) is counted against their own slot and gets kicked with `CLOSE_ROOM_FULL` instead of being allowed to replace their stale connection.
=====================
FILE: server/room.ts:304
ID: 3519441015
---
_🔒 Security & Privacy_ | _🔴 Critical_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Advance `lastPoseTick` on accepted `cmd` poses in `server/room.ts:234-239`**  
`lastPoseTick` only advances in the `"pose"` path, so skipping pose updates or replaying rejected ones lets `elapsed` grow without bound. Since `applyRemotePose()` scales its clamp linearly with `elapsed`, a client can eventually make arbitrarily large `cmd`-driven jumps. Update the tick when a `cmd` pose is accepted, and cap the maximum elapsed used for remote-pose clamps.
=====================
FILE: server/roomRegistry.ts:46
ID: 3519441022
---
_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Capacity check has a TOCTOU race across concurrent loads.**
The `this.rooms.size >= this.maxRooms` check (Line 34) doesn't account for rooms currently loading in `this.loading`. Two concurrent `getOrLoad` calls for two *different* worldIds when `rooms.size == maxRooms - 1` will both pass the check before either registers in `this.rooms`, letting the process exceed `maxRooms`.
=====================
FILE: server/room.ts:121
ID: 3519912287
---
_🚀 Performance & Scalability_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Reset `bytesOut` when reading diagnostics**  
`kbOutPerSec` is a lifetime average, not “since last read”: `bytesOut` is only incremented in `tick()`/`broadcast()` and never cleared, while `seconds` grows with `tickCount`. Clear the counter in `diagnostics()` or track the last diagnostics tick so the gauge reflects the recent window.

I've now read and verified all 25. First, the good news: **CI is fully green** (verify ✅ e2e ✅ CodeRabbit ✅) — the PGlite fix cleared the red `verify`.

Here's my triage of the 25 CodeRabbit findings, verified against the actual code:

## A. Real bugs — should fix (no design call needed)

**Security / server (highest priority):**
- **🔴 Critical `server/room.ts` — unbounded pose clamp** (+ its Major companion in `GameEngine.ts:457`): the `cmd` path computes `elapsed` from `lastPoseTick` but never *advances* it, and `applyRemotePose` scales its speed clamp linearly with `elapsed` — so a client that sends only `cmd`s can eventually teleport. Real speed-hack vector. Fix: advance `lastPoseTick` on accepted cmd poses **and** cap `elapsed`.
- **`server/room.ts:202` (Major)** — a member reconnecting to a *full* room is rejected `ROOM_FULL` because the capacity check counts their own stale slot before the replacement runs. Fix: skip the capacity check when `claims.sub` is already connected.
- **`server/roomRegistry.ts:34` (Major)** — `MAX_ROOMS` TOCTOU: concurrent loads of different worlds ignore the in-flight `loading` map. Fix: count `rooms.size + loading.size`.
- **`lib/net/protocol.ts:229` (Major)** — `enchant` passes an arbitrary string into `canEnchant`/`ENCHANTMENT_DEFS[id]`; add an id allow-list like the other commands.

**Engine correctness (some affect single-player too):**
- **`GameEngine.ts:721` (Major)** — `applyMoveStack` uses `state.inventory`/`openContainerIndex` (primary aliases), so a non-primary player's chest/inventory move hits the *primary's* inventory. Real MP data bug.
- **`GameEngine.ts:1019` (Major)** — `restorePlayerFields` never reads the persisted `gameMode`/`gameOver` it serializes; a rejoining player loses their mode.
- **`players.ts:128` (Major)** — `nearestTargetablePlayer` doesn't skip dead players, so mobs target corpses (SP too). One-liner.
- **`playerStats.ts:86` (Major)** — hardcore game-over hearts get topped back to `MAX_HEARTS` next tick, overwriting the `hearts=0` withered state (SP hardcore too). One-liner guard.

**Web-app concurrency:**
- **`worldsService.ts:171` (Major)** — cloud-save LWW check-then-act races; fold the stale compare into the `UPDATE` predicate + check affected rows.
- **`worldsService.ts:226` (Major)** — invite `maxUses` check-then-act races; enforce the cap at write time.
- **`auth/server.ts:62` (Major)** — the guest→account re-parenting does 4 non-atomic writes then deletes the guest; wrap in `db.transaction` (the "guests keep worlds" promise).

**Client robustness / my Phase 5–6 code:**
- **`db/index.ts:36` (Minor)** — `void client.exec(SCHEMA_DDL)` swallows a DDL failure as an unhandled rejection; `.catch` it.
- **`GameShell.tsx:105` (Major)** — `playOnline` isn't re-entrancy-guarded; a double-click leaks a WebSocket. Guard on `connecting`.
- **`room.ts:121` (Minor)** — my `kbOutPerSec` is a *lifetime* average, not "since last read" as the comment claims; window it.
- **`AccountPanel.tsx:48` (Minor)** — no try/catch around the auth awaits; a network reject strands the button `disabled`.
- **`NetworkSession.ts:470` (Minor)** — the `cmd` eye-pose (`y+1.62`) gets written into the authoritative foot position for a tick.
- **`WorldSelect.tsx:87` (Minor)** — a failed `createOnlineWorld` closes the form silently, no error shown.
- **`GameEngine.ts:1044` (Major)** — if the last awake player leaves, sleeping players aren't re-checked and can hang. Small.

## B. Real, but a design call is yours
- **`server/room.ts:77` (Minor)** — any member can send `setDifficulty`/`setGameMode`. Should these be **owner-only** in co-op? (I'd say yes.)
- **`GameShell.tsx:164` (Minor)** — online Game Over "delete" only returns to the menu; it doesn't delete the world server-side. Wire it to `DELETE /api/worlds/:id`, or hide the button? (v1 scope.)

## C. Not real / already handled — skip
- **`save/route.ts:37`** — NaN `x-save-version` is already rejected by `putSaveBlob`'s `Number.isInteger` guard → 400. (Defense-in-depth only.)
- **`GameEngine.ts:1157`** — CodeRabbit self-marked "✅ Addressed"; it's the documented v1 scope cut (server rooms track no advancements/stats).
- **`save.ts:275` (inventoryCounts)** — verified: a v16 save can't carry the pre-v2 `inventoryCounts` format, so the migration never loses it in practice. Harmless 1-line hardening at most.
- **`save/route.ts:40`** (pre-buffer size check) — minor DoS hardening on an auth-gated route; low value.

=== applyRemotePose (full) ===
   * `elapsedSeconds` is the time since this player's last ACCEPTED pose.
   */
  applyRemotePose(
    playerId: PlayerId,
    pose: { x: number; y: number; z: number; yaw: number; pitch: number; onGround: boolean },
    elapsedSeconds: number
  ): { accepted: boolean } {
    const player = mustGetPlayer(this.state, playerId);
    const elapsed = Math.max(elapsedSeconds, 0.01);
    // A mounted player's pose belongs to the vehicle (server-side); ignore the stream.
    if (player.mountedVehicleId !== null) return { accepted: false };

    const dx = pose.x - player.position.x;
    const dz = pose.z - player.position.z;
    const dy = pose.y - player.position.y;
    const horizontal = Math.hypot(dx, dz);

    const free = isNoclip(player.gameMode) || (player.isFlying && player.gameMode === "creative");
    // Generous ceilings: jitter, knockback, and catch-up bursts must not
    // false-positive; a speedhack is an order of magnitude out anyway.
    const maxHorizontal = (free ? FLY_SPEED : SPRINT_SPEED * speedMultiplier(player)) * 1.6 * elapsed + 0.5;
    const maxUp = free ? FLY_SPEED * 1.6 * elapsed + 0.5 : (JUMP_VELOCITY + jumpBoostBonus(player)) * elapsed * 1.6 + 0.6;
    const maxDown = free ? FLY_SPEED * 1.6 * elapsed + 0.5 : GRAVITY * 2 * Math.max(elapsed, 0.5) * elapsed + 2;

    if (horizontal > maxHorizontal || dy > maxUp || -dy > maxDown) return { accepted: false };

    const wasGrounded = player.onGround;
    const verticalSpeed = dy / elapsed;
    player.position.set(pose.x, pose.y, pose.z);
    player.yaw = pose.yaw;
    player.pitch = Math.max(-Math.PI / 2 + 0.01, Math.min(Math.PI / 2 - 0.01, pose.pitch));
    player.onGround = pose.onGround;

    // Landing: the same threshold/formula as tickPlayerMotion, on the
    // velocity the pose stream implies (Feather Falling honored, armor path).
    const didLand = !wasGrounded && pose.onGround && verticalSpeed < 0;
    if (!free && didLand && verticalSpeed < -14) {
      const raw = Math.min(19, Math.floor((-verticalSpeed - 13) * 0.5));
      const softened = raw * (1 - featherFallingReduction(player.equippedArmor.boots));
      this.damageCombat(player, Math.max(1, Math.round(softened)));
    }

    const moving = horizontal > 1e-3;
    const didSprint = moving && player.input.move.sprint && !player.input.move.crouch;
    const previous = player.remoteMove;
    player.remoteMove = {
      didSprint,
      didWalk: moving && !didSprint,
      didJump: (previous?.didJump ?? false) || (wasGrounded && !pose.onGround && verticalSpeed > 2),
      didLand: (previous?.didLand ?? false) || didLand,
      landImpact: didLand ? -verticalSpeed : (previous?.landImpact ?? 0),
      horizontalDistance: (previous?.horizontalDistance ?? 0) + horizontal
    };
    return { accepted: true };
  }

  /**
   * Advances the simulation by dt seconds. The renderer draws the state
   * afterwards. `input` is the SP shell's live FrameInput for the primary
   * player; a server omits it and feeds every player via setPlayerInput.
   */
  step(dt: number, input?: FrameInput): void {
    const state = this.state;
    if (state.paused) {
      // Full freeze: mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all stop.
      this.refreshSnapshot();
      return;
    }
    const primary = state.players.get(state.primaryPlayerId) ?? null;

  "new_string": "  /** Admits a verified ticket onto a socket: joins the engine and syncs the world. */\n  async join(claims: TicketClaims, sink: ClientSink): Promise<boolean> {\n    // A reconnecting member already owns a slot — only a genuinely NEW player\n    // counts against capacity, so a dropped socket can always come back.\n    const reconnecting = this.clients.has(claims.sub);\n    if (!reconnecting && this.clients.size >= ROOM_CAPACITY) {\n      sink.close(CLOSE_ROOM_FULL, \"room full\");\n      return false;\n    }\n    // A reconnect replaces the old socket (the stale one is closed silently).\n    this.clients.get(claims.sub)?.sink.close(CLOSE_KICKED, \"replaced by a new connection\");\n    this.clients.delete(claims.sub);"
}

```
export function canEnchant(slot: InventorySlot | null | undefined, id: EnchantmentId): boolean {
  if (!slot?.id || !slot.kind || slot.count <= 0) return false;
  const def = ENCHANTMENT_DEFS[id];
  if (!def.kinds.includes(slot.kind)) return false;
  if (def.itemIds && !def.itemIds.includes(slot.id)) return false; // item-specific enchant (e.g. bow-only Power/Punch)
  return enchantLevel(slot, id) < def.maxLevel;
}

/** A new slot with `id` added (level 1) or its level bumped by one; returns the slot unchanged if not allowed. */
export function applyEnchant(slot: InventorySlot, id: EnchantmentId): InventorySlot {
  if (!canEnchant(slot, id)) return slot;
  const current = slot.enchantments ?? [];
  const enchantments: Enchantment[] = current.some((e) => e.id === id)
    ? current.map((e) => (e.id === id ? { id, level: e.level + 1 } : e))
    : [...current, { id, level: 1 }];
  return { ...slot, enchantments };
```

  "new_string": "  /** Restores one player's persisted slice onto a live PlayerState (the mirror of serializePlayer). */\n  private restorePlayerFields(player: PlayerState, saved: SavedPlayer): void {\n    // Resolve mode the same way the constructor does for the primary: a dead\n    // hardcore world spectates, hardcore forces survival, else the saved mode.\n    player.gameOver = saved.gameOver === true;\n    player.gameMode = player.gameOver ? \"spectator\" : this.state.hardcore ? \"survival\" : restoreGameMode(saved);\n    player.isFlying = player.gameMode === \"spectator\";\n    player.inventory = restoreInventorySlots(saved) ?? player.inventory;\n    player.equippedArmor = restoreEquippedArmor(saved) ?? player.equippedArmor;\n    player.selectedSlot = restoreSelectedSlot(saved) ?? player.selectedSlot;\n    player.hearts = restoreHearts(saved) ?? player.hearts;"
}

  "old_string": "  private applyMoveStack(from: number, to: number): void {\n    const state = this.state;\n    const container = state.openContainerIndex !== null ? state.containers.get(state.openContainerIndex) : undefined;\n    const resolve = (index: number): { arr: InventorySlot[]; local: number } | null => {\n      if (index >= CONTAINER_SLOT_BASE) return container ? { arr: container, local: index - CONTAINER_SLOT_BASE } : null;\n      return { arr: state.inventory, local: index };\n    };\n    const a = resolve(from);\n    const b = resolve(to);\n    if (!a || !b) return;\n    const moved = inv.moveStack(a.arr, a.local, b.arr, b.local);\n    if (!moved) return;\n\n    // Resolve each side's destination BEFORE writing: the first write reassigns\n    // state.inventory, which would make a later `arr === state.inventory` check\n    // stale and misroute an inventory↔inventory move into the open chest.\n    const aIsInventory = a.arr === state.inventory;\n    const bIsInventory = b.arr === state.inventory;\n    const writeBack = (isInventory: boolean, next: InventorySlot[]): void => {\n      if (isInventory) state.inventory = next;\n      else if (state.openContainerIndex !== null) state.containers.set(state.openContainerIndex, next);\n    };\n    writeBack(aIsInventory, moved.a);\n    writeBack(bIsInventory, moved.b);\n  }",
  "new_string": "  private applyMoveStack(player: PlayerState, from: number, to: number): void {\n    const state = this.state;\n    const openIndex = player.openContainerIndex;\n    const container = openIndex !== null ? state.containers.get(openIndex) : undefined;\n    const resolve = (index: number): { arr: InventorySlot[]; local: number } | null => {\n      if (index >= CONTAINER_SLOT_BASE) return container ? { arr: container, local: index - CONTAINER_SLOT_BASE } : null;\n      return { arr: player.inventory, local: index };\n    };\n    const a = resolve(from);\n    const b = resolve(to);\n    if (!a || !b) return;\n    const moved = inv.moveStack(a.arr, a.local, b.arr, b.local);\n    if (!moved) return;\n\n    // Resolve each side's destination BEFORE writing: the first write reassigns\n    // player.inventory, which would make a later `arr === player.inventory` check\n    // stale and misroute an inventory↔inventory move into the open chest.\n    const aIsInventory = a.arr === player.inventory;\n    const bIsInventory = b.arr === player.inventory;\n    const writeBack = (isInventory: boolean, next: InventorySlot[]): void => {\n      if (isInventory) player.inventory = next;\n      else if (openIndex !== null) state.containers.set(openIndex, next);\n    };\n    writeBack(aIsInventory, moved.a);\n    writeBack(bIsInventory, moved.b);\n  }"

118	/**
119	 * Nearest player hostiles may hunt — Creative/Spectator players aren't a
120	 * threat target (mobsThreaten), so they're skipped. Null when nobody is
121	 * huntable (or the world is empty, e.g. an idle server room).
122	 */
123	export function nearestTargetablePlayer(state: GameState, x: number, z: number): PlayerState | null {
124	  let best: PlayerState | null = null;
125	  let bestSq = Infinity;
126	  for (const player of state.players.values()) {
127	    if (!mobsThreaten(player.gameMode)) continue;
128	    const dx = player.position.x - x;
129	    const dz = player.position.z - z;
130	    const d = dx * dx + dz * dz;
131	    if (d < bestSq) {
132	      bestSq = d;
133	      best = player;
134	    }
135	  }
136	  return best;
137	}

  "new_string": "/** Accepting twice is fine (idempotent); each NEW membership consumes one use. */\nexport async function acceptInvite(db: Db, userId: string, token: string): Promise<{ ok: true; worldId: string } | Failure> {\n  const resolved = await resolveInvite(db, token);\n  if (!resolved.ok) return resolved;\n  const existing = await membership(db, userId, resolved.worldId);\n  if (existing) return { ok: true, worldId: resolved.worldId };\n  // Consume one use atomically, enforcing the cap in the predicate: concurrent\n  // accepts can't both slip past a maxUses that only one increment should clear.\n  const consumed = await db\n    .update(schema.worldInvites)\n    .set({ uses: sql`${schema.worldInvites.uses} + 1` })\n    .where(and(eq(schema.worldInvites.token, token), or(isNull(schema.worldInvites.maxUses), lt(schema.worldInvites.uses, schema.worldInvites.maxUses))))\n    .returning({ id: schema.worldInvites.id });\n  if (consumed.length === 0) return fail(\"expired\"); // the cap filled under concurrency\n  await db.insert(schema.worldMembers).values({ worldId: resolved.worldId, userId, role: \"member\" }).onConflictDoNothing();\n  return { ok: true, worldId: resolved.worldId };\n}"

  "old_string": "        onLinkAccount: async ({ anonymousUser, newUser }) => {\n          // Everything the guest owned moves to the upgraded account. The\n          // anonymous user row is deleted right after this hook, and the FKs\n          // cascade — so a missed table here would silently destroy data.\n          const target = database as unknown as import(\"@/db\").Db;\n          const from = anonymousUser.user.id;\n          const to = newUser.user.id;\n          await target.update(schema.worlds).set({ ownerId: to }).where(eq(schema.worlds.ownerId, from));\n          await target.update(schema.worldInvites).set({ createdBy: to }).where(eq(schema.worldInvites.createdBy, from));\n          // Memberships can collide if the new account already joined the same\n          // world; drop the guest's row in that case (the membership exists).\n          const memberships = await target.select().from(schema.worldMembers).where(eq(schema.worldMembers.userId, from));\n          for (const membership of memberships) {\n            await target\n              .insert(schema.worldMembers)\n              .values({ ...membership, userId: to })\n              .onConflictDoNothing();\n          }\n          await target.delete(schema.worldMembers).where(eq(schema.worldMembers.userId, from));\n        }",
  "new_string": "        onLinkAccount: async ({ anonymousUser, newUser }) => {\n          // Everything the guest owned moves to the upgraded account. The\n          // anonymous user row is deleted right after this hook, and the FKs\n          // cascade — so a missed table (or a partial failure) would silently\n          // destroy data. One transaction makes the re-parent all-or-nothing:\n          // if any statement throws, nothing moves and the guest survives.\n          const target = database as unknown as import(\"@/db\").Db;\n          const from = anonymousUser.user.id;\n          const to = newUser.user.id;\n          await target.transaction(async (tx) => {\n            await tx.update(schema.worlds).set({ ownerId: to }).where(eq(schema.worlds.ownerId, from));\n            await tx.update(schema.worldInvites).set({ createdBy: to }).where(eq(schema.worldInvites.createdBy, from));\n            // Memberships can collide if the new account already joined the same\n            // world; drop the guest's row in that case (the membership exists).\n            const memberships = await tx.select().from(schema.worldMembers).where(eq(schema.worldMembers.userId, from));\n            for (const membership of memberships) {\n              await tx\n                .insert(schema.worldMembers)\n                .values({ ...membership, userId: to })\n                .onConflictDoNothing();\n            }\n            await tx.delete(schema.worldMembers).where(eq(schema.worldMembers.userId, from));\n          });\n        }"
}

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01Dqtddy6bzUZvA46bXHa9N2
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/net/protocol.ts",
  "old_string": "    case \"enchant\":\n      // Allow-list the id: an unknown one would throw in canEnchant (indexes ENCHANTMENT_DEFS).\n      return isStr(c.enchant) && c.enchant in ENCHANTMENT_DEFS ? { type: \"enchant\", enchant: c.enchant as EnchantmentId } : null;",
  "new_string": "    case \"enchant\":\n      // Allow-list the id: an unknown one would throw in canEnchant (indexes\n      // ENCHANTMENT_DEFS). hasOwnProperty (not `in`) so \"__proto__\"/\"toString\" don't slip through.\n      return isStr(c.enchant) && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ENCHANTMENT_DEFS, c.enchant)\n        ? { type: \"enchant\", enchant: c.enchant as EnchantmentId }\n        : null;"
}

i < 8; i += 1) expect(await room.join(claimsFor(`p${i}`, \"w1\"), fakeSink())).toBe(true);\n    expect(room.playerCount()).toBe(8);\n\n    // A NEW 9th player is refused…\n    const stranger = fakeSink();\n    expect(await room.join(claimsFor(\"stranger\", \"w1\"), stranger)).toBe(false);\n    expect(stranger.frames.some((f) => f.kind === \"close\" && f.code === 4002)).toBe(true); Then a teleport-sized cmd pose must be rejected.\n    for (let i = 0; i < 40; i += 1) {\n      tickRoom();\n      await room.handleMessage(\"alice\", { t: \"cmd\", seq: i + 1, cmd: { type: \"toggleInventory\" }, pose: { x, y, z, yaw: 0, pitch: 0 } });\n    }\n    a.frames.length = 0;\n    await room.handleMessage(\"alice\", { t: \"cmd\", seq: 999, cmd: { type: \"attack\" }, pose: { x: x + 60, y, z: z + 60, yaw: 0, pitch: 0 } });\n    expect(alice.position.x).toBeCloseTo(x, 3); // the jump was clamped, not admitted\n  });\n});"

Advance the\n  pose clock on an accepted cmd pose too (the elapsed cap in GameEngine is the\n  companion defense).\n- **Reconnect wrongly rejected as room-full**: the capacity check counted a\n  member's own stale slot; skip it when the id is already connected, so a\n  dropped socket can always return.\n- **World settings gated to the owner**: `setDifficulty`/`setGameMode` change\n  the world for everyone — reject them from non-owner members before dispatch.\n- **enchant allow-list**: an unknown enchant id reached `canEnchant` and threw\n  (indexing ENCHANTMENT_DEFS); validate it in readCommand with hasOwnProperty\n  (not `in`, so `__proto__`/`toString` can't slip through).\n- **cmd pose is the foot, not the eye**: the client sent eye height (y+1.62),\n  which the server wrote into the authoritative foot position and the engine\n  then re-offset by EYE_HEIGHT — send the foot pose like the stream does.\n- **MAX_ROOMS TOCTOU**: count in-flight loads so two concurrent loads of\n  different worlds can't both slip past the cap.\n- **Bandwidth gauge windowed**: `kbOutPerSec` was a lifetime average; report\n  the delta since the last diagnostics read.\n\nTests: owner-only settings, reconnect into a full room, a cmd-only client's\njump still clamped, the enchant allow-list, and the windowed gauge.\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -1",

}

## Code review triage & fixes — done

I read and verified all **25 CodeRabbit findings** against the actual code, fixed the ~18 real ones across **3 commits** (local, not pushed), and skipped 4 as false-positives/documented-scope.

**Committed:**
- `ef5609a` **server/wire hardening** — the 🔴 Critical (unbounded pose clamp: `cmd` now advances `lastPoseTick` + a companion `elapsed` cap), owner-only world settings, reconnect-into-full-room, the enchant allow-list, cmd-pose-is-the-foot, `MAX_ROOMS` TOCTOU, windowed bandwidth gauge — with tests.
- `898dfaa` **engine correctness** — per-player `moveStack` (was hitting the primary alias), `gameMode`/`gameOver` restore, mobs no longer target corpses, hardcore game-over hearts stay 0, sleep-recheck on leave — with tests.
- `1e4878d` **online API + client UX** — atomic cloud-save LWW, atomic invite-cap, transactional account re-parenting, `db()` pglite `.catch`, `playOnline` re-entrancy guard, online Game-Over delete wired to the server, AccountPanel try/catch, WorldSelect create-failure surfacing.

**A nice catch:** a test I wrote for the enchant allow-list flushed out a bug in my *own* first-cut fix — `"__proto__" in ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` is `true` via the prototype chain, so `in` would've let `__proto__`/`toString` through. Switched to `hasOwnProperty`.

**Skipped (with reasons):** NaN save-version (already rejected by `putSaveBlob`), progression-to-primary (documented v1 scope cut), `inventoryCounts` migration (can't occur at save v16), pre-buffer body-size check (minor, auth-gated).

**Local gate:** lint, typecheck, format:check, `bun test` **exit 0 (1080 pass)**, build all green. Full e2e running now — I'll report the result.

> **"Copy invite" reports success even when the copy didn't happen.**

Good question — here's the honest state, then a concrete walkthrough.

## Are there deploy docs?

The pieces are documented, but there's **no single deploy runbook**. What exists today:

| Where | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `docs/online.md` → **Production** section | 4 lines: "put web env vars on Vercel, point DATABASE_URL at Neon; Fly shares DATABASE_URL + GAME_TICKET_SECRET." Thin. |
| `docs/online.md` → **Runbook** | *Operations* (kick, revoke, replay, redeploy drain, capacity) — not first-time deploy. |
| `server/fly.toml` (header comments) | The actual Fly deploy commands. |
| `server/Dockerfile` | The game-server image (Bun, no build step). |
| `.env.example` | Every env var, web + server. |
| `drizzle.config.ts` | Migration config. |

So it's spread across five files. I'd recommend I consolidate it into a proper `docs/deploy.md` (offer at the end).

## How to deploy (three parts, sharing one database + one secret)

The architecture is **Vercel** (Next app + auth + API) + **Neon Postgres** + **Fly.io** (the Bun game server). Two hard links between them: they share the **same `DATABASE_URL`** and a **byte-identical `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`**.

**1. Database — Neon (or any Postgres)**
```bash
# Create a Neon project, copy its connection string, then apply the schema:
DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' bunx drizzle-kit migrate
```
That runs the committed `db/migrations/0000_online-foundation.sql`.

**2. Web app — Vercel**
Import the repo in Vercel (or `vercel --prod`), and set these env vars (from `.env.example`):
- `DATABASE_URL` → the Neon string
- `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` → `openssl rand -base64 32`
- `BETTER_AUTH_URL` → your deployed origin, e.g. `https://monecraft.vercel.app`
- `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` → a shared random secret (**must match the game server**)
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` → `wss://monecraft-server.fly.dev` (note **wss**, not ws)

`next build` needs no env (the auth mount is lazy), so a missing var won't fail the build — it'll fail at runtime, so double-check them.

**3. Game server — Fly.io** (from the repo root, per `server/fly.toml`'s header):
```bash
fly launch --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --no-deploy
fly secrets set DATABASE_URL='…' GAME_TICKET_SECRET='…' ADMIN_TOKEN='…'
fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile
```
`fly.toml` already pins: single region (`nrt`), always-on (`min_machines_running=1`, `auto_stop=off` — a room must keep ticking), `/health` checks, `PERSISTENCE=postgres`, `MAX_ROOMS=6`, 2GB VM. Redeploys drain rooms to Postgres on SIGTERM (≤60s loss, crash-safe).

**Gotchas worth knowing:**
- The game server is on Fly, **not** Vercel, because Vercel functions can't hold long-lived WebSockets — that split is deliberate.
- `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` mismatch = every join fails with close code `4000` (bad ticket). It's the #1 misconfiguration.
- Single-player needs **none** of this — it stays fully offline; only online co-op touches the stack.
- The container is platform-neutral (plain Docker + `/health` + env) — Railway/Render/a VPS work by swapping the Fly config.

---

**Want me to write `docs/deploy.md`?** I'd turn the above into a proper first-time deploy runbook (with a "verify it works" smoke check and the shared-secret checklist), link it from `docs/online.md` and the README, and fold in the ops runbook cross-reference. Say the word and I'll add it as a commit on the branch.
