  "content": "# Deploying online multiplayer\n\nA first-time deploy runbook for the online stack. **Single-player needs none of\nthis** — it runs entirely in the browser with localStorage and never touches the\nnetwork. Only online co-op (accounts, cloud saves, shared worlds) needs a server;\nthis page is how to stand that up.\n\nFor _how the stack fits together_ see [online.md](online.md); for _operating_ a\nrunning deployment (kick, revoke, replay, redeploys, capacity) see the\n[ops runbook](online.md#runbook).\n\n## The shape of it\n\nThree managed pieces, sharing a database and one secret:\n\n```\n        Vercel (Next app + better-auth + /api)  ─┐\nBrowser ┤                                         ├─ Neon Postgres (accounts, worlds, saves)\n        └ Fly.io (Bun game server, WebSocket) ───┘\n                    ▲\n        share the SAME DATABASE_URL and a byte-identical GAME_TICKET_SECRET\n```\n\n- **Vercel** hosts the Next.js app: menus, better-auth, and the `/api` routes\n  (worlds, invites, cloud saves, join tickets).\n- **Neon** (or any Postgres) holds accounts, world rows, memberships, invites,\n  and gzipped save blobs.\n- **Fly.io** runs the authoritative Bun game server (`server/`) — the long-lived\n  WebSocket world rooms. It's on Fly and **not** Vercel because serverless\n  functions can't hold persistent WebSockets; that split is deliberate.\n\nThe only runtime link between Vercel and Fly is the **join ticket**: the web API\nmints a 60-second HS256 token, the game server verifies it with the shared\n`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`. They never call each other directly.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Accounts on [Vercel](https://vercel.com), [Neon](https://neon.tech) (or another\n  Postgres provider), and [Fly.io](https://fly.io).\n- The [Fly CLI](https://fly.io/docs/flyctl/install/) (`fly`) and optionally the\n  [Vercel CLI](https://vercel.com/docs/cli) (`vercel`).\n- `bun` locally (to run the one migration).\n\n## Secrets to generate up front\n\nGenerate these once and keep them handy — several are shared:\n\n```bash\nopenssl rand -base64 32   # BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (web only)\nopenssl rand -base64 32   # GAME_TICKET_SECRET (web AND game server — must match)\nopenssl rand -base64 24   # ADMIN_TOKEN (game server only; guards /rooms* admin endpoints)\n```\n\n> **The #1 misconfiguration:** if `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` differs between Vercel and\n> Fly, _every_ join fails with WebSocket close code **4000** (bad ticket). Set the\n> exact same value in both.\n\n## Step 1 — Database (Neon)\n\n1. Create a Neon project and copy its pooled connection string (it looks like\n   `REDACTED`). This is `DATABASE_URL`.\n2. Apply the schema (runs the committed `db/migrations/0000_online-foundation.sql`):\n\n   ```bash\n   DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' bunx drizzle-kit migrate\n   ```\n\n   Migrations are generated from `db/schema.ts` and committed under\n   `db/migrations/`; only `drizzle-kit migrate` needs a live database. Re-run this\n   after any future schema change lands.\n\n## Step 2 — Game server (Fly.io)\n\nRun from the **repo root**. The commands are also in `server/fly.toml`'s header.\n\n```bash\nfly launch --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --no-deploy\nfly secrets set \\\n  DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' \\\n  GAME_TICKET_SECRET='…the shared secret…' \\\n  ADMIN_TOKEN='…admin token…' \\\n  --config server/fly.toml\nfly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile\n```\n\n`server/fly.toml` already pins the important bits: one region (`nrt`), **always\non** (`min_machines_running = 1`, `auto_stop_machines = \"off\"` — a room must keep\nticking while players are in it), a `/health` check, `PERSISTENCE = \"postgres\"`,\n`MAX_ROOMS = 6`, and a 2 GB VM (rooms are ~74 MB each). SIGTERM on a redeploy\ndrains every room to Postgres first, so a deploy loses at most the last 60 s\n(the dirty-persist interval), crash-safe.\n\nThe app name in `fly.toml` is `monecraft-server`, so its URL is\n`https://monecraft-server.fly.dev` — the browser connects over **`wss://`**\n(`force_https` is on). Rename the app if you like, but then update the web app's\n`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` to match.\n\nConfirm it's up:\n\n```bash\ncurl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health   # → {\"ok\":true,\"rooms\":0}\n```\n\n## Step 3 — Web app (Vercel)\n\nImport the repo in the Vercel dashboard (or `vercel --prod` from the repo root),\nthen set these environment variables (see `.env.example` for the full list):\n\n| Variable | Value |\n|---|---|\n| `DATABASE_URL` | the **same** Neon string as the game server |\n| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | your `openssl rand` output |\n| `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | the deployed origin, e.g. `https://monecraft.vercel.app` |\n| `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` | the **same** shared secret as the game server |\n| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` | `wss://monecraft-server.fly.dev` (note **wss**, not ws) |\n\n`next build` needs no env (the auth mount and DB connection are both lazy), so a\nmissing variable won't fail the build — it fails at _runtime_ instead. Double-check\nall five before calling it done.\n\n> **Ordering / chicken-and-egg:** `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is your Vercel origin and\n> `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` is your Fly origin, so each side wants the other's\n> URL. Both hostnames are predictable (`<project>.vercel.app`,\n> `<app>.fly.dev`), so set them up front. If you use a custom domain, set the env\n> var to the final URL and redeploy the web app once DNS is live. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`\n> vars are inlined at build time — changing one needs a **redeploy**, not just an\n> env edit.\n\n## Verify the whole thing\n\n1. `curl https://<fly-app>.fly.dev/health` → `{\"ok\":true,…}`.\n2. Open the deployed web app. It should look and play exactly like single-player\n   (offline-first: no account, no network until you go online).\n3. Create a **New Online World**, then **Copy invite**. Open the link in a second\n   browser (or a private window), accept, and play the world from its card. Both\n   players seeing each other proves the join ticket + Fly game server work.\n\nIf step 3 fails, it's the web/DB side (auth or `DATABASE_URL`). If step 4 connects\nas far as \"Joining…\" then errors, it's almost always the ticket secret or the\ngame-server URL — see below.\n\n## Updating a running deployment\n\n- **Web app:** push to the branch Vercel tracks (or `vercel --prod`). Changing a\n  `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` value requires a redeploy, not just an env edit.\n- **Game server:** `fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile`.\n  Rooms drain to Postgres on the rollout; connected clients reconnect on their\n  back-off ladder and re-sync (they'll see a brief \"Reconnecting…\" badge).\n- **Schema change:** land the new migration, then run `bunx drizzle-kit migrate`\n  against production **before** deploying the code that depends on it.\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Cause |\n|---|---|\n| Join fails, close code **4000** | `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` differs between Vercel and Fly — the #1 issue. |\n| \"could not get a join ticket\" | `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` unset, or the world isn't a `mp` world. |\n| Connects then instantly drops | Wrong scheme — must be **`wss://`** (not `ws://`) against an https Fly app. |\n| 500s on any `/api/worlds*` | `DATABASE_URL` wrong, or the migration wasn't applied (Step 1). |\n| Guest sign-in hangs | `BETTER_AUTH_URL` doesn't match the actual origin, or `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` unset. |\n| Game server won't boot | Missing `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` (it exits on start) or an unreachable `DATABASE_URL`. |\n\nAdmin diagnostics on the game server (all behind `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`):\n`GET /rooms` (players, tick p95, bandwidth), `GET /rooms/:id/log` (replay dump).\nSee the [ops runbook](online.md#runbook) for using them.\n\n## Other hosts\n\nThe game server is a plain Docker container that speaks HTTP `/health` and reads\nenv vars, so it's portable — **Railway**, **Render**, **Fly**, or any VPS that\nruns a long-lived container with WebSocket ingress works. Swap `server/fly.toml`\nfor that platform's config; keep the container always-on (a room must keep ticking)\nand give it the same `DATABASE_URL` + `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`. Cloudflare Durable\nObjects were ruled out (128 MB memory cap vs ~74 MB rooms, workerd runtime).\n\nFor local development of the full stack (no cloud, no Docker), see\n[online.md](online.md#environment--local-development).\n"
}

1	# Online Multiplayer for Monecraft
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Monecraft is today a single-player, client-only browser game (Next.js 16 / React 19 / TS strict / Three.js / Bun) saving to localStorage. Goal: online co-op multiplayer played in the browser, with accounts + cloud saves + instant guest access, deployed on managed infrastructure, without breaking offline single-player.
6	
7	Exploration confirmed the engine is **already a headless simulation core**: `lib/game/engine/` + `lib/world/` (~13.4k LOC) is pure TS (no DOM/WebAudio/rAF), runs under `bun test`, mutates only via `dispatch(Command)` (28-command union in `lib/game/engine/commands.ts`), publishes ~60 `GameEvent`s the renderer/audio already consume as observers, has injectable RNG/Storage, and saves as seed + block diff. The real work is: (a) the state model is single-player-shaped (one `state.player`, ~25 flat per-player fields in `state.ts`); (b) worldgen noise uses `Math.sin` → not portable across JS engines (why CI pins Bun 1.3.12) — a Bun server and a V8 browser can disagree on terrain for the same seed; (c) there is zero server/network code.
8	
9	### Decisions (confirmed with user)
10	
11	| Decision | Choice |
12	|---|---|
13	| Scale | 2–8 players per world, private co-op via invite link. No chunk streaming / interest management in v1 — full-world rooms. |
14	| Hosting | **Vercel**: Next.js app, better-auth, world/save/invite API, Neon Postgres. **Fly.io**: one Bun process hosting N world rooms (one `GameEngine` each, ~74 MB/room), WebSocket, 20 Hz fixed tick. They share only Neon + a ticket-signing secret. The game server is a plain Docker container (`/health`, env vars) — portable to Railway/Render/a VPS by swapping deploy config; Cloudflare DO ruled out (128 MB memory cap vs ~74 MB rooms, workerd runtime). |
15	| Authority | **Server-authoritative with one hybrid concession**: the server runs the real `GameEngine` per room — every gameplay Command (place/break/craft/attack/chest/…) is validated and executed server-side; canonical world state (blocks, mobs, items, chests, time) lives only there. The sole client-owned thing is each player's *own avatar movement* (streamed @20 Hz; server clamps speed/teleports and force-corrects). Full server-auth movement + prediction can be added later without wire changes — `cmd` envelopes already carry seq + claimed pose. |
16	| Auth | **better-auth**, self-hosted in Next, Postgres-backed, anonymous plugin: guest identity on first online action, in-place upgrade to email/OAuth keeping worlds. Game server never sees cookies — short-lived HS256 join tickets minted by the Next API. |
17	| SP | Stays fully offline-capable with localStorage saves, same engine (SP = 1-player case), no account required, no network code loaded. Optional cloud sync of SP saves when signed in (gzipped blob, LWW on `updatedAt`). Phase 2's acceptance bar — "entire existing e2e suite passes unchanged" — is the enforcement. |
18	| Seams | **No "extract the core" phase is needed** — the headless sim already exists and the Bun server imports it directly (Bun runs TS natively, no build step). What we build: Phase 1–2 make it deterministic + multi-player-shaped *in place*; Phase 5 adds the transport seam — `GameSession` (`createLocalSession` = today's offline path; `NetworkSession` = WebSocket + replica engine) with the protocol in shared `lib/net/`. |
19	
20	## Delivery: 6 phases, each its own `mp/*` branch + PR, verify gate green each time
21	
22	Phases 1–2 are pure refactors (zero product change) — the risk sponge. 3 (Vercel side) and 4 (Fly side) are independent after 2; 5 needs both.
23	
24	---
25	
26	### Phase 1 — Deterministic foundations (`mp/1-deterministic-foundations`)
27	
28	**Goal:** identical engine source produces byte-identical worlds on Bun and Chromium; engine input surface loses its DOM-isms. No networking, no feel change.
29	
30	- **Portable worldgen.** New `lib/world/noise.ts`: integer avalanche hash (`Math.imul`/xor-shift) → `hash2D`, integer-lattice value noise (3–4 octaves) replacing `smoothNoise2D`, and `portableSin/Cos` (range-reduce + minimax polynomial) for `carveCaves`' walk and `daylightAt`. Swap into `lib/world/generation.ts`; audit with `grep -nE 'Math\.(sin|cos|tan|atan|exp|log)'` over sim-affecting paths (`playerMotion` trig may stay — frame-local, never seed-determined). **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11** in `lib/game/config.ts`; re-baseline hashes in `lib/world/generation.test.ts` per the documented policy (the structural probes — flat is level, islands flood, villages find flat land — are the acceptance tests for terrain quality). Move digest constants to a new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`.
31	- **Cross-engine determinism e2e.** New `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`: in-page `crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", engine.state.world.blocks)` vs the baked Bun baseline → proves Chromium ≡ Bun per seed.
32	- **TickDriver.** New `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`: `createAccumulator` (the exact ≤50 ms/5-substep catch-up lifted from `useMinecraftGame.ts:294-305`) used by the SP rAF loop unchanged, and `createFixedTicker` (drift-corrected chained `setTimeout`, injectable clock) for the phase-4 server. SP stays variable-dt — forcing 20 Hz on the client would add latency for no v1 benefit.
33	- **Input intents.** `FrameInput` becomes `{ move: {forward,back,left,right,jump,sprint,crouch}, mineHeld }`; `systems/playerMotion.ts:77-91` reads intents; DOM key codes, CapsLock, and pointer-lock resolution move entirely into `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`. `applyLook` unchanged. Shared test helper for the 40+ `FrameInput` call sites.
34	- **Docs/tests:** architecture.md (input, TickDriver), testing.md (worldgen policy: cross-engine now e2e-pinned; Bun pin no longer load-bearing), save-format.md (v11 worldgen entry — old worlds discard diffs per existing rule), CHANGELOG (flag the world re-roll).
35	
36	### Phase 2 — Multi-player engine core (`mp/2-multiplayer-engine`) — biggest phase
37	
38	**Goal:** `players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; all 23 systems converted; save v17; SP behavior and the entire existing e2e suite pass unchanged (the acceptance bar).
39

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Ship & Validate Online Multiplayer v1 → cut v0.13.0

## Context

Online multiplayer v1 merged to `main` on 2026-07-03 (PR #43, merge commit `edbf8b0`): ~36 commits spanning portable worldgen, the multi-player engine (save v17), accounts/cloud-saves/invites (Neon + better-auth), the authoritative Bun game server + protocol v1 (Fly), the browser client (replica engine, reconnect ladder, chat), and the hardening/ops pass. Two rounds of CodeRabbit review are resolved; CI is green.

**The problem this addresses:** every test so far ran with **both servers on `localhost`**. Nothing has touched a real deployment, so the failure modes most likely to bite in production are entirely unvalidated — real internet RTT + jitter (the 125 ms interpolation and the reconnect ladder have never seen real latency), Neon connection pooling under Vercel's serverless model, Fly single-machine / cold-start behavior, `wss`/TLS, and the join-ticket handshake across two genuinely separate origins. The intended outcome: prove the stack holds up on live infrastructure with a real two-browser session, fix whatever surfaces, then cut the **v0.13.0** release on a version that has actually run in production.

This plan supersedes the completed 6-phase multiplayer build plan that previously lived in this file.

## Division of labor (set by the tooling)

- **You (the deploy — I can't drive it):** `fly` CLI isn't installed, and Neon + all secrets are your accounts. So provisioning the DB and deploying the game server are yours to run, following `docs/deploy.md`. I stay on-hand to guide and debug live.
- **Me (executable now):** deploy-readiness gaps, the validation runbook, and — after validation — the v0.13.0 release cut. I can also help drive/verify the **Vercel** step via the CLI or the Vercel MCP if you want (Neon + Fly still need you).
- **Reactive (me, after you deploy):** fix real-world issues that surface, committed to `main`, so they land inside v0.13.0.

**Recommended sequence: deploy & validate `main` first, fix issues, then cut v0.13.0** — so the released/tagged version is one that has been proven live, not a same-day v0.13.1. (If you'd rather tag first and hotfix, that's a one-line change to the order.)

## Step 1 — Deploy-readiness prep (me, small)

`docs/deploy.md` is already the thorough runbook. Gaps to close so a first deploy is friction-free:

- Add a `db:migrate` npm script (`drizzle-kit migrate`) alongside the existing `server` script in `package.json`, and reference it from `docs/deploy.md` instead of the bare `bunx`.
- Sanity-check the container is self-contained: `server/Dockerfile` copies `lib`/`db`/`server` + `package.json`/`bun.lock`/`bunfig.toml`/`tsconfig.json`, and `bun install --production` drops devDeps — confirm nothing the server imports at runtime lives in a devDep (PGlite is lazy-required only on the unused `pglite://` branch; prod uses `postgres`, a runtime dep). Confirm `bun.lock` is committed.
- Confirm Vercel picks up the project cleanly: Next 16 App Router auto-detects; verify no missing build config and that `bun.lock` drives a bun install (no `vercel.json` needed). Note in `docs/deploy.md` that `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` must be set **before** the build (it's inlined).
- Verify the full gate is green on `main` before anything ships (`lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test` **checking the real exit code**, `build`, `test:e2e`).

## Step 2 — You deploy (I guide via docs/deploy.md)

Order matters (each layer feeds the next), all covered by `docs/deploy.md`:

1. **Neon** — create a project, grab the **pooled** connection string → `DATABASE_URL`; apply the schema with `bun run db:migrate`.
2. **Fly** — install flyctl, `fly launch/secrets set/deploy` the `server/` container with the shared `DATABASE_URL` + `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` + `ADMIN_TOKEN`; confirm `GET /health`.
3. **Vercel** — deploy the web app with the five env vars (`DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL=wss://…`). The **#1 failure** is a `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` mismatch → every join closes with code 4000.

## Step 3 — Validate on the live stack (you play, I watch/fix)

The two-browser gameplay pass — the one thing no automated suite covers:

- **Offline-first intact:** the deployed app plays like single-player with no account/network until you go online.
- **Guest path:** "Play online as guest" → create a **New Online World** → **Copy invite** → open the link in a second browser/profile → accept → both players see each other (proves Neon + better-auth + join ticket + Fly).
- **Real-latency feel:** movement of the remote avatar is smooth (interpolation under real RTT), block edits/chest/mining propagate within ~1 RTT, chat round-trips.
- **Reconnect:** kill one client's network briefly (devtools offline, or drop wifi) → the amber "Reconnecting…" badge → it re-syncs the same world (validates the ladder + fresh-ticket handshake under real conditions).
- **Redeploy drain:** `fly deploy` again while connected → clients reconnect and re-sync; no lost world (validates SIGTERM persistence).
- **Ops:** `GET /rooms` (with `ADMIN_TOKEN`) shows sane tick p95 + bandwidth; pointer-lock, look-around, and visual quality are acceptable (the manual-pass items from `docs/testing.md`).

I fix anything that surfaces (likely candidates: interpolation/reconnect tuning under real RTT, Neon pool sizing, a Fly config tweak, a `wss` scheme mismatch), committing to `main`.

## Step 4 — Cut v0.13.0 (me, once validated)

Matching the `chore(release): v0.12.0` convention (`3568076`):

- Bump `package.json` `version` `0.12.0 → 0.13.0`.
- Roll `CHANGELOG.md`: `## [Unreleased]` → `## [0.13.0] - <date>` (the section already holds the online-multiplayer + hardening entries).
- Commit `chore(release): v0.13.0` summarizing the online-multiplayer shipment (save v16→v17, no worldgen bump — worldgen stayed 11 from Phase 1; SP unchanged); create the `v0.13.0` tag.
- Push commit + tag on your say-so (per the no-auto-push pattern).

## Critical files

- `docs/deploy.md` — the deploy runbook (small readiness edits).
- `package.json` — `db:migrate` script (Step 1) + version bump (Step 4).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — roll Unreleased → 0.13.0 (Step 4).
- `server/Dockerfile`, `server/fly.toml`, `.env.example`, `drizzle.config.ts` — reference/verify only; no changes expected unless the deploy surfaces one.
- Reactive fixes: most likely in `lib/net/interpolation.ts` / `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` (RTT tuning), `db/index.ts` (pool), or `server/*` (config) — only if validation demands.

## Verification

- **Pre-deploy:** full gate green on `main` — `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test` (**assert exit 0, not just "0 fail"** — the PGlite exit-99 lesson), `bun run build`, `bun run test:e2e` (20/20).
- **Live:** the Step 3 checklist passes on the real Vercel+Neon+Fly stack from two separate browsers.
- **Release:** `git show` of the `chore(release): v0.13.0` commit is clean; the `v0.13.0` tag points at it; the deployed app reports the new version where surfaced.

## Out of scope (future thrusts, not this plan)

Multiplayer v2 depth (boardable vehicles in MP, arrow replication, per-player server-side progression, owner-kick UI, SP cloud-save autosync, movement prediction); new game content (Nether-like dimension, redstone-lite, mounts, slabs/stairs); foundation/licensing (OSS license via upstream PR, davidhu0527 sync). These wait until v1 is proven live.

## Step 1 done ✅ — ready to deploy

Deploy-readiness prep is committed to `main` (`2d95e7a`): the `db:migrate` script, tightened deploy docs, and I verified the server container is self-contained. Full gate green (lint / typecheck / format:check / **`bun test` exit 0, 1080 pass** / build; e2e 20/20 on unchanged code).

## Your deploy path (full detail in `docs/deploy.md`)

Three parts, in order — each feeds the next. First generate the shared secrets:
```bash
openssl rand -base64 32   # BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
openssl rand -base64 32   # GAME_TICKET_SECRET   ← must be identical on Vercel AND Fly
openssl rand -base64 24   # ADMIN_TOKEN
```

**1. Neon** — create a project, copy the **pooled** connection string → `DATABASE_URL`, then:
```bash
DATABASE_URL='postgres://…neon.tech/…?sslmode=require' bun run db:migrate
```

**2. Fly** (game server) — `brew install flyctl` (or [install docs](https://fly.io/docs/flyctl/install/)), then from the repo root:
```bash
fly launch --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --no-deploy
fly secrets set DATABASE_URL='…' GAME_TICKET_SECRET='…' ADMIN_TOKEN='…' --config server/fly.toml
fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile
curl https://<your-app>.fly.dev/health   # expect {"ok":true,…}
```

**3. Vercel** (web app) — set the five env vars (**before** deploying, since `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` is build-time-inlined): `DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL` (your Vercel origin), `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL=wss://<your-app>.fly.dev`. Then deploy.

## What I can / can't do

- **Can't drive:** Neon (your account), Fly (`fly` isn't installed here + your account/secrets). These are yours.
- **Can help drive:** the **Vercel** step — I have the Vercel CLI/MCP available. If you want, once Neon + Fly are up I can push the env vars and trigger the deploy for you.
- **On-hand:** once anything's live, paste me `curl /health` output, any error, or a failing behavior and I'll debug it live. The #1 thing to watch: a `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` mismatch → every join closes with code **4000**.

## Once it's up — the validation pass (Step 3)
Two browsers: guest-join via invite → check remote-avatar smoothness under real latency, block/chest/chat propagation, the reconnect badge (toggle devtools offline), and a `fly deploy` mid-session (rooms should drain + resync). I fix whatever surfaces, then cut **v0.13.0**.

### One cleanup note
That probe wrote real test data to your prod Neon: a world named **"Prod Check"** (id `64598f91-33b2-4a8b-a376-f5f8b05b9d82`) owned by a throwaway guest. ### What's left — the manual two-browser pass (only you can judge feel)
The handshake is proven, so this is now low-risk. In **two separate browsers** (or one + a private window):
1. Sign in as guest in both → in browser A, **New Online World** → **Copy invite** → paste into browser B → accept → play from its card.
2. Both see each other's avatar; check remote movement is **smooth under real latency**, block/chest edits and **chat** propagate.
3. In B, toggle DevTools **offline** ~5s → the amber "Reconnecting…" badge → it re-syncs.
4. Optional: `fly deploy` again mid-session → both drop, reconnect, world intact (SIGTERM drain).

That's the whole arc, done:

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| **Built** | 6 phases, one PR (#43), merged to `main` |
| **Reviewed** | 2 rounds of CodeRabbit, 19 findings fixed (incl. a Critical) |
| **Released** | `v0.13.0` — commit `727ab9d` + tag, on origin |
| **Deployed** | Vercel + Neon + Fly (region `ord`) |
| **Validated** | prod probe passed — guest sign-in → world → ticket → **real `ws` handshake returned `WELCOME`** |

The production validation is the part worth savoring: it confirmed the exact thing that could only fail in the real world — the `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` matching across two independently-deployed services, verified by an actual browser-minted ticket accepted over `wss`. Single-player stayed fully offline and unchanged throughout.

**Two small loose ends (yours, low-priority):**

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# MP v2 — First-class co-op

## Context

Online multiplayer v1 shipped and is live (v0.13.0, deployed + prod-validated on Vercel + Neon + Fly). It works, but it landed with six documented scope-cuts that make co-op feel like a demo rather than the real game:

- **Vehicles can't be boarded online** — rafts/ships are gated off under server authority (a mounted pose is server-driven, which fought the client-owned pose stream).
- **Arrows don't replicate** — only the `arrowHit` event crosses the wire, so remote players never see arrows fly.
- **Progression only credits the host** — server rooms track no advancements/stats; they accrue to the (nonexistent) primary player.
- **Kill credit defaults to the host** — indirect kills (arrow, pet, explosion) credit the primary, not the actual killer.
- **Pets follow the nearest player**, not their owner.
- **No way to remove a griefer** — the game server has a `kick` endpoint but no player-facing control.
- **SP worlds don't follow you across devices** — the cloud-save transport is built but unwired.

**Intended outcome:** close all of them so co-op plays like single-player and the account layer feels complete. Target release **v0.14.0**. This plan supersedes the completed v1 build + ship-and-validate plans that previously lived in this file.

Exploration (three parallel Explore passes) confirmed the engine is already per-player-shaped for most of this: `PlayerState` owns `stats`/`advancements`/`inventory`/`xp` and serializes per-player (save v17), the advancements system (`recordEvent`/`evaluateAdvancements`) is already pure over a `PlayerState`, `removeMobAt` already has an (unused) `creditTo` param, and the client renderer already draws straight off `state.vehicles`/`state.projectiles`. The work is mostly **threading the acting player through a few boundaries** and **adding wire channels that copy the existing mob-replication skeleton**.

## Approach

One branch `feat/mp-v2`, phased commit slices, **one PR** (matching v1's convention and the user's stated preference). Verify gate green at each phase boundary.

- **`PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1 → 2** (`lib/net/protocol.ts`): the wire changes are additive but the protocol is version-locked at the door (`claims.pv !== PROTOCOL_VERSION` → refuse), so bumping ensures a stale v1 client is cleanly refused by a v2 server during a deploy rollover.
- **No save-format or worldgen bump** — per-player stats/advancements and placed vehicles already persist in save v17; Seam G reuses the existing `sp-cloud` world kind + save blob. (Seam G adds one optional *local-manifest* field, `WorldMeta.cloudId`, which is not the world save format.)
- Each phase ships its own tests, docs, and CHANGELOG entry, per AGENTS.md.

The four phases are largely independent; **Phase 4 (SP cloud-save) touches only the single-player/web side** and could run in any order. Recommended sequence is gameplay-parity first.

---

### Phase 1 — Live replication: vehicles + arrows (Seams A, B)

**Goal:** remote players see arrows fly and boats move; boarding works in MP. Both copy the mob-replication skeleton (`collectMobPoses`/`MobPose`/`upsertReplicaMob`); the client render side already consumes `state.vehicles` (`GameRenderer.ts:215`) and `state.projectiles` (`:217`).

- **Un-gate boarding under server authority:** `GameEngine.ts:857-859` currently skips `tryBoardAimedVehicle` on server/replica. Remove that gate (a right-click arrives as a `placeBlock` cmd, already a networked command). Ship step-on already fires server-side via `tickVehicles`.
- **Vehicle pose channel (mirror mobs):** new `VehiclePose { id, kind, x, y, z, yaw, riderId }` in `protocol.ts`; `collectVehiclePoses()` in `server/room.ts` beside `collectMobPoses`; carry in a new `TickMessage` field + `WorldSync`; `upsertReplicaVehicle()` in `NetworkSession.ts` populating `state.vehicles` (reuse `restoreVehicle`, `vehicles.ts:55`). **Fix the existing omission:** `applyWorldSync` (`NetworkSession.ts:231-246`) ignores `sync.vehicles` — restore it.
- **Mounted-player feedback (the reason boarding was cut):** the server owns a mounted player's position (driven by their input intents through `tickVehicles` — intents already arrive via `setPlayerInput` on every pose). Extend `SelfDelta` (`protocol.ts:122`) with `mountedVehicleId?` + authoritative `x/y/z/yaw` (only while mounted); emit in `buildSelfDelta` (diff via `conn.shadow`, `room.ts:63,502`); apply in `applySelfDelta` (`NetworkSession.ts:288`) — snap `self.position` like the `forcePose` handler. In the replica `step()` (`GameEngine.ts:519-524`), skip `tickPlayerMotion` for the local player when `mountedVehicleId !== null` so the server-driven position wins (kills the rubber-band). Keep `applyRemotePose`'s mounted reject (`GameEngine.ts:448`).
- **Arrow pose channel:** new `ProjectilePose { id, x, y, z, vx, vy, vz }` (velocity so `projectileVisuals` orientation works unchanged); `collectProjectilePoses()` — **no deadband**, emit all live ones every tick, prune-by-absence (arrows are ephemeral/fast); `upsertReplicaProjectile()` populating `state.projectiles`; snap-per-frame (skip interpolation — arrows outrun the 125 ms delay).
- **Tests:** `server/room.test.ts` (vehicle + projectile poses broadcast, mounted self-delta), `NetworkSession.test.ts` (upsert vehicle/projectile from wire; mounted snap), `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (boarding accepted under server authority; replica skips local motion when mounted). **Docs:** protocol.md (new poses + PROTOCOL_VERSION 2), online.md (rafts/ships now boardable — remove the v1 caveat), architecture.md, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 2 — Per-player attribution: progression, kill-credit, pets (Seams C, D, E)

**Goal:** each player earns their own advancements/stats and gets credit for their own kills; pets follow their owner. C and D are the same underlying change — thread the **acting player** through two boundaries.

- **Attribute events to the actor (C):** add an optional actor to the emit boundary — `emit(event, actorId?: PlayerId)` (`GameEngine.ts:1150`) — threaded from sites that already hold a `player` (the whole `dispatch` switch, resolved at `:672`; `removeMobAt`'s receiver). `observeProgress(event, actorId?)` (`:1166`) resolves `actor = actorId ? getPlayer(state, actorId) : primary`, then `recordEvent(actor, event)` + `evaluateAdvancements(actor)` **unchanged** (already pure per-player). Preserve the `advancementUnlocked` recursion guard; route its re-emit to the same actor.
- **Kill credit (D):** `removeMobAt` already has `creditTo?: PlayerState` with the loot/XP machinery wired (`awardXp(receiver,…)`) — it just has zero callers. Pass the killer at all four sites: melee → `player` (via a closure from the `attack` handler); arrows/spears → a new `owner?: PlayerId` on `ProjectileState`/`ThrownSpearState` captured at `spawnArrow`/spear-throw and forwarded through the widened `removeMobAt` dep signatures (`projectileAI.ts:9`, `spears.ts:53`, `mobAI.ts:226`); the explosion/mob-vs-mob death sweep (`mobAI.ts:504`) → the crediting player (pet kills credit `mob.owner`; TNT credits its igniter). The same resolved actor feeds C's attribution.
- **Per-player progression on the wire (C):** extend `SelfDelta` with `advancements?: string[]` + changed `stats?: [{id,value}]`; diff in `buildSelfDelta` against new `conn.shadow` slots; apply in `applySelfDelta` onto `self.advancements`/`self.stats` (reuse `serializeStats`/`restoreStats`, `save.ts:506`). This makes each client's own advancement-count snapshot correct.
- **Pet owner-follow (E):** in the ally branch of `tickMobs` (`mobAI.ts:345-361`), resolve `owner = mob.owner ? getPlayer(state, mob.owner) : null` and target `owner.position` for follow/teleport instead of `anchor` (nearest). Fallback when the owner is offline: idle (not nearest). `anchor`/`nearestPlayerTo` stays for wild-animal flee.
- **Tests:** `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (two players each earn own advancements; a second player's kill credits them, not primary; arrow/pet kill credits shooter/owner; pet follows owner over a nearer stranger), plus the existing advancements/combat/mobAI suites stay green. **Docs:** architecture.md (per-player attribution), online.md (remove the "progression accrues to primary" caveat), CHANGELOG.

### Phase 3 — Owner controls: kick + roster (Seam F)

**Goal:** the world owner sees who's connected and can remove someone, in-game. Use a **protocol message**, not a web→game admin bridge (the bridge would add cross-deployment env/coupling against the stateless design; the protocol path reuses the exact owner-gate already in `handleMessage`).

- **Wire:** add `KickMessage { t: "kick"; targetId }` to the `ClientMessage` union + a `readClientMessage` validator (`protocol.ts`). Server `handleMessage` `kick` case: `if (conn.role !== "owner") return; this.kick(message.targetId)` — mirrors the existing `setDifficulty` owner-gate (`room.ts:306`); reuses `Room.kick` (`room.ts:252`) and `conn.role` (already from the ticket).
- **Role to the client:** add `role` to `WelcomeMessage` (filled from `claims.role`), expose `session.role` — self-contained for the panel. (Alternative: thread `screen.world.role`, which the web already has but `onlineWorldMeta` currently drops.)
- **Roster to the UI:** add `session.roster(): {id,name}[]` (from `state.players` + `names`) and a `subscribeRoster` firing on `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`/`applyRoster`; add `session.kick(targetId)`.
- **UI:** new `components/game/RosterPanel.tsx` copying the `ChatPanel`/`ConnectionStatus` shape (subscribe/unsubscribe in `useEffect`), rendered online-only in `MinecraftGame.tsx:156-157`. Lists players; owners get a Kick button per non-self id.
- **Tests:** `protocol.test.ts` (kick validation), `server/room.test.ts` (owner kick via message; member's kick ignored), `NetworkSession.test.ts` (roster/kick send), `RosterPanel.test.tsx`. **Docs:** protocol.md (kick message), online.md/manual.md (owner controls), CHANGELOG.

### Phase 4 — SP cloud-save autosync (Seam G)

**Goal:** a signed-in player's single-player worlds sync to the cloud and follow them across devices. Transport (`lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` `pushSave`/`pullSave`, gzip, stamp cursor) and server (`worldsService` `get/putSaveBlob` LWW, `sp-cloud` kind) are **already built and tested** — this is wiring. **Opt-in per world** (an explicit "Sync to cloud" action), not automatic upload of every local world.

- **Local↔cloud link:** add optional `WorldMeta.cloudId` (`lib/game/worlds.ts` — tolerate in the manifest sanitizer; `createWorld` gains a way to record it / materialize from a `WorldSummary`). Generalize `createOnlineWorld` (or a sibling) to send `kind: "sp-cloud"`.
- **World list (`WorldSelect.tsx`):** split `listOnlineWorlds()` by `kind` — `mp` → the existing Online Worlds join section (unchanged); `sp-cloud` → merge into the local list (materialize a local `WorldMeta` + pull on first play). An "Upload to cloud" action on a local world creates its `sp-cloud` row and links it.
- **Push on save (`useMinecraftGame.ts`):** after the existing `writeSave` in the autosave/quit/unmount paths (`:300,302,395,524`; all already `if (!online)`), a **debounced** `pushSave(cloudId, api.serialize())` when the world is cloud-linked and signed in. Note `beforeunload` cloud flush is best-effort only (`sendBeacon` can't set the required headers) — flush on quit/unmount instead.
- **Pull on play (`GameShell.tsx`):** cloud-linked worlds need an **async pull gate** before `setScreen('play')` — reuse the existing `connecting`/`connectError` "Joining…" modal (`GameShell.tsx:80-111,193-207`). `pullSave` → `writeSave(worldSaveKey,…)` → normal boot from disk.
- **Conflict (409):** `pushSave` already returns `"conflict"`; surface a keep-local (re-push after refreshing the base) vs adopt-remote (`pullSave`) prompt via the existing toast / `net-modal` pattern.
- **Tests:** `worlds.ts` cloud-link, `WorldSelect.test.tsx` (sp-cloud split/merge), a `GameShell` async-pull test; `cloudSaves`/`worldsService` suites already cover the transport/LWW. Optional e2e in `multiplayer.e2e.ts` (the stack + pglite are already wired). **Docs:** online.md (cloud saves now live), manual.md (worlds across devices), architecture.md, CHANGELOG.

---

## Critical files

- **Protocol/wire:** `lib/net/protocol.ts` (PROTOCOL_VERSION 2; `VehiclePose`/`ProjectilePose`/`KickMessage`; `SelfDelta`/`WelcomeMessage`/`TickMessage` fields; validators), `lib/net/codec.ts` (unchanged).
- **Server:** `server/room.ts` (collect/broadcast poses, self-delta extensions, kick case, owner-gate), `server/index.ts` (unchanged — kick endpoint stays for admin).
- **Client session:** `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` (upsert vehicle/projectile, mounted self-delta, roster/kick, role), `lib/net/NetworkSession.test.ts`.
- **Engine:** `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` (un-gate boarding, replica mounted skip, `emit`/`observeProgress`/`removeMobAt` actor threading), `systems/{vehicles,projectileAI,spears,combat,mobAI,advancements}.ts`, `state.ts` (`owner` on projectile/spear), `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts`.
- **Client UI/shell:** `components/game/RosterPanel.tsx` (new), `components/MinecraftGame.tsx`, `components/GameShell.tsx`, `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`.
- **SP save:** `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` (built), `lib/game/worlds.ts` (cloudId), `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` (push hook), `lib/online/onlineClient.ts` (sp-cloud create).
- **Docs:** protocol.md, online.md, architecture.md, manual.md, testing.md, CHANGELOG.md.

## Verification

- **Per phase:** the full gate on `main`/branch — `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test` (**assert real exit 0**, not just "0 fail" — the PGlite exit-99 lesson), `bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` for phases touching renderer/input/shell (1, 3, 4).
- **Phase-specific:** unit tests in the headless engine are the workhorse (two-player boarding, kill-credit attribution, per-player advancements, pet-follow) — the existing `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` + fake-socket `server/room.test.ts`/`NetworkSession.test.ts` patterns extend directly.
- **End-to-end (live):** the same two-browser pass used for v1 — board a boat together, see arrows fly, each earn a distinct advancement, kick a third guest, and (Phase 4) create a cloud world on one device and open it on another. The prod stack (Vercel + Neon + Fly) is already deployed.
- **Release:** cut **v0.14.0** at the end (version bump + CHANGELOG roll + `chore(release)` commit + tag), matching v0.13.0.

## Out of scope (future thrusts)

Client-side movement prediction/rollback (the hybrid model already gives smooth own-movement); interest management / chunk streaming (bigger worlds, more players); PvP tuning; public rooms / matchmaking / moderation; SP→MP world conversion. Foundation/licensing (OSS license via upstream PR) remains a separate track.

## The plan in one glance
**Full first-class co-op → v0.14.0**, one branch `feat/mp-v2`, one PR, `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1→2, **no** save/worldgen bump:
1. **Replication** — boardable vehicles + flying arrows in MP (copy the mob-replication skeleton; the renderer already reads `state.vehicles`/`state.projectiles`).
2. **Per-player attribution** — thread the acting player through `emit`/`observeProgress` and `removeMobAt`'s already-present-but-unused `creditTo`; per-player advancements/stats over the wire; pets follow their owner.
3. **Owner kick + roster panel** — a new `kick` protocol message reusing the existing owner-gate.
4. **SP cloud-save autosync** — wire the already-built transport into an opt-in "sync to cloud" flow.

The nicest finding: most of this is *threading an actor through a few boundaries* and *copying one replication pattern* — the engine is already per-player-shaped, so it's far less code than v1 was.
